PRD

PRD-001 - RCF Lite

Executive summary: RCF Lite is the tooling product of the RCF suite. It runs the full Requirements Confidence Framework over a project whose RCF documents live in the source repository, alongside the code. It gives a non-engineering product owner deterministic create, read, update and delete operations on every RCF document type, a visual review surface, traceability and query, a build loop that turns build specifications into implementation prompts, and a local MCP surface that exposes all of this to AI tooling.

Problem statement: Power vibe-coders build real applications without engineering teams. They cannot read code, so they cannot judge whether what an AI tool produces is trustworthy. The full RCF chain makes output trustworthy without reading code, but authoring that chain by hand is the very effort these users lack the time and discipline for. There is no tool that runs the full RCF method over in-repository documents and surfaces it through structured, deterministic operations.

Target users 3
  • Power vibe-coders: product owners, founders and business voices building applications without engineering teams
  • AI coding tools that need a structured, deterministic surface over a project's RCF documents
  • Maintainers dogfooding RCF on the Build Lite repository itself
In scope 9
  • On-disk RCF project structure under a project rcf folder
  • Visual review surface rendering the whole RCF tree as a diagram and a browsable page
  • Deterministic create, read, update and delete on every RCF document type
  • Traceability and query: coverage, trace forward, trace back, impact analysis
  • SDD build loop: assemble an implementation prompt from a build specification and mark it done on merge
  • Local stdio MCP surface exposing query, CRUD, view and build to AI tooling
  • Validation of every document against the published schema package at every boundary
  • Deploy-aware, runtime-honest build guidance: a documented local preview as the default build outcome, an early deploy-target question that constrains the stack, and runtime-provenance labels on verification claims
  • End-to-end verification contract: version-pinned Playwright MCP in verify, e2e as a declared test level in the chain (application-spa browserSurface and delivery-ci-workflows e2e CI job), doctor checks for browser-facing projects, and init that writes a Playwright MCP entry only when no scope-visible entry exists
Out of scope 6
  • The schema package itself, which is the separately published rcf-schemas contract
  • A hosted service: MCP is local stdio and the CLI is a local binary
  • A web application with a server, authentication or a database
  • Language-agnostic tooling: Build Lite is Node 24 ESM
  • The one-off v1 to v2 migration script, which is not a product feature
  • Generation of executable test code: verification artefacts accrue per implementation phase
Objectives 5
  • Make the full RCF chain usable with minimal user effort while keeping the method full-strength
  • Guarantee the in-repository differentiator by operating directly on local files as the source of truth
  • Keep every RCF document valid against the published schemas at all times
  • Surface the whole tree visually so a non-coder can review what is being built in their name
  • Stay harness-agnostic so the tooling survives a change of AI harness
Constraints 5
  • Node 24 ESM, plain JavaScript, no TypeScript pin
  • Apache 2.0 license
  • Depends on the published rcf-schemas package as an external contract
  • Local filesystem is the source of truth; no network source of truth
  • MCP transport is local stdio only

Requirements

114 of 114 visible
REQ-001 On-disk RCF project structure projectStructure US2 AC6 draft

Build Lite initialises and maintains a project's RCF documents on the local filesystem, under a top-level rcf folder, with the project manifest declaring the three root documents (PRD, TAD, Build Sequence) and every other document discovered by walking from the roots. The local files are the single source of truth; no external store mirrors them.

Why: The in-repository differentiator depends on RCF documents living beside the code. A predictable on-disk layout is the foundation every other capability reads from and writes to.

capability:project-init structure manifest filesystem

User stories (2)

US-101 Initialise an RCF project on disk AC3 draft

US-101 - Initialise an RCF project on disk

As a: project owner starting a new RCF project

I want: to run a single initialise command that creates the rcf folder, the manifest and the root document placeholders

So that: I have a valid RCF project structure on disk without authoring any layout by hand

Description: A project owner starts a new RCF project and gets the canonical on-disk structure created for them, ready to receive documents.

Requirement

REQ-001

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-101-1 - Initialise creates the rcf folder and a manifest declaring the three roots

    Given an empty target directory

    When the initialise command runs

    Then an rcf folder exists containing a manifest that declares prd, tad and bs root references and validates against the manifest schema

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-001

  • AC-101-2 - Initialise refuses to overwrite an existing project

    Given a directory that already contains an rcf manifest

    When the initialise command runs without an explicit force flag

    Then the command exits non-zero, makes no changes and reports that a project already exists

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-001

  • AC-101-3 - Every document is discoverable by walking from the roots

    Given an initialised project with a PRD, a TAD and a Build Sequence

    When the project is loaded

    Then all child documents are resolved by reading the parent id lists, with no child enumeration in the manifest

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-001

US-102 Load and walk the tree AC3 draft

US-102 - Load and walk the tree

As a: project owner or AI tool

I want: to load the whole RCF tree from the on-disk files in one operation

So that: every later command works against a single, validated in-memory view of the project

Description: A project owner or an AI tool loads the whole RCF tree from on-disk files in one operation, producing a single validated in-memory view for later commands.

Requirement

REQ-001

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-102-1 - Loading reads the manifest roots and resolves every child by walking parent id lists

    Given an initialised project

    When the tree is loaded

    Then the manifest roots are read and every child is resolved by walking the parent id lists

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-002

  • AC-102-2 - Missing or unparseable files are reported as structured errors and do not crash the load

    Given a document file that is missing or unparseable

    When the tree is loaded

    Then the load reports a structured error naming the document id and the file path, and does not crash

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-002

  • AC-102-3 - Broken references are reported as part of project health, not swallowed

    Given a reference to a document id that has no file

    When the tree is loaded

    Then the broken reference is reported as part of project health, not swallowed

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-002

REQ-002 Visual review surface view US4 AC15 draft

Build Lite renders the whole RCF tree as a diagram and as a browsable static page, so a non-coding owner can see the documents and their links without reading any JSON. The view is read-only and generated from the on-disk tree on demand. Build/DAG sub-tab lays FBS by `dependsOnFbsIds` depth with click-to-highlight closure, dependency inspector, filters, unconnected lane and `#tab=build&sub=dag&entity=` deep links, per viewer UI refresh design section 7.

Why: The owner cannot review code and will not read raw JSON. A visual surface is the only way they can see and steer what is being built in their name. It is delivered first (Phase 3) so every later phase has a review surface.

capability:review-surface view diagram review

User stories (4)

US-201 Render the tree as a diagram AC3 draft

US-201 - Render the tree as a diagram

As a: project owner who cannot read code

I want: a diagram of the whole RCF tree showing documents and the links between them

So that: I can see what is specified at a glance

Description: A non-coding owner sees the whole RCF tree at a glance as a diagram of documents and the links between them.

Requirement

REQ-002

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-201-1 - The tree is rendered as per-requirement subdiagrams carrying chain edges

    Given a loaded project

    When the diagrams are generated

    Then each requirement is rendered as its own subdiagram showing the requirement, its user stories and acceptance criteria with edges following the chain and FBS delivery back-links, scoped to that requirement only

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-003

  • AC-201-2 - Broken references are marked visibly rather than omitted

    Given a project with a broken reference

    When the diagram is generated

    Then the broken link is marked visibly rather than omitted silently

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-003

  • AC-201-3 - The diagram is produced as source that renders without a running server

    Given a valid project

    When the diagram is generated

    Then it is produced as a diagram source that renders without a running server

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-003

  • AC-202-3 - Inter-document links navigate between sections

    When a document links to another

    Then the link navigates to that document's section

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-004

US-204 An engineer sees the FBS DAG AC7 draft

US-204 - An engineer sees the FBS DAG

As a: an engineer looking at the build sequence

I want: a dependency DAG of the FBS with click-to-highlight closure, an inspector and filters

So that: I can see what feeds what, pick the next buildable work and spot the critical path without reading JSON

Description: The Build tab's DAG sub-tab lays FBS out by dependency depth from `dependsOnFbsIds` with click-to-highlight closure, a dependency inspector, status/area/Buildable-now/Critical-path/Show-unconnected filters, a hidden unconnected lane with a count, and `#tab=build&sub=dag&entity=<id>` deep links so a node is a link. The canvas scrolls inside its own box and the viewer never scrolls horizontally. See viewer UI refresh design doc section 7.

Requirement

REQ-002

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-204-1 - [happy] Given the Build tab's DAG sub-tab, when it renders, then every connected FBS sits in a column whose index equals its longest dependency depth from `dependsOnFbsIds` (0 for no dependency) and rows inside a column are ordered by `buildOrder` ascending.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-203

  • AC-204-2 - [happy] Given the DAG canvas, when a node is clicked, then it is selected, its upstream closure outlines in the link colour and its downstream closure outlines in the warning colour; a second click on the same node clears the selection.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-203

  • AC-204-3 - [happy] Given a selected FBS, when the inspector renders, then it lists status, area, AC count, size, build order, a buildable-now flag, direct and transitive needs, direct and transitive waits-on and an "Open in Specs" link that moves to `#tab=build&sub=specs&entity=<id>`.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-203

  • AC-204-4 - [happy] Given a selection, when it is set or cleared, then the hash becomes `#tab=build&sub=dag&entity=<id>` (or drops the entity key when cleared) and a reload with that hash restores the selection and scrolls the node into view.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-203

  • AC-204-5 - [happy] Given the DAG toolbar, when the Status, Area, Buildable-now, Critical-path or Show-unconnected filter changes, then the visible nodes update and the current selection is kept.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-203

  • AC-204-6 - [failure] Given a `dependsOnFbsIds` cycle on disk, when the DAG renders, then the cycle is reported as a finding in the toolbar area and the remaining non-cycle FBS still render.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-203

  • AC-204-7 - [must-not] Given the DAG canvas, when a node is clicked, filtered or inspected, then no `postMessage` is sent to the parent window and no outbound network request is made.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-203

REQ-003 Deterministic create, read, update and delete over RCF documents crud US4 AC12 draft

Build Lite provides deterministic create, read, update and delete operations for every RCF document type, operating directly on the local files. Operations are structural and predictable so an AI agent cannot fudge document shape: each operation validates before it writes and reports a clear error on failure.

Why: Deterministic CRUD is the foundational primitive everything else sits on. Hand-writing the tree in this phase surfaces exactly which operations the owner and the agent need.

capability:requirements-authoring crud cli validation

User stories (4)

US-301 Read any document AC3 draft

US-301 - Read any document

As a: project owner or AI tool

I want: to read any RCF document by its id

So that: I can inspect a document's current content without opening files by hand

Description: A project owner or AI tool reads any RCF document by id and gets its current content together with a validity report.

Requirement

REQ-003

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-301-1 - Reading a valid document returns it and reports it as valid

    Given a document id

    When read runs

    Then the document is returned and reported as valid against its schema

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-005

  • AC-301-2 - Reading an id with no file returns a structured not-found error naming the id

    Given an id with no file

    When read runs

    Then a structured not-found error is returned naming the id

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-005

  • AC-301-3 - Reading an invalid document returns both the content and the validation errors

    Given a document that exists but fails validation

    When read runs

US-302 Create a document with parent linkage AC3 draft

US-302 - Create a document with parent linkage

As a: project owner or AI tool

I want: to create a new RCF document and have its parent linkage maintained

So that: the tree stays consistent without me editing two files by hand

Description: A project owner or AI tool creates a new RCF document and the tool maintains the parent linkage automatically.

Requirement

REQ-003

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-302-1 - Creating a requirement writes a validating child file carrying the parent edge; the PRD file is not modified

    Given a request to create a requirement under a PRD

    When create runs

    Then the requirement file is written carrying its prdId parent edge and validating, and the parent PRD file is not modified (child-owned parent edges)

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-006

  • AC-302-2 - Creating a document with a conflicting id writes nothing and returns a clear conflict error

    Given a request to create a document whose id already exists

    When create runs

    Then no file is written and a clear conflict error is returned

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-006

  • AC-302-3 - Creating an invalid document writes nothing and returns the validation error

    Given a request to create a document that would not validate

    When create runs

    Then nothing is written and the validation error is returned

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-006

US-303 Update fields safely AC3 draft

US-303 - Update fields safely

As a: project owner or AI tool

I want: to update fields on an existing document

So that: I can revise content without rewriting the whole document or risking an invalid result

Description: A project owner or AI tool updates fields on an existing document; valid updates persist and invalid updates are refused without disturbing disk state.

Requirement

REQ-003

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-303-1 - A valid update is persisted with updatedAt advanced and validates

    Given a valid field update

    When update runs

    Then the document is rewritten with the change and its updatedAt timestamp advanced, and it validates

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-006

  • AC-303-2 - An update that would invalidate the document leaves disk unchanged and returns the validation error

    Given an update that would make the document invalid

    When update runs

    Then the document on disk is unchanged and the validation error is returned

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-006

  • AC-303-3 - Updating a non-existent document returns a not-found error and writes nothing

    Given an update to a document that does not exist

    When update runs

    Then a not-found error is returned and nothing is written

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-006

US-304 Delete with reference safety AC3 draft

US-304 - Delete with reference safety

As a: project owner or AI tool

I want: to delete a document without silently orphaning the documents that depend on it

So that: I cannot accidentally break the tree

Description: A project owner or AI tool deletes a document and the tool refuses to silently orphan its dependants, offering a cascade flag for intentional sub-tree removal.

Requirement

REQ-003

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-304-1 - Deleting a document with dependants without the cascade flag is refused and the blocking references are listed

    Given a document with children or inbound references

    When delete runs without a cascade flag

    Then nothing is deleted and the blocking references are listed

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-007

  • AC-304-2 - Deleting with the cascade flag removes the sub-tree and cleans parent references, leaving the tree valid

    Given a document with children

    When delete runs with a cascade flag

    Then the document and its children are removed and every parent reference to them is cleaned up, leaving the tree valid

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-007

  • AC-304-3 - Deleting an unreferenced document removes the file and updates the parent id list

    Given a document with no references

    When delete runs

    Then the file is removed and the parent id list is updated, leaving the tree valid

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-007

  "description": "Build Lite provides deterministic create, read, update and delete operations for every RCF document type, operating directly on the local files. Operations are structural and predictable so an AI agent cannot fudge document shape: each operation validates before it writes and reports a clear error on failure.",
  "category": "functional",
  "domain": "crud",
  "priority": "must",
  "rationale": "Deterministic CRUD is the foundational primitive everything else sits on. Hand-writing the tree in this phase surfaces exactly which operations the owner and the agent need.",

REQ-004 Traceability and query over the RCF chain traceability US3 AC9 draft

Build Lite answers traceability questions over the RCF chain: coverage (which requirements lack stories, which acceptance criteria lack tests), trace forward (from a PRD or requirement down to acceptance criteria and tests), trace back (from a test or acceptance criterion up to its requirement and PRD), and impact analysis (what is affected if a given document changes). Queries walk the chain from the on-disk tree.

Why: Traceability is the confidence the framework is named for. The owner needs to know that nothing is unspecified and nothing is untested, and what an edit ripples into, without reading the documents end to end.

capability:requirements-authoring traceability query coverage

User stories (3)

  • AC-401-1 - Coverage lists every requirement that has no user story

    Given a loaded project

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-008

  • AC-401-2 - Coverage lists every acceptance criterion that has no test suite

    Given a loaded project

    When coverage runs

    Then it lists every acceptance criterion that has no test suite

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-008

  • AC-401-3 - A fully covered project reports complete coverage with no gaps

    Given a fully covered project

    When coverage runs

    Then it reports complete coverage with no gaps

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-008

REQ-005 Specification-driven build loop build US3 AC9 draft

Build Lite turns a Functional Build Specification into a single implementation prompt by walking the FBS, its acceptance criteria (to the parent user stories), and its declared architectural context (referenced TACs and ADRs), then assembles a markdown prompt for a coding agent. It marks a build slice done when the slice is finished.

Why: For someone who cannot read code, the specification-to-build loop is the only thing between them and a confident but wrong result. Assembling the prompt from the tree is what makes the output solid and traceable to an agreed decision.

capability:build-sequence build sdd fbs

User stories (3)

US-501 Assemble a build prompt AC3 draft

US-501 - Assemble a build prompt

As a: project owner or AI tool

I want: to turn a Functional Build Specification into a single implementation prompt

So that: a coding agent has everything it needs to implement the slice, traceable to the acceptance criteria it must satisfy

Description: A project owner or AI tool turns a Functional Build Specification into a single implementation prompt with the acceptance criteria and the architectural context the coding agent needs.

Requirement

REQ-005

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-501-1 - Build assembly walks each AC in acIds to its parent user story and includes the Given/When/Then in the prompt

    Given an FBS id

    When build assembly runs

    Then it walks each acceptance criterion in acIds to its parent user story and includes the criterion's Given/When/Then in the prompt

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-010

  • AC-501-2 - Build assembly walks the referenced TACs and ADRs and includes their relevant content in the prompt

    Given an FBS that declares architectural context

    When build assembly runs

    Then it walks the referenced TACs and ADRs and includes their relevant content in the prompt

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-010

  • AC-501-3 - The assembled prompt is a single markdown document naming FBS, summary, approach, ACs and architectural context

    Given the assembled prompt

    When it is produced

    Then it is a single markdown document naming the FBS, its summary and approach, the acceptance criteria, and the architectural context

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-010

US-502 Build order respects dependencies AC3 draft

US-502 - Build order respects dependencies

As a: project owner or AI tool

I want: the build order to respect the dependency graph declared on the FBS items

So that: no slice is built before the work it depends on

Description: A project owner or AI tool computes a build order that honours the dependency graph declared on FBS items, surfaces parallel-safe items, and detects cycles.

Requirement

REQ-005

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-502-1 - The computed order is a valid topological order in which dependencies precede dependents

    Given a set of FBS items with declared dependencies

    When the build order is computed

    Then it is a valid ordering in which every dependency precedes the items that depend on it

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-010

  • AC-502-2 - FBS items with no dependency between them are reported as parallel-safe

    Given FBS items with no dependency between them

    When the build order is computed

    Then they are reported as parallel-safe

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-010

  • AC-502-3 - A dependency cycle is detected and reported rather than producing a partial order

    Given a dependency cycle

    When the build order is computed

    Then the cycle is detected and reported rather than producing a partial order

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-010

REQ-006 Local MCP surface over the full feature set mcp US2 AC6 draft

Build Lite exposes its query, CRUD, view and build operations through a local stdio MCP server, so an AI harness can drive the whole feature set as structured tools. The MCP server is a thin adapter over the same operations the CLI uses; it carries no behaviour the core does not already own.

Why: The harness is where the owner's AI tooling lives. A local stdio MCP surface gives that tooling the full RCF feature set while preserving filesystem access and the source-of-truth rule. Remote MCP is excluded because it cannot see the user's codebase.

capability:mcp mcp harness stdio

User stories (2)

US-601 Query and view over MCP AC3 draft

US-601 - Query and view over MCP

As a: AI tool running in a harness

I want: the query and view operations exposed as MCP tools over local stdio

So that: I can read and report on the project's RCF tree without shelling out to the CLI

Description: An AI tool running in a harness uses the local stdio MCP server to query and view the project's RCF tree without shelling out to the CLI.

Requirement

REQ-006

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-601-1 - An MCP client listing tools sees the query and view operations with structured input and output

    Given a running local stdio MCP server

    When an MCP client lists tools

    Then the query and view operations are present with structured input and output

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-012

  • AC-601-2 - A coverage query over MCP returns the same result the CLI coverage command returns for the same project

    Given a coverage query over MCP

    When it runs

    Then it returns the same result the CLI coverage command returns for the same project

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-012

  • AC-601-3 - The MCP server communicates over local stdio only and opens no network listener

    Given the MCP server

    When it runs

    Then it communicates over local stdio only and opens no network listener

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-012

REQ-007 Validation at every boundary quality US2 AC6 draft

Every RCF document is validated against the published schema package on load and before persist. No operation writes an invalid document. Validation failures are reported as clear, structured errors that name the offending field and the rule it broke.

Why: A non-coder cannot catch a malformed document by eye. The tool must refuse to write invalid state and must explain why, so the owner can trust that what is on disk is always valid.

capability:requirements-authoring validation quality schemas

User stories (2)

US-701 Refuse invalid writes AC3 draft

US-701 - Refuse invalid writes

As a: project owner

I want: the tool to refuse to write any document that does not validate against the schema

So that: what is on disk is always valid, even though I cannot check it myself

Description: A project owner trusts that the tool refuses to write any document that does not validate, so on-disk state is always valid even when the owner cannot inspect it.

Requirement

REQ-007

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-701-1 - A create or update that would produce an invalid document writes nothing

    Given any create or update that would produce an invalid document

    When it runs

    Then nothing is written

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-006

  • AC-701-2 - A successful write produces a document that validates against its schema

    Given a successful write

    When it completes

    Then the written document validates against its schema

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-006

  • AC-701-3 - Validation uses the published schema bundle registered once at start-up, not a local copy

    Given the validation step

    When it runs

    Then it uses the published schema bundle registered once at start-up, not a local copy that could drift

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-002

REQ-008 Deploy-aware, runtime-honest build guidance guidance US5 AC20 draft

The agent guidance pack teaches a build method that keeps the deployment runtime present in the loop from elicitation to verification, so that a non-coding owner who cannot self-verify is not led into an undeployable stack or a false 'verified' claim. It requires four properties of the method the tool ships: (1) every build lands a working, documented local preview loop as its default outcome; (2) elicitation establishes where the app will run early and constrains the stack to that answer, with a jargon-free hosting-choice walkthrough when the owner does not know; (3) every 'verified' or 'tested' claim names the runtime it was checked against and never implies deploy-runtime verification that did not happen; (4) the method carries guidance for a periodic and end-of-build fresh-context self-review that drives the app against its acceptance criteria, subordinate to the independent verification gate rather than a substitute for it. This requirement governs the shipped guidance/prompt surface, not a new runtime subsystem.

Why: The five-run rcf-persona-testing programme (concluded 2026-07-20) found the tool builds excellently at every level but its own loop missed a ship-blocking or user-facing defect in three of five runs, with a single root cause: the deploy runtime is absent from the loop. It is absent from elicitation (runs 03/04 chose Cloudflare-incompatible stacks a CF-only holder cannot host, run 03 silently) and absent from verification (run 05 shipped a production auth 500 while 89/89 tests were green and the tool claimed a live-Worker verification its E2E never ran). The target user cannot diagnose 'wrong stack for your host' or 'verified against the wrong runtime', so the method itself must foreclose both. These are Tier-1 hardening fixes to make the base offering usable now, while the productised independent verification gate (rcf verify-lite) is built separately.

capability:build-sequence guidance deploy verification

User stories (5)

US-801 Every build leaves a working local preview AC4 draft

US-801 - Every build leaves a working local preview

As a: non-coding product owner

I want: every build to leave me a working, documented way to run the app locally

So that: I can see and use what was built without needing to deploy it anywhere first

Description: The build loop leaves every project with a working, documented local preview as its default outcome, so a non-coding owner always has a runtime they can drive and review without a cloud account or a deploy step.

Requirement

REQ-008

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-801-1 - A build's definition of done requires a documented local preview loop as the default outcome

    Given the RCF build method as taught by the shipped guidance pack

    When a build reaches its definition of done

    Then the guidance requires a working, documented local preview loop (a dev server, and seeded data where the app needs it) to be present as the default deliverable

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

  • AC-801-2 - The local preview is startable via a single documented command where the stack allows

    Given the shipped build guidance describing the local preview

    When it states how the owner starts the app

    Then it directs the build toward one documented command to start the preview wherever the stack makes a single command possible

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

  • AC-801-3 - The local preview is produced whether or not a hosting target was stated

    Given an owner who has not stated a hosting target, or who asked for a recommendation instead

    When the build completes

    Then the guidance still requires the local preview to be produced as the default, not made conditional on a stated host

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

  • AC-801-4 - The preview includes seeded data when the app needs data to be usable

    Given an application that needs data present to be exercisable

    When the local preview loop is produced

    Then the guidance requires seeded or sample data so the preview can actually be driven, not an empty shell

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

US-802 Deploy target is established before the stack is chosen AC4 draft

US-802 - Deploy target is established before the stack is chosen

As a: non-coding product owner

I want: the tool to work out where my app will run before it picks the technology to build it with

So that: it does not build me something my hosting cannot actually run

Description: Elicitation establishes where the application will run before any stack is committed, and the stack the tool builds is constrained by that answer, so the owner is not led into a stack their hosting cannot run.

Requirement

REQ-008

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-802-1 - Elicitation asks where the app will run as an early item before any stack is committed

    Given the shipped elicitation guidance

    When an agent runs elicitation with an owner

    Then the guidance places a deploy-target question early, before any technology stack is committed

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-013

  • AC-802-2 - The stack choice is constrained by the deploy-target answer

    Given a stated deploy target

    When the agent chooses the technology stack

    Then the guidance requires the stack to be constrained to what that target can host, so an incompatible stack is not committed

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-013

  • AC-802-3 - The deploy target and its stack implication are captured as an ADR on the project tree

    Given a deploy target established during elicitation

    When the decision is made

    Then the guidance requires it and the stack constraint it implies to be recorded as an ADR on the project's own tree, visible and revisable

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-013

  • AC-802-4 - The harness fragment forbids committing a stack before the deploy target is established

    Given the harness fragment written into agent-instructions files

    When it is inspected

    Then it carries a rule that a technology stack must not be committed before the deploy target is established

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-013

US-803 Hosting-choice guidance when the owner is unsure AC4 draft

US-803 - Hosting-choice guidance when the owner is unsure

As a: non-coding product owner who does not know my hosting options

I want: to be walked through choosing and setting up somewhere to run my app, in plain language

So that: I can make and act on the hosting decision without already being an expert

Description: When the owner does not know where the application will run, the agent walks them through choosing and configuring a hosting account in plain language, honestly isolating the steps only the human account-holder can do, rather than choosing silently or pretending to act as them.

Requirement

REQ-008

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-803-1 - When the owner does not know where the app will run, the agent runs a hosting-choice walkthrough rather than choosing silently

    Given an owner who does not know their hosting options

    When the deploy-target question is reached

    Then the guidance directs the agent to run a hosting-choice walkthrough instead of silently selecting a host

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-013

  • AC-803-2 - The walkthrough explains the options in plain language

    Given the hosting-choice walkthrough guidance

    When it presents hosting options to the owner

    Then it requires plain-language explanation with no unexplained jargon

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-013

  • AC-803-3 - Steps only the human account-holder can do are isolated and named honestly

    Given the walkthrough reaching steps only the account-holder can perform (sign-ups, billing, tokens, CLI authentication)

    When those steps arise

    Then the guidance requires them to be isolated and named honestly as the human's to do, not performed silently by the agent nor pretended

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-013

  • AC-803-4 - The walkthrough covers configuring the chosen account, not only naming a provider

    Given a hosting choice the owner has made

    When the walkthrough continues past the choice

    Then the guidance requires it to cover configuring the account - accounts, tokens and CLI setup - not just naming a provider

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-013

US-804 Verification claims name their runtime AC4 draft

US-804 - Verification claims name their runtime

As a: non-coding product owner

I want: every claim that something was verified to say what it was verified against

So that: I am not told the deployed app works when only a local emulator was checked

Description: Every claim the tool or its agent makes that something is verified or tested names the runtime it was checked against, and never implies verification on a deployed runtime that did not happen, so the owner can tell what was actually proven.

Requirement

REQ-008

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-804-1 - Every verified or tested claim names the runtime it was checked against

    Given the shipped build guidance on reporting verification

    When a 'verified' or 'tested' claim is made

    Then the guidance requires the claim to name the runtime it was checked against

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

  • AC-804-2 - No claim implies deploy-runtime verification that did not happen

    Given a verification that ran against a local or emulated runtime

    When the claim is written

    Then the guidance forbids the claim from stating or implying verification on a deployed runtime that was not exercised

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

  • AC-804-3 - The PR-authoring guidance requires the runtime label in the verification section

    Given the build-cycle PR-authoring guidance

    When the verification section of a PR body is authored

    Then it requires each verification claim to carry the runtime it was checked against

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

  • AC-804-4 - The guidance includes an explicit labelled-claim example

    Given the shipped build guidance

    When it illustrates a verification claim

    Then it includes an explicit example naming the runtime (for example 'verified against wrangler dev (localhost) - NOT the deployed Worker runtime')

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

US-805 Interim self-review guidance AC4 draft

US-805 - Interim self-review guidance

As a: non-coding product owner

I want: the build to include a periodic fresh look that actually drives the app against what it is supposed to do

So that: defects my passing tests miss are caught before I rely on the result

Description: The method carries guidance for a periodic and end-of-build fresh-context self-review that drives the app against its acceptance criteria to catch the defect classes green test suites miss, honestly scoped as an in-loop check subordinate to the independent verification gate that rcf build finalise runs.

Requirement

REQ-008

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-805-1 - The guidance describes a periodic and end-of-build fresh-context self-review dispatch

    Given the shipped build guidance

    When it describes the self-review

    Then it describes a fresh-context manual-review subagent dispatch run periodically (every few FBS builds) and once at the end of the build

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

  • AC-805-2 - The reviewer drives the app against the acceptance criteria rather than reading the code

    Given the self-review guidance

    When it states what the reviewer does

    Then it requires the reviewer to drive the running application against its acceptance criteria, not to read the code

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

  • AC-805-3 - The review targets the named defect classes

    Given the self-review guidance

    When it states what the review looks for

    Then it names the target defect classes: session-class bugs, false-promise UI, runtime mismatch (localhost versus deployed), dead auth paths and dead code

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

  • AC-805-4 - The guidance scopes the self-review honestly as an in-loop check and not the independent gate

    Given the self-review guidance

    When it frames the review

    Then it states plainly that this is an in-loop check and not the independent verification gate, names rcf build finalise (section 7) as the gate, and says it is guidance and not a new subsystem

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-014

  "description": "The agent guidance pack teaches a build method that keeps the deployment runtime present in the loop from elicitation to verification, so that a non-coding owner who cannot self-verify is not led into an undeployable stack or a false 'verified' claim. It requires four properties of the method the tool ships: (1) every build lands a working, documented local preview loop as its default outcome; (2) elicitation establishes where the app will run early and constrains the stack to that answer, with a jargon-free hosting-choice walkthrough when the owner does not know; (3) every 'verified' or 'tested' claim names the runtime it was checked against and never implies deploy-runtime verification that did not happen; (4) the method carries guidance for a periodic and end-of-build fresh-context self-review that drives the app against its acceptance criteria, subordinate to the independent verification gate rather than a substitute for it. This requirement governs the shipped guidance/prompt surface, not a new runtime subsystem.",
  "rationale": "The five-run rcf-persona-testing programme (concluded 2026-07-20) found the tool builds excellently at every level but its own loop missed a ship-blocking or user-facing defect in three of five runs, with a single root cause: the deploy runtime is absent from the loop. It is absent from elicitation (runs 03/04 chose Cloudflare-incompatible stacks a CF-only holder cannot host, run 03 silently) and absent from verification (run 05 shipped a production auth 500 while 89/89 tests were green and the tool claimed a live-Worker verification its E2E never ran). The target user cannot diagnose 'wrong stack for your host' or 'verified against the wrong runtime', so the method itself must foreclose both. REQ-009 Umbrella CLI: verify as a first-class subcommand cli US1 AC3 draft

Post 0.7.1 packaging consolidation the RCF Lite suite ships as one npm package with one unified `rcf` CLI. The adversarial ship-gate verifier that used to live behind its own `rcf verify` bin is mounted as `rcf verify <run|report|provision|cleanup|mcp>` on that unified CLI. The pre-existing `rcf verify` bin remains as a transition-grace alias that dispatches through the same handlers, deprecated in favour of `rcf verify`. Behaviour of each verify verb is unchanged; only the invocation form gains a canonical route.

Why: The packaging consolidation ruling (docs/2026-08-06_packaging-consolidation-proposal.md, ratified 2026-08-11) picks one install (`rcf-lite`) with one CLI verb space (`rcf`). Verify is a first-class part of the RCF chain (define, build, verify) and must sit inside that verb space, not beside it. Keeping `rcf verify` as an alias avoids a hard break for existing scripts across a transition window.

capability:project-init packaging cli verify

User stories (1)

US-901 Route the verify suite under the `rcf verify` group and delete the legacy alias bin AC3 draft

US-901 - Route the verify suite under the `rcf verify` group and delete the legacy alias bin

As a: consumer of the RCF Lite CLI

I want: to invoke the verify suite as `rcf verify <verb>` inside the unified CLI

So that: verify sits inside the same verb space as the rest of the RCF chain and I only have to install one package

Description: A consumer running the unified `rcf` CLI reaches the adversarial ship-gate verifier as `rcf verify <verb>` (run | report | provision | cleanup | mcp | browser). The pre-0.10.0 standalone `rcf-verify` bin is deleted outright; the historical 0.7.1 transition-grace alias is gone. The old flat `rcf-verify <verb>` invocation form is not available at all; consumers scripting against it must move to `rcf verify <verb>`.

Requirement

REQ-009

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-901-1 - The `rcf` bin exposes `verify` as a top-level group whose sub-verbs run | report | provision | cleanup | mcp | browser dispatch to the verify-suite handlers

    Given the unified `rcf` binary imported from bin/rcf.js

    When `verify` is looked up on the top-level GROUPS map

    Then the sub-verb resolves to the corresponding main() from src/verify/cli/{run,report,provision,cleanup,mcp}.js or src/cli/browser-verify.js

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-015

  • AC-901-2 - The top-level `rcf help` output advertises the `verify` group with its sub-verbs

    Given the unified `rcf` binary

    When `--help` or `help` runs

    Then the printed usage lists the verify group header with the sub-verb catalogue (run, report, provision, cleanup, mcp, browser)

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-015

  • AC-901-3 - The legacy standalone `rcf-verify` bin is deleted; invoking `rcf-verify <verb>` is not possible from an rcf-lite install, and calling any old flat top-level token via the umbrella `rcf` bin exits 2 with a stderr hint naming the new grouped form

    Given an installed rcf-lite@0.10.0

    When the operator invokes `rcf <old-flat-verb>` where old-flat-verb is a pre-0.10.0 name (validate, coverage, browser-verify, ...)

    Then package.json:bin carries no `rcf-verify` entry, bin/rcf-verify.js does not exist in the package, and bin/rcf.js writes '[error] usage unknown top-level command <verb>. Try rcf <group> <verb>' to stderr and exits 2 (not a back-compat fallback)

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-015

REQ-010 Blueprint library mechanism (composition, standards, selective retrieval) cli US4 AC23 draft

The framework provides a Blueprint mechanism the operator uses to compose blueprint packages (specifications + assets, not code) onto a project tree at any point in its life. Composition is many blueprints per project. Blueprint-contributed docs are namespaced by the blueprint's slug so multiple blueprints cannot collide on ids. Standards packs register at rcf init (or later via rcf define standards add), reference-by-default, copied to rcf/standards/<slug>/ only when the source lives outside the project root. Manifest registration is authoritative. Selective retrieval populates fbs.contextRequirements.standardIds at bundle-assembly time by analysing the FBS work text against the standards tag vocabulary; operator override is supported by authoring the array on the FBS. scope:global ADR contributions surface as blocking conflicts at rcf define blueprint add time.

capability:blueprint-library

User stories (4)

US-1001 Blueprint verb family: add, list, remove, upgrade AC5 draft

US-1001 - Blueprint verb family: add, list, remove, upgrade

As a: operator on an RCF project

I want: to add, list, remove and upgrade blueprints against my project tree from a single `rcf define blueprint` verb family

So that: composition is a first-class action instead of a one-shot init flag, and I can layer several blueprints across the life of a project without hand-editing the manifest

Description: A `rcf define blueprint` verb family provides the primary operator seat for composing blueprints onto a project. Every verb runs against the current tree, is idempotent where the semantics allow, and writes to the manifest's `blueprints[]` registry so the applied set is greppable and mechanical.

Requirement

REQ-010

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-1001-1 - `rcf define blueprint add <slug>` on a project with no blueprints applied writes an entry into `manifest.blueprints[]` and prints the applied slug and version

    Given a validated project tree with no existing `blueprints[]` entries and a resolvable blueprint slug

    When `rcf define blueprint add <slug>` runs

    Then the manifest gains one `blueprints[]` entry (slug, version, appliedAt, source, and any contributions[] the blueprint wrote), and stdout names the slug and applied version

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-016

  • AC-1001-2 - `rcf define blueprint list` prints every applied blueprint (slug, version, appliedAt) in apply order

    Given a project with one or more blueprints already applied

    When `rcf define blueprint list` runs

    Then every applied blueprint prints, one per line, ordered by `appliedAt`, with slug, version and apply timestamp columns

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-016

  • AC-1001-3 - `rcf define blueprint remove <slug>` removes the manifest entry and refuses when any project-authored doc references a contributed id

    Given a project with the blueprint applied and no project-authored doc referencing any of the contributions[] ids

    When `rcf define blueprint remove <slug>` runs

    Then the `blueprints[]` entry is dropped from the manifest; when a project-authored doc DOES reference a contribution, the verb exits non-zero and prints the referencing id + path without mutating the manifest

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-016

  • AC-1001-4 - `rcf define blueprint add <slug>` is idempotent: repeating on an already-applied clean slug is a no-op with a friendly message

    Given a project with `<slug>` already in `blueprints[]`

    When `rcf define blueprint add <slug>` runs again with no conflicts to surface

    Then the manifest is not rewritten, exit code is 0, and stdout names the slug as already applied at the applied version

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-016

  • AC-1001-5 - `rcf --help` lists `blueprint` alongside the other top-level commands

    Given the unified `rcf` bin

    When `rcf --help` runs

    Then the top-level usage advertises `blueprint <verb>` as an available command

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-016

US-1002 Composition, namespaced ids and scope:global ADR conflict surfacing AC10 draft

US-1002 - Composition, namespaced ids and scope:global ADR conflict surfacing

As a: operator on an RCF project

I want: blueprint contributions to compose without id collisions, and for `scope: global` ADR conflicts to be surfaced with both sides visible before anything is written

So that: composition never silently merges incompatible whole-project decisions

Description: Multiple blueprints may be applied to a single project. Blueprint-contributed docs are namespaced by the blueprint's slug so ids cannot collide across blueprints. A blueprint's ADR contributions may be tagged `scope: global`; two applied blueprints each contributing a `scope: global` ADR are a genuine conflict and `rcf define blueprint add` surfaces both entries and refuses to write. Conflict-presentation ergonomics are prototype-unknown #1 (design brief); this US covers the first pass.

Requirement

REQ-010

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-1002-1 - Blueprint-contributed doc ids are namespaced with the blueprint's slug so composition cannot collide on ids at the id layer

    Given two blueprints `spa` and `rest` that both contribute a REQ, a US and an ADR

    When both are applied to the same project via `rcf define blueprint add`

    Then every contributed id carries the blueprint slug as its prefix (REQ/US: `spa-REQ-001`, `rest-REQ-001`) or as its kebab-suffix (ADR: `ADR-004-spa-theme`, `ADR-005-rest-versioning`); no two contributed ids across the two blueprints match

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-017

  • AC-1002-2 - `rcf define blueprint add <slug>` refuses when the new blueprint contributes a `scope: global` ADR on a topic already contributed by an applied blueprint

    Given a project with blueprint `alpha` already applied contributing an ADR tagged `scope: global` on topic `versioning`

    When `rcf define blueprint add beta` runs and blueprint `beta` also contributes a `scope: global` ADR on `versioning`

    Then the verb exits non-zero, prints both ADR ids and their file paths, and the manifest is unchanged

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-017

  • AC-1002-3 - Conflict output leads with per-side headers (ADR title + one-sentence decision) and names four honest resolution paths with actual blueprint slugs filled in (Phase 3.5 reshape)

    Given the conflict case above

    When the verb prints the conflict

    Then the output opens with `conflict on topic (<topic>)` and one line per side carrying `blueprint <slug>: <title> — <decision>` (or `<id> at <path>` when the tree did not carry the ADR body), a `refs:` footer with both ids + paths, and four honest resolutions numbered 1-4: adopt-incoming (`rcf define blueprint remove <existing-slug>`), keep-existing (do not add the incoming), supersede via a project-level ADR (`rcf define blueprint supersede <topic>`), and declare-on-add (`rcf define blueprint add <source> --resolve <topic>=project:<ADR-id>`) — all with the actual conflicting blueprint slugs already substituted, no `<slug>` placeholders

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-017

  • AC-1002-4 - Non-global TACs, ADRs, REQs, USs and FBSes are namespaced and cannot conflict

    Given two blueprints each contributing a TAC on the same topic without `scope: global`

    When both are applied

    Then both TACs co-exist under distinct namespaced ids; no conflict is surfaced

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-017

  • AC-1002-5 - The supersession record's two sides are the CONFLICT PAIR — one currently-applied blueprint's scope:global ADR on the topic PLUS one incoming (would-be-applied) blueprint's scope:global ADR on the same topic — and the `rcf define blueprint supersede` verb accepts the incoming blueprint as the second side. Operator ruling (Baz, w-2026-08-19-008 round 3): option 3 as printed in the reshaped conflict message MUST be executable EXACTLY as printed from the refused-add state, with zero prep. Mechanism (builder judgement against the chain): the reshaped conflict message names option 3 as `rcf define blueprint supersede <topic> --incoming <source>`, carrying the very same `<source>` argument the refused add was invoked with; `supersede` loads the incoming blueprint from `--incoming <source>`, finds its scope:global ADR on `<topic>`, stamps its id into the incoming blueprint's namespace, and uses `{slug, adrId}` for the incoming blueprint as the second side of `manifest.resolutions[].supersedes[]`. The scaffolded project ADR file lists both blueprint ADR ids (applied + incoming stamped) under `relatedAdrs[]`; after supersede returns, re-running `rcf define blueprint add <source>` succeeds because the detector honours the freshly-recorded resolution. `--incoming <source>` is required when applied count on the topic is < 2 and is silently accepted (informational) when applied count is already >= 2.

    Given a fresh project with ZERO applied blueprints and the shipped SPA + REST blueprints on disk (both carry scope:global ADRs on camelCase topics `errorEnvelope` and `authModel`)

    When the operator runs the flow verbatim as printed: `rcf define blueprint add <spa>`; `rcf define blueprint add <rest>` (refused with the reshaped four-honest-paths message); then follows option 3 EXACTLY as printed: `rcf define blueprint supersede errorEnvelope --incoming <rest>` and `rcf define blueprint supersede authModel --incoming <rest>`; then re-runs `rcf define blueprint add <rest>`

    Then each supersede exits 0, scaffolds a project ADR at `rcf/adrs/adr-NNN-<kebab-topic>.json` (topic string verbatim on `manifest.resolutions[].topic`; ADR id tail kebab-ified per ADR-010), and appends a `manifest.resolutions[]` record listing both blueprint ADR ids in `supersedes[]`; the subsequent `rcf define blueprint add <rest>` exits 0 (detector honours the resolution) and both blueprint ADR files co-reside on disk with the project supersedes-ADR alongside them

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-017

  • AC-1002-6 - `rcf define blueprint add --reason <text>` attaches the operator's ruling text to every `manifest.resolutions[]` record minted on that add. Whitespace-only reasons are refused at the writer edge (schema does not enforce a minimum floor on the field itself; the writer's floor is emptiness, not length).

    Given an incoming blueprint whose apply would collide on one or more topics, resolved via one or more --resolve declarations

    When the operator adds `--reason "..."` alongside the --resolve flags

    Then every newly-minted resolutions[] record carries the reason string verbatim; a whitespace-only --reason exits 2 with an error naming the topic and no record is written

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-017

  • AC-1002-7 - Duplicate `--resolve` declarations for the same topic within a single `rcf define blueprint add` are deduped: the first declaration is kept, subsequent declarations on the same topic are dropped, and a `[warn]` line names each dropped topic on stderr. The add still exits 0 on success; the manifest carries exactly one resolutions[] record per topic.

    Given an incoming blueprint whose apply would collide on topic X

    When the operator passes `--resolve X=project:ADR-A --resolve X=project:ADR-B` on the same command

    Then the manifest carries exactly one resolutions[] record on topic X with `resolvedByAdrId: ADR-A` (first-wins), and stderr carries a warn line naming X as a duplicate --resolve topic

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-017

  • AC-1002-8 - Conflict enrichment is symmetric: the CLI's conflict report and `--json` output both carry `title` + one-sentence `decision` on BOTH sides of a globalAdrTopic conflict — the existing side read from the walker's tree, the incoming side read from the blueprint's ADR file on disk. Round-1 only enriched the existing side, which read asymmetrically against shipped blueprints.

    Given an incoming blueprint that would collide with an applied blueprint on a scope:global ADR topic, both ADRs carrying a title and a decision

    When `rcf define blueprint add <source>` refuses with the reshaped message (with or without --json)

    Then both `incoming` and `existing` sides render `blueprint <slug>: <title> — <decision>` in the terminal output, and `conflicts[].incoming` and `conflicts[].existing` both carry `title` and `decision` in the --json output

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-017

  • AC-1002-9 - Chain-level decision (ADR-010): the blueprint conflict-topic vocabulary is a FREE LABEL — a lookup key used by the detector (exact-match between an incoming ADR's topic and each applied ADR's topic) and stored verbatim on `manifest.resolutions[].topic`. No character-class constraint beyond the manifest schema's `minLength: 1` plus a writer-edge whitespace-only refuse. The shipped SPA + REST blueprints declare their scope:global ADR topics in camelCase (authModel, errorEnvelope, clientRouting, theming, clientState, apiVersioning, logging) and that vocabulary is canonical. Kebab-ification is confined to the projection into the ADR-id slug tail (ADR grammar requires kebab), never at the vocabulary edge.

    Given the shipped SPA + REST blueprint packs on disk (topics: authModel, errorEnvelope, ...)

    When supersede and add --resolve run on any of those topics as printed

    Then the writer accepts the topic verbatim; the manifest.resolutions[].topic value byte-matches the applied ADR's topic; the scaffolded project ADR id carries a kebab-cased tail derived from the topic (`authModel` -> `ADR-NNN-auth-model`); no rcfError references 'kebab slug' or 'valid kebab' on any non-whitespace topic string

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-017

  • AC-1002-10 - Error-message prefix discipline on supersede: rcfError messages returned from `src/blueprint/supersede.js` MUST NOT prepend their own `blueprint supersede: ` prefix — the CLI edge already writes `[error] blueprint supersede: ` on every rcfError from the supersede verb. Round-2 caught the same bug on the `add` path; round-3 catches it on the supersede path (six sites: supersede.js:54, :70, :85, :107, :145, :160).

    Given any error path in `src/blueprint/supersede.js` (missing topic, --reason whitespace-only, sub-2 applied ADRs, missing prd/tad, overwrite guard tripped, ADR write ioFailure)

    When `rcf define blueprint supersede ...` runs into that error path at the CLI

    Then the printed stderr line matches `^\[error\] blueprint supersede: <message>$` with exactly one `blueprint supersede: ` prefix; the string `blueprint supersede: blueprint supersede:` does not appear anywhere in the output

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-017

US-1003 Standards ingestion: reference by default, copy only when out of root AC4 draft

US-1003 - Standards ingestion: reference by default, copy only when out of root

As a: operator on an RCF project

I want: to register standards packs against my project tree, referencing in place when the source is already inside the repo and copying into `rcf/standards/<slug>/` only when the source lives outside the project root

So that: duplication inside the repo is not accepted, portability across machines is preserved for external sources, and the manifest is the single source of truth for what standards apply

Description: Standards packs are per operator or organisation and register at `rcf init` (or later via `rcf define standards add`). Manifest registration is authoritative. In-repo sources are referenced in place. Out-of-root sources are copied into `rcf/standards/<slug>/` so the tree remains portable. Provenance (personal vs corporate) is recorded per pack.

Requirement

REQ-010

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-1003-1 - `rcf define standards add <path>` writes a manifest entry with the pack's id, slug, sourcePath, tag vocabulary, testsProvidedBy and provenance

    Given a project with no standards registered and a valid standards folder anywhere on disk

    When `rcf define standards add <path> --slug wsd-naming --tags naming,conventions --tests-provided-by agent --provenance corporate` runs

    Then the manifest gains one `standards[]` entry with all named fields populated and validates against the schema

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-018

  • AC-1003-2 - In-repo sources are referenced in place; no copy is written

    Given a standards folder path inside the project root (e.g. `docs/standards/wsd-naming`)

    When `rcf define standards add` runs against it

    Then the `sourcePath` records the in-repo path, `copyPath` is absent, and no file is written under `rcf/standards/`

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-018

  • AC-1003-3 - Out-of-root sources are mirrored into `rcf/standards/<slug>/` and `copyPath` records the mirror

    Given a standards folder path outside the project root (an absolute path pointing outside the repo)

    When `rcf define standards add` runs against it

    Then the source is copied into `rcf/standards/<slug>/`, the manifest entry records the original `sourcePath` and the in-tree `copyPath`, and re-running the verb is idempotent (no double copy)

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-018

  • AC-1003-4 - The manifest.standards[] entry validates against the shipped schema (@stravica-ai/rcf-schemas standardsPackRecord)

    Given a manifest with one or more standards[] entries

    When `rcf define validate` runs

    Then the manifest validates without errors under the shipped schema

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-018

US-1004 Selective retrieval at bundle assembly (contextRequirements.standardIds) AC4 draft

US-1004 - Selective retrieval at bundle assembly (contextRequirements.standardIds)

As a: operator on an RCF project with standards registered

I want: the bundle assembler to select relevant standards per FBS automatically, and to honour my override when I author the array on the FBS itself

So that: the default path does not require operator authoring and the override path exists when the agentic selection needs correcting

Description: The build-context bundle assembler runs a deterministic selector during FBS bundle assembly that reads the FBS work text plus the standards manifest (tags, titles, and short summaries) and returns the subset of standard slugs relevant to the FBS. The selected slugs populate `contextRequirements.standardIds` for that bundle only. Operator override is supported by authoring the array on the FBS.

Requirement

REQ-010

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-1004-1 - The bundle for an FBS with no operator-authored standardIds carries the agentically-selected subset

    Given a project with two standards packs (`wsd-naming` tagged `naming`, `security-baseline` tagged `security`) and an FBS whose summary names `security`

    When the bundle assembler runs for that FBS with no operator-authored `standardIds`

    Then the bundle's `context` section carries `standardIds` including `security-baseline` and the pack's rendered summary in the standards payload

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-019

  • AC-1004-2 - Operator-authored `contextRequirements.standardIds` on the FBS overrides the agentic selection

    Given the same project and FBS as AC-1004-1, but with `contextRequirements.standardIds: ['wsd-naming']` authored on the FBS

    When the bundle assembler runs

    Then the bundle's `context.standardIds` matches the operator-authored value byte-for-byte; the agentic selection is not invoked

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-019

  • AC-1004-3 - The assembler never blocks on an empty selection

    Given a project with no standards registered, or an FBS whose work text matches no standard

    When the bundle assembler runs

    Then the bundle assembles with `context.standardIds` empty (or absent) and no standards payload; the assembler does not error

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-019

  • AC-1004-4 - Selection is stable per input (deterministic tag-scoring; no wall-clock or random source)

    Given an FBS work text and a standards manifest, both fixed

    When the selector is invoked twice

    Then the two returned selections are equal (same slugs, same order)

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-019

  "description": "The framework provides a Blueprint mechanism the operator uses to compose blueprint packages (specifications + assets, not code) onto a project tree at any point in its life. Composition is many blueprints per project. Blueprint-contributed docs are namespaced by the blueprint's slug so multiple blueprints cannot collide on ids. Standards packs register at rcf init (or later via rcf define standards add), reference-by-default, copied to rcf/standards/<slug>/ only when the source lives outside the project root. Manifest registration is authoritative. REQ-011 e2e verification contract: pinned Playwright MCP, declared e2e test level, doctor and init behaviour verify US4 AC18 draft

The rcf-lite verify pass provisions a version-pinned Playwright MCP server instead of @latest, prints the effective pin in preflight, and honours an emergency override. The rcf method exposes e2e as a declared test level: the application-spa blueprint declares a browserSurface, contributes browser-facing acceptance criteria, and cross-links a test-case template to the browser-verify TAC; the delivery-ci-workflows blueprint materialises a distinct e2e CI job when an applied blueprint declares a browserSurface. rcf doctor gains playwright-present, browser-present, playwright-mcp-reachable, and playwright-mcp-redundant checks for browser-facing projects; non-browser projects skip the three with one reason line. rcf init writes a Playwright MCP entry only when a project-scope signature is absent and a user-scope harness probe cannot prove one exists; otherwise it leaves the wiring alone or writes the distinctly named playwright-rcf fallback. All four parts observe the ratified 2026-09-03 e2e contract at projects/rcf-lite-wsd/specs/rcf-lite-e2e-contract-spec-2026-09-03.md.

Why: Verify is the ship gate. A silent runtime change in the browser MCP on the next verify run is the reproducibility hole Baz named on 2026-09-03. Pinning the MCP closes it. Formalising e2e as a declared test level gives browser-facing projects a first-class contract instead of relying on the verify browser stage as a proxy for coverage. Doctor and init together make Playwright the operator's decision, not rcf-lite's ambient inheritance.

capability:verify verify playwright-mcp e2e blueprint-library doctor init

User stories (4)

US-1101 Verify pins the Playwright MCP version and prints it in preflight AC4 draft

US-1101 - Verify pins the Playwright MCP version and prints it in preflight

As a: operator running rcf verify as the ship gate

I want: the verify launcher to provision a version-pinned @playwright/mcp instead of @latest, print the effective pin in preflight, record it in the report, and honour an emergency override with a loud stderr notice

So that: a newly published Playwright MCP release cannot become a silent runtime change on the next verify run, and every report artefact carries the exact browser tooling version the pass ran against

Requirement

REQ-011

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-1101-1 - packages/rcf-lite/src/verify/engine/launcher.js exports a PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VERSION constant, and DEFAULT_MCP_CONFIG.args composes @playwright/mcp@<PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VERSION> instead of @playwright/mcp@latest.

    Given the rcf-lite source at HEAD

    When the launcher module is imported

    Then PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VERSION resolves to a semver string and DEFAULT_MCP_CONFIG.mcpServers.playwright.args contains the exact-pinned @playwright/mcp@<version> token, with no @latest anywhere in the module

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-020

  • AC-1101-2 - rcf verify run prints one preflight line naming the effective @playwright/mcp pin on stderr; the line is not suppressed by --quiet.

    Given a browser-facing fixture project and a stubbed verify launcher

    When rcf verify run is invoked with valid required flags

    Then stderr contains one line matching /^Playwright MCP: pinned to @playwright\/mcp@/ carrying the effective pin

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-020

  • AC-1101-3 - rcf verify run --playwright-mcp-version <semver> overrides the pinned constant for one run, prints a loud stderr override notice, and records the effective pin on the report as runStats.playwrightMcpVersion. A non-semver value refuses with exit 2.

    Given the same fixture, run with --playwright-mcp-version 0.0.99

    When the run completes

    Then stderr carries one line matching /^Playwright MCP: OVERRIDE @playwright\/mcp@0\.0\.99/, the report's run.runStats.playwrightMcpVersion equals 0.0.99, and rerunning with --playwright-mcp-version notasemver exits 2 with a semver-shape error

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-020

  • AC-1101-4 - Even when no override fires, the report records the effective (default) pin as run.runStats.playwrightMcpVersion so a report re-render tells the operator what browser tooling the pass ran against.

    Given a completed verify run with no override

    When the report JSON is inspected

    Then report.run.runStats.playwrightMcpVersion equals PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VERSION

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-020

US-1102 Application-spa declares browserSurface and delivery-ci-workflows materialises an e2e CI job AC5 draft

US-1102 - Application-spa declares browserSurface and delivery-ci-workflows materialises an e2e CI job

As a: operator applying the application-spa and delivery-ci-workflows blueprints

I want: the SPA blueprint's manifest to declare a browserSurface field, its browser-facing acceptance criteria and e2e test-case template to ship, and the delivery-ci-workflows materialiser to wire a distinct e2e CI job when at least one applied blueprint carries a browserSurface

So that: e2e is a first-class declared test level in the chain, and browser-facing projects get a distinct pull-request-checks e2e job while API-only projects keep the existing workflow shape verbatim

Requirement

REQ-011

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-1102-1 - blueprints/application-spa/blueprint.json is at version 1.4.0 and carries a top-level browserSurface object with declared: true; the object also carries routes[] and themes[] as reference hint arrays.

    Given the SPA blueprint at HEAD

    When blueprint.json is inspected

    Then version equals 1.4.0 and .browserSurface.declared is true

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-021

  • AC-1102-2 - The SPA blueprint contributes two new browser-facing acceptance criteria in the 1101 to 1899 band (existing 1131 and 1132 are already occupied by unrelated 1.3.x contributions): US-1134 binds an e2e AC on application-spa-REQ-011 (iconography), US-1135 binds an e2e AC on application-spa-REQ-009 (user arrival and auth surfaces); a paste-in assets/tc-templates/e2e.md test-case template ships and names the browser-verify TAC as its driver seam.

    Given the SPA blueprint at HEAD

    When blueprints/application-spa/contributions/user-stories/ and blueprints/application-spa/assets/tc-templates/ are inspected

    Then application-spa-us-1134.json and application-spa-us-1135.json exist, each binds one AC whose scope is deployed and whose description names an e2e observable at a rendered browser surface; assets/tc-templates/e2e.md exists and references TAC-208

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-021

  • AC-1102-3 - blueprints/delivery-ci-workflows/blueprint.json is at version 2.2.0 and contributes a new US-6124 whose AC binds the elicited e2e check to a distinct e2e CI job that runs project testLevel: e2e cases against a local preview or --parity-env runtime, uploads browser artefacts, and reports a distinct row in the aggregate pipeline report.

    Given the delivery-ci-workflows blueprint at HEAD

    When blueprint.json and contributions/user-stories/delivery-ci-workflows-us-6124.json are inspected

    Then version equals 2.2.0 and the US-6124 record binds an AC-6124-1 whose description names the four points above

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-021

  • AC-1102-4 - The illustrative GHA workflow at blueprints/delivery-ci-workflows/assets/ci-provider-examples/github-actions/pull-request-checks.yml carries a documented e2e job, and the alternate-provider notes file at ../notes.md carries one line per provider translating the same four points.

    Given the delivery-ci-workflows blueprint at HEAD

    When the illustrative workflow file is inspected

    Then the workflow declares an e2e job as an example, and notes.md contains one line per provider (GitLab CI, CircleCI, Buildkite, Jenkins) naming the four points

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-021

  • AC-1102-5 - Applying application-spa v1.4.0 to a scratch project produces a manifest that still validates against rcf-schemas 0.5.1; the applied blueprint record carries no new field, and doctor and the delivery-ci-workflows materialiser both read browserSurface from the applied record's source blueprint.json via the existing manifest.blueprints[].source reference.

    Given a scratch project created by rcf init with application-spa v1.4.0 applied

    When the resulting rcf/manifest.json is validated against the shipped schemas

    Then validation passes and no browserSurface key appears on the applied blueprint record itself

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-021

US-1103 rcf doctor checks Playwright and a browser on browser-facing projects and skips them otherwise AC4 draft

US-1103 - rcf doctor checks Playwright and a browser on browser-facing projects and skips them otherwise

As a: operator running rcf doctor on either a browser-facing or an API-only project

I want: doctor to run playwright-present, browser-present, and playwright-mcp-reachable checks when at least one applied blueprint declares a browserSurface, and to skip all three with one printed reason line otherwise

So that: browser-facing projects surface missing Playwright, missing browser, or an unreachable @playwright/mcp with actionable fix lines, while API-only projects are not asked to install a browser stack they will never use

Requirement

REQ-011

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-1103-1 - packages/rcf-lite/package.json declares @playwright/mcp and playwright as optional peer dependencies (peerDependenciesMeta.<pkg>.optional: true). npm and pnpm do not fail install when the peers are absent.

    Given packages/rcf-lite at HEAD

    When package.json is inspected

    Then .peerDependencies['@playwright/mcp'] and .peerDependencies.playwright are declared and .peerDependenciesMeta.<pkg>.optional is true for both

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-022

  • AC-1103-2 - On a browser-facing fixture project (application-spa v1.4.0 applied), rcf doctor runs playwright-present, browser-present, and playwright-mcp-reachable; each check emits at most one fix line naming the exact remedy per the spec's fix-line table.

    Given a browser-facing fixture with no @playwright/mcp installed

    When rcf doctor is run

    Then the three checks appear in the drift output and their fix lines match the spec's fix-line strings

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-022

  • AC-1103-3 - On an API-only fixture project (application-api-rest applied, no browser-facing blueprint), rcf doctor prints one line naming the three skipped checks and their skip reason. The line is not suppressed by --quiet.

    Given an API-only fixture project

    When rcf doctor is run

    Then stdout contains exactly one line 'rcf doctor: skipping playwright-present, browser-present, playwright-mcp-reachable (no applied blueprint declares a browser surface).'

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-022

  • AC-1103-4 - The three checks are legal values of --check <check>[,check]; passing one explicitly on a non-browser project overrides the skip and runs it.

    Given an API-only fixture project

    When rcf doctor --check playwright-present is run

    Then the playwright-present check runs and reports its result rather than being skipped

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-022
