REQ-053 T-1 lifecycle events facadeReady kvHit kvMiss kvWrite carry metadata-only fields key size ttl timestamp platform US2 AC2 draft

T-1 lifecycle events. The facade emits facadeReady on the injected sink once the ready-check returns; kvHit on a get that resolves to a non-null value; kvMiss on a get that resolves to null; kvWrite on put and delete. Every event record carries EXACTLY the fields {event, key, size, ttl, timestamp}: no body bytes, no metadata bag pass-through, no user id beyond the key itself. The event-secrecy probe drives this at REQ-053 mechanism reach.

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (2)

US-5301 T-1 lifecycle events fire on facadeReady kvHit kvMiss kvWrite with metadata-only payload AC1 draft

US-5301 - T-1 lifecycle events fire on facadeReady kvHit kvMiss kvWrite with metadata-only payload

As a: shelf consumer applying platform-cloudflare-kv v1.0.0

I want: the facade to emit facadeReady kvHit kvMiss kvWrite events with metadata-only payload on the injected sink

So that: the applied logging companion can render KV activity without ever writing a body byte to the log stream

Requirement

REQ-053

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-5301-1 - Each lifecycle event emitted by the facade carries EXACTLY the whitelist {event, key, size, ttl, timestamp}. No body value, no metadata blob, no additional field ever appears on the record the sink receives.

    Given the facade wired to a spy event sink, with a mix of put/get/delete/list operations

    When the operations run

    Then the sink records each event with only the whitelist keys; any extra key trips the probe

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-070

US-5302 T-1 event secrecy: no body bytes no PII no user id beyond the key ever reach the event sink AC1 draft

US-5302 - T-1 event secrecy: no body bytes no PII no user id beyond the key ever reach the event sink

As a: shelf consumer applying platform-cloudflare-kv v1.0.0

I want: the event-secrecy probe to prove no body bytes or PII ever reach the event sink

So that: the operator can trust that a KV that holds a PII fixture (users/1234/profile with SSN) never leaks the body to the log stream even under a mutation-run

Requirement

REQ-053

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-5302-1 - The event-secrecy probe puts, gets and deletes a PII fixture (key users/1234/profile, body {ssn: REDACTED-fixture}); every event record on the sink carries only the whitelist and no substring of the SSN, no substring of the user id beyond the key itself, and no substring of the body. A mutation-run turning on SIMULATE_PII_LEAK flips the probe to fail with the leaked field named.

    Given the facade wired to a spy sink with a PII fixture

    When put/get/delete operations run on the PII key

    Then the recorded events contain only the whitelist; PII-substring scan returns zero hits; the mutation-run under SIMULATE_PII_LEAK trips the probe to fail

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-070

REQ-054 T-1 eventual-consistency note in the guide: a write may not appear on a global read within the same request and the elicited TTL sets the staleness ceiling platform US1 AC1 draft

T-1 eventual-consistency note: Workers KV is eventually consistent per the Cloudflare KV consistency documentation at https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/concepts/how-kv-works/. A write may not appear on a global read within the same request; the elicited cache-aside TTL (default 60 seconds per Cloudflare-documented cache TTL default) sets the staleness ceiling readers observe. The guide surfaces the note and the decision-tree cross-reference to platform-cloudflare-durable-objects for strong-consistency needs (round-6 T-3 owns the DO adapter).

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (1)

US-5401 T-1 real-account eventual-consistency smoke: write eventually appears on a global read within a bounded 60-second cap or records accountBoundSkipped in CI AC1 draft

US-5401 - T-1 real-account eventual-consistency smoke: write eventually appears on a global read within a bounded 60-second cap or records accountBoundSkipped in CI

As a: shelf consumer applying platform-cloudflare-kv v1.0.0 in CI with real Cloudflare credentials

I want: the real-account eventual-consistency smoke to open the facade against a real KV namespace and observe the write eventually appearing on a global read

So that: the applied project has one probe that exercises the real vendor surface (not just the in-memory driver) and closes the mechanism-reach gap between fixture and production

Requirement

REQ-054

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-5401-1 - When CI_HAS_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT is set (with CF_ACCOUNT_ID, CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID and CF_API_TOKEN), the real-account probe opens the facade against the real KV namespace via the Workers KV REST API, writes a fixture key, polls the same key with bounded 60-second cap, and asserts the value eventually returns. Without CI_HAS_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT the probe records accountBoundSkipped true and the aggregate flips to pass per spec section 3.5. The probe cleans up its written key on exit.

    Given the real-account smoke shim with or without CI_HAS_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT

    When the shim runs

    Then with the env var: the write eventually returns within 60 seconds and the aggregate is pass; without: the aggregate is pass and the report records accountBoundSkipped true

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-070

REQ-060 T-2 platform-cloudflare-cron-triggers v1.0.0 blueprint: the scheduled() handler is the sole reader of the Cron Trigger event and opens on boot with cronReady platform US3 AC3 draft

T-2 platform-cloudflare-cron-triggers v1.0.0: one scheduled() handler in the applied project source tree is the SOLE reader of the Cloudflare Workers Cron Trigger event (the event handler shape documented at https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/cron-triggers/). The handler binds on boot, wires the dispatcher (REQ-061) and the event sink (per TAC-3303), and emits a cronReady lifecycle event on the injected sink with a metadata-only payload. Chain: HQ round-6 T-2 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07T12:25Z.

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (3)

US-6001 T-2 scheduled() handler opens against the elicited cron triggers on boot and emits cronReady AC1 draft

US-6001 - T-2 scheduled() handler opens against the elicited cron triggers on boot and emits cronReady

As a: shelf consumer applying the platform-cloudflare-cron-triggers v1.0.0 blueprint on a Workers project using the cf-platform fixture

I want: one scheduled() handler module (src/scheduled.mjs) that opens against the elicited cron triggers on process boot, wires the dispatcher and event sink, and emits a cronReady lifecycle event with a metadata-only payload

So that: boot ordering is observable, the scheduled seam is a single call site, and the applied project can compose its own bootstrapping around one predictable event

Requirement

REQ-060

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-6001-1 - On process boot, the scheduled handler binds against the elicited cron triggers (the [triggers] crons block in wrangler.toml on the fixture), wires the dispatcher and the injected event sink, and emits a cronReady event on the sink with a payload of exactly {event, key, size, ttl, timestamp} where key is null, size is 0 and ttl is null. The scheduled handler does NOT dereference the KV binding (env.CACHE stays owned by the T-1 facade).

    Given a Node or Worker process with the scheduled handler module imported and its factory invoked with the elicited configuration

    When the process boots and the scheduled handler ready() call resolves

    Then a cronReady event fires on the injected event sink with the metadata-only payload; the module does not dereference env.CACHE

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-080

US-6002 T-2 wrangler dev --test-scheduled fires cronFired on the fixture handler AC1 draft

REQ-060

On a shipped wrangler regression that prevents --test-scheduled from binding, the probe returns aggregateVerdict: warn with the observed CLI stderr quoted and the mechanism-reach gap noted, per section 3.1 pass-with-skip conventions.

US-6003 T-2 real-account live-cron smoke fires cronFired at least once against a real Cloudflare Worker AC1 draft

US-6003 - T-2 real-account live-cron smoke fires cronFired at least once against a real Cloudflare Worker

As a: operator validating platform-cloudflare-cron-triggers v1.0.0 against a real Cloudflare account

I want: the real-account-scheduled-smoke probe to schedule a per-minute cron on a real Worker, wait bounded 90 seconds and assert cronFired fires at least once

So that: the shipped scheduled() surface is proven against the vendor's global cron scheduler, not only against wrangler dev

Requirement

REQ-060

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-6003-1 - The real-account-scheduled-smoke probe, when CI_HAS_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT=true and the paired CF_ACCOUNT_ID / CF_WORKER_NAME / CF_API_TOKEN env vars are set, deploys a scheduled Worker with a per-minute cron expression (* * * * *), waits bounded 90 seconds (poll every 5s) for a cronFired event to appear on the Worker's log stream, and returns aggregateVerdict: pass. Without CI_HAS_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT the probe records accountBoundSkipped: true and aggregates to pass per spec section 3.5.

    Given a real Cloudflare account with the paired env vars, or no such account and CI_HAS_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT unset

    When the probe runs

    Then with the account: cronFired appears within 90s and the probe passes. Without the account: the probe records accountBoundSkipped: true and exits 0.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-080

REQ-061 T-2 expression-router: multiple cron expressions route to distinct handlers by expression match platform US1 AC2 draft

T-2 platform-cloudflare-cron-triggers v1.0.0: the dispatcher module accepts an ordered map of cron-expression to handler pairs and, on every scheduled() invocation, matches the incoming Cron Trigger event's cron expression against the map and routes exactly to the matched handler. An unmatched expression records an unmatchedExpression event on the sink and the scheduled invocation returns without side effect. The routed handler receives a bounded context {expression, scheduledTime, sink} so its own emissions can be attributed. Chain: HQ round-6 T-2 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07T12:25Z.

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (1)

US-6101 T-2 dispatcher routes multiple cron expressions to distinct handlers by expression match AC2 draft

US-6101 - T-2 dispatcher routes multiple cron expressions to distinct handlers by expression match

As a: developer whose Worker needs to schedule two or more distinct workloads on distinct cron cadences

I want: one dispatcher module (src/dispatcher.mjs) that accepts an ordered map of cron expressions to handler functions and, on every scheduled invocation, routes to the matched handler with a bounded context

So that: one wrangler.toml [triggers] block with multiple cron expressions cleanly maps to distinct handler code paths without hand-rolled conditionals

Requirement

REQ-061

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-6101-1 - createDispatcher({routes: [{expression, handler}, ...], eventSink}) returns a dispatch(event) function. Calling dispatch({cron: '* * * * *', scheduledTime}) invokes exactly the handler whose expression is '* * * * *' and passes {expression, scheduledTime, sink} to it; no other route's handler is called on that dispatch.

    Given a dispatcher wired with two routes and two spy handlers

    When dispatch is called with a specific expression

    Then only the matched spy handler is invoked exactly once with the bounded context

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-080

  • AC-6101-2 - Calling dispatch({cron: expressionNotInRoutes, scheduledTime}) does NOT invoke any handler, fires a cronUnmatched event on the sink with metadata {expression, scheduledTime, outcome: unmatched, duration: 0} and returns without side effect.

    Given a dispatcher wired with two routes and two spy handlers

    When dispatch is called with an expression not in the routes

    Then no spy is called, a cronUnmatched event fires, and dispatch returns without side effect

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-080

REQ-062 T-2 skew tolerance: a fire inside the elicited window is onTime; outside it records cronSkewed with the delta platform US1 AC2 draft

T-2 platform-cloudflare-cron-triggers v1.0.0: an elicited skew-tolerance window (default 30 seconds per ADR-3303; floor 5s, ceiling 5 minutes) governs how the dispatcher classifies a fire. If the observed handler start time is within the window of the event's scheduledTime, the fire's outcome is onTime and a cronFired event carries {expression, scheduledTime, outcome: onTime, duration}. If the observed start is outside the window, a cronSkewed event fires with the delta (observed minus scheduled, in milliseconds) and the outcome is skewed; the handler still runs. Chain: HQ round-6 T-2 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07T12:25Z.

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (1)

US-6201 T-2 skew tolerance: fires inside the elicited window are onTime; outside record cronSkewed with delta AC2 draft

US-6201 - T-2 skew tolerance: fires inside the elicited window are onTime; outside record cronSkewed with delta

As a: operator observing the timeliness of scheduled work on a Worker

I want: the dispatcher to classify every fire against an elicited skew window and record cronSkewed for late fires with the delta

So that: the applied logging companion surfaces cron drift as a first-class signal without every handler having to keep its own clock

Requirement

REQ-062

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-6201-1 - With an elicited skew window of 30 seconds and a fake clock aligned to scheduledTime, dispatching a scheduled event fires cronFired with {expression, scheduledTime, outcome: onTime, duration: >=0} on the sink; no cronSkewed event fires for that dispatch.

    Given a dispatcher configured with skewToleranceMs=30000 and a fake clock aligned to scheduledTime

    When an event is dispatched

    Then a cronFired event fires with outcome onTime and no cronSkewed fires

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-080

  • AC-6201-2 - With an elicited skew window of 30 seconds and a fake clock advanced 60000ms past scheduledTime, dispatching a scheduled event fires cronSkewed with {expression, scheduledTime, outcome: skewed, duration: >=0, deltaMs: 60000} on the sink; the routed handler still runs.

    Given a dispatcher configured with skewToleranceMs=30000 and a fake clock advanced 60000ms past scheduledTime

    When an event is dispatched

    Then a cronSkewed event fires with the observed delta and the handler still runs

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-080

REQ-063 T-2 soft budget and event secrecy: a handler running past the elicited budget logs cronStalled but does not terminate; every event record is metadata-only platform US2 AC3 draft

T-2 platform-cloudflare-cron-triggers v1.0.0: an elicited soft-budget duration (default 30 seconds per elicited answer, no floor) governs when a running handler is flagged as stalled. The dispatcher never terminates a handler on soft-budget breach (Cloudflare's platform concern is the sole terminator); it fires a cronStalled event with metadata-only payload {expression, scheduledTime, outcome: stalled, duration, softBudgetMs} at the moment the observed duration crosses the budget and lets the handler continue. Every scheduled-side event record on the sink carries only {expression, scheduledTime, outcome, duration} plus the event tag; handler input closures, PII fields and body bytes never cross the sink boundary. Chain: HQ round-6 T-2 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07T12:25Z.

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (2)

US-6301 T-2 soft budget: a handler running past the elicited budget logs cronStalled and continues AC2 draft

US-6301 - T-2 soft budget: a handler running past the elicited budget logs cronStalled and continues

As a: operator observing long-running scheduled work on a Worker

I want: the dispatcher to fire cronStalled at the moment a handler's observed duration crosses the elicited soft budget, without terminating the handler

So that: the applied logging companion surfaces stalled fires as a first-class signal, and the Worker's own CPU budget remains the vendor's concern

Requirement

REQ-063

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-6301-1 - With softBudgetMs=100 and a spy handler that resolves after 250ms of fake-clock time, dispatching fires exactly one cronStalled event on the sink with {expression, scheduledTime, outcome: stalled, duration: >=100, softBudgetMs: 100} at the moment the observed duration crosses 100ms.

    Given a dispatcher configured with softBudgetMs=100 and a spy handler that resolves after 250ms fake-clock

    When an event is dispatched

    Then a cronStalled event fires exactly once with the observed duration at or past the budget

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-080

  • AC-6301-2 - With softBudgetMs=100 and a spy handler that resolves after 250ms of fake-clock time, the dispatcher does NOT terminate the handler on the soft-budget breach; the handler runs to completion, resolves, and a final cronFired event follows the cronStalled record with the total duration.

    Given a dispatcher configured with softBudgetMs=100 and a spy handler that resolves after 250ms fake-clock

    When an event is dispatched

    Then the handler runs to completion and a cronFired follows the cronStalled record

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-080

US-6302 T-2 event secrecy: every scheduled-side event record carries only metadata; no closure or PII AC1 draft

US-6302 - T-2 event secrecy: every scheduled-side event record carries only metadata; no closure or PII

As a: security reviewer reading the applied logging companion's stream

I want: every cron lifecycle event record to carry only {event, expression, scheduledTime, outcome, duration} and optional numeric metadata fields; never a handler input, closure or PII substring

So that: the logging stream stays safe to ship to any downstream sink without a per-blueprint scrub pass

Requirement

REQ-063

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-6302-1 - The event-secrecy probe drives the dispatcher with a spy handler that receives a PII fixture ({userId, ssn}) via a closure, and drives put/get/delete-style operations on a fixture key. The probe asserts (layer 1) every event record's keys are a subset of the allow-list {event, expression, scheduledTime, outcome, duration, softBudgetMs, deltaMs}; and (layer 2) the JSON serialisation of every record (excluding the expression field, which is a legitimate literal from wrangler.toml) contains no PII substring (userId numeric, ssn placeholder). SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=true injects a wrapper sink that forwards the closure onto the record; the probe surfaces the forbidden keys and the leaked substrings and returns aggregateVerdict: fail.

    Given the event-secrecy probe run under both modes

    When the shipped code path runs without the switch; the mutation-path runs with SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=true

    Then shipped: aggregateVerdict pass with zero forbidden keys and zero PII hits. Switch on: aggregateVerdict fail with the leaked fields named.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-080

REQ-070 T-3 platform-cloudflare-durable-objects v1.0.0 blueprint: the DO facade is the sole reader of env.CELL and env.HUB and opens on boot with namespaceReady platform US2 AC2 draft

T-3 platform-cloudflare-durable-objects v1.0.0: one DO facade module in the applied project source tree is the SOLE reader of env.CELL and env.HUB (per https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/). On process boot, the facade wires the injected event sink and emits a namespaceReady lifecycle event with a metadata-only payload; the facade exposes typed handles per named object (cellHandle(name), hubHandle(name)) and never exposes the raw binding to consumers. Chain: HQ round-6 T-3 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07 (REQ-070..079 / US-70xx..79xx / TS-100..109 / FBS-090..099 / CN-290..319).

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (2)

US-7001 T-3 DO facade opens against env.CELL and env.HUB and emits namespaceReady AC1 draft

US-7001 - T-3 DO facade opens against env.CELL and env.HUB and emits namespaceReady

As a: shelf consumer applying the platform-cloudflare-durable-objects v1.0.0 blueprint on a Workers project using the cf-platform fixture

I want: one DO facade module (src/do-facade.mjs) that opens against env.CELL and env.HUB on boot, wires the injected event sink and emits a namespaceReady lifecycle event with a metadata-only payload

So that: boot ordering is observable, the DO namespace seam is a single call site, and the applied project can compose its own bootstrapping around one predictable event

Requirement

REQ-070

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-7001-1 - On process boot, createDoFacadeInProcess (the in-process seam over the shipped facade code path) wires the injected event sink and emits a namespaceReady event on the sink with a payload of exactly {event, key, size, ttl, timestamp} where key is null, size is 0 and ttl is null. facade.cell(name) and facade.hub(name) return the registered SingleCellObject and HubObject instances.

    Given a facade wired with in-process SingleCellObject and HubObject instances and a spy event sink

    When the facade ready() call resolves

    Then a namespaceReady event fires exactly once on the sink with the metadata-only payload; the registered handles return the instances

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-090

REQ-071 T-3 single-cell shape exposes typed domain verbs and serialises concurrent invocations per instance platform US1 AC1 draft

T-3 single-cell shape: a named SingleCellObject exposes typed domain verbs (increment, read, reset) that wrap the injected storage driver. Cloudflare's documented DO consistency model serialises invocations against the same instance; the shipped class realises that contract via a per-instance FIFO promise queue so a concurrent-increment probe observes the counter sum and one increment observed the other via a written witness (per REQ-071 and AC-33102-1, AC-33109-1).

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (1)

US-7101 T-3 single-cell concurrent increments serialise per instance and return witness of prior write AC1 draft

US-7101 - T-3 single-cell concurrent increments serialise per instance and return witness of prior write

As a: developer whose Worker needs an authoritative counter, session store or lock behind a swappable boundary

I want: one SingleCellObject instance to observe concurrent increments in per-instance FIFO order and return the sum plus a written witness

So that: two concurrent callers cannot silently overwrite each other and a domain assertion can prove the write happened before the read

Requirement

REQ-071

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-7101-1 - Two concurrent increment(1) invocations against a SingleCellObject with counter 0 resolve to counters [1, 2] and witnesses [0, 1] in FIFO order; a subsequent read() returns counter 2.

    Given a SingleCellObject at counter 0

    When two concurrent increment(1) calls fire and read() follows

    Then counters are [1,2], witnesses are [0,1], read returns 2

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-090

REQ-072 T-3 storage API provides typed put/get/delete on the object with an elicited backend (SQL or KV) platform US1 AC1 draft

T-3 storage API: the object's state.storage surface exposes typed put(key,value), get(key), delete(key) and list({prefix}) verbs. Storage backend is elicited (sql or kv per ADR-3403); the shipped storage driver factory is backend-agnostic and threads through the elicited answer as driver.backend. A storage-round-trip probe drives both backends via a fixture switch (AC-33103-1, AC-33111-1).

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (1)

US-7201 T-3 storage round-trip covers put/get/delete/list on both SQL and KV backends AC1 draft

US-7201 - T-3 storage round-trip covers put/get/delete/list on both SQL and KV backends

As a: developer configuring the storage backend on a new SingleCellObject

I want: the shipped storage driver factory to round-trip put/get/delete/list on both SQL and KV backends

So that: the applied project can elicit the backend at apply time and the shipped code path exercises both branches without code changes

Requirement

REQ-072

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-7201-1 - createInMemoryDoStorage({backend: "sql"}) and createInMemoryDoStorage({backend: "kv"}) both round-trip put("k","v")->get("k"), delete("k") followed by get returning undefined, and list({prefix:"p/"}) returning a Map keyed by the prefix. driver.backend reports the chosen backend on each factory.

    Given two storage drivers, one on each backend

    When put/get/delete/list operations are driven on each driver in turn

    Then both round-trip identically and driver.backend reports the elicited answer

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-090

REQ-073 T-3 alarm surface fires alarm() exactly once per scheduled time and doAlarmFired carries objectName and scheduledTime platform US1 AC1 draft

T-3 alarm surface: a named object supports storage.setAlarm(scheduledTime) and an alarm() handler. The shipped alarm handler drains the persisted alarm from storage on each fire so a second alarm() call on the drained storage does not re-fire for the same schedule; the injected event sink records a doAlarmFired event with {objectName, scheduledTime} metadata fields on each fire (AC-33104-1, AC-33106-1).

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (1)

US-7301 T-3 alarm fires exactly once and doAlarmFired records objectName and scheduledTime AC1 draft

US-7301 - T-3 alarm fires exactly once and doAlarmFired records objectName and scheduledTime

As a: developer whose SingleCellObject schedules future work via storage.setAlarm

I want: the alarm() handler to fire exactly once per scheduled time and doAlarmFired to carry objectName and scheduledTime

So that: the applied project can observe alarm delivery through the metadata-only sink and trust the once-per-schedule contract

Requirement

REQ-073

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-7301-1 - A SingleCellObject with setAlarm(100) fires alarm() once. The handler drains the persisted alarm (storage.getAlarm returns null after) and emits doAlarmFired with objectName and scheduledTime. A second alarm() call on the drained storage records scheduledTime null (no re-fire for the same schedule).

    Given a SingleCellObject with setAlarm(100)

    When alarm() is driven once and then again after the fire

    Then the first fire emits doAlarmFired with the scheduledTime; the second fire records scheduledTime null; storage.getAlarm returns null after the first fire

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-090

REQ-074 T-3 hibernatable WebSocket hub accepts clients via state.acceptWebSocket and the wake handler runs from cold reading the same storage platform US2 AC2 draft

T-3 hibernatable WebSocket hub: a named HubObject accepts websocket clients via state.acceptWebSocket, routes each webSocketMessage by JSON type field, and broadcasts to all connected sockets. Storage persists the last broadcast so a re-emerging client can catch up; on hibernate-and-wake the wake handler runs from a cold start, reads the same storage, and emits doWakeUp exactly once (idempotent-by-contract per ADR-3405) (AC-33105-1, AC-33110-1).

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (2)

US-7401 T-3 hub broadcast fans out a payload from A to all connected clients within the elicited window AC1 draft

US-7401 - T-3 hub broadcast fans out a payload from A to all connected clients within the elicited window

As a: developer coordinating multiplayer websocket clients through one authoritative hub

I want: the HubObject to fan out a broadcast payload from one connected client to all connected clients within the elicited window

So that: the shipped hub shape delivers the coordinated-multiplayer contract without a hand-rolled broadcast layer

Requirement

REQ-074

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-7401-1 - A HubObject with two accepted fake websockets A and B, when driven with webSocketMessage(A, JSON.stringify({type:"broadcast", payload:"ping"})), delivers a JSON message to both A and B whose type is "broadcast" and payload is "ping" within 500ms elapsed on the fixture clock. The persisted lastBroadcast key in storage carries the serialised outbound payload.

    Given a HubObject with two accepted fake websockets

    When a broadcast message is sent from A

    Then both A and B receive the broadcast within 500ms; storage.get("lastBroadcast") returns the serialised payload

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-090

US-7402 T-3 hibernate-and-wake round-trip preserves storage and doWakeUp fires exactly once AC1 draft

US-7402 - T-3 hibernate-and-wake round-trip preserves storage and doWakeUp fires exactly once

As a: developer whose HubObject hibernates when idle and wakes on the next message

I want: the wake handler to run from cold and read the same lastBroadcast key from storage the pre-hibernate state persisted

So that: a re-emerging client can catch up on the missed broadcast without a full re-sync

Requirement

REQ-074

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-7402-1 - A HubObject that has processed a broadcast, hibernated (doHibernate emitted), and then woken (doWakeUp emitted once) resolves wake() with lastBroadcast equal to the serialised outbound payload. A second wake() resolves with alreadyAwake=true and the same lastBroadcast; no second doWakeUp fires.

    Given a HubObject with a persisted lastBroadcast that has hibernated

    When wake() is called once, then again

    Then the first wake emits doWakeUp once and returns lastBroadcast; the second wake reports alreadyAwake without a second event

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-090

REQ-075 T-3 lifecycle events fire at namespace and object level with metadata-only payloads platform US1 AC1 draft

T-3 lifecycle events: the facade and both DO classes emit metadata-only records on the injected event sink: namespaceReady (facade), doAccept, doAlarmFired, doWakeUp, doHibernate (object). Every record carries only allowed keys drawn from {event, key, size, ttl, timestamp, objectName, scheduledTime}; no message payloads, request bodies or PII cross the sink. The event-secrecy result on the websocket-hub-broadcast probe (AC-33106-1) covers the metadata-only contract on the shipped path.

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (1)

US-7501 T-3 lifecycle events on the shipped path carry only allowed metadata keys AC1 draft

US-7501 - T-3 lifecycle events on the shipped path carry only allowed metadata keys

As a: reviewer verifying the platform-cloudflare-durable-objects v1.0.0 blueprint at mechanism reach

I want: every lifecycle event emitted on the shipped code path to carry only the allowed metadata keys and never a forbidden key

So that: a logging companion can render the sink directly without a per-blueprint scrub pass

Requirement

REQ-075

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-7501-1 - The event-secrecy result on the websocket-hub-broadcast probe scans every record emitted through the facade and both DO classes on the shipped path and asserts every top-level key is drawn from {event, key, size, ttl, timestamp, objectName, scheduledTime}. Under SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=true a wrapped sink forwards a synthetic body-bearing record; the probe surfaces the forbidden keys (body, ssn, userId) and returns fail on the AC-33106-1 result.

    Given a driven facade + single-cell + hub with an accumulating spy sink, and the SIMULATE_PII_LEAK switch

    When the event-secrecy AC-33106-1 result runs on the shipped path and the simulate path

    Then the shipped path returns pass with zero forbidden keys; the simulate path surfaces the injected fields and returns fail

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-090

REQ-076 T-3 sole-reader guarantee enforced by AST scan: no non-facade module imports env.CELL or env.HUB platform US1 AC1 draft

T-3 sole-reader guarantee: the shipped sole-reader-scan probe reads every .mjs/.js/.ts file under the fixture's applied source root, strips block and line comments, and matches literal occurrences of env.CELL and env.HUB against the file path. The clean-fixture pass asserts src/do-facade.mjs is the ONLY file whose live source matches; any other file with a live match is a leak returned as fail (AC-33107-1).

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (1)

US-7601 T-3 sole-reader-scan probe surfaces every non-facade module that dereferences env.CELL or env.HUB AC1 draft

US-7601 - T-3 sole-reader-scan probe surfaces every non-facade module that dereferences env.CELL or env.HUB

As a: reviewer enforcing the sole-reader guarantee on env.CELL and env.HUB

I want: the sole-reader-scan probe to walk every .mjs/.js/.ts file under the fixture applied source root and assert only src/do-facade.mjs dereferences env.CELL or env.HUB in live source

So that: a legacy call site or an accidental new one surfaces at self-review, not at runtime

Requirement

REQ-076

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-7601-1 - The sole-reader-scan probe reads every .mjs/.js/.ts file under packages/rcf-lite/test/fixtures/cf-platform/src, strips block and line comments, matches literal env.CELL and env.HUB and reports every non-facade file with a live match as a leak. The clean-fixture scan surfaces zero leaks. Under SIMULATE_NON_FACADE_IMPORT=true a scratch leaker at $TMPDIR/t3-sole-reader-scratch is included in the scan; the scan surfaces the leak and returns fail.

    Given the cf-platform fixture applied source root, and optionally the SIMULATE_NON_FACADE_IMPORT switch

    When the sole-reader-scan probe runs

    Then clean scan returns pass with zero leaks; simulate scan surfaces the injected leaker and returns fail

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-090

REQ-077 T-3 migration-safe class exports: stable class names committed to wrangler with a paired [[migrations]] block platform US1 AC1 draft

T-3 migration-safe class exports: the DO class names are stable strings committed under [[durable_objects.bindings]] blocks in wrangler.toml, and a paired [[migrations]] block records the mint classes under tag "v1" per Cloudflare's migration documentation. A rename ships as a subsequent migrations tag; a rename without one is a runtime error the anatomy assertion catches at self-review (AC-33108-1).

capability:platform-integrations

User stories (1)

US-7701 T-3 wrangler.toml commits stable DO class names on both binding blocks and a migrations tag records the mint classes AC1 draft

US-7701 - T-3 wrangler.toml commits stable DO class names on both binding blocks and a migrations tag records the mint classes

As a: operator applying platform-cloudflare-durable-objects on a fresh Workers project

I want: the generated wrangler.toml to carry [[durable_objects.bindings]] blocks and a paired [[migrations]] block with a stable tag

So that: a future rename lands as a wrangler migration rather than a silent rewire and the DO class identity survives the mint

Requirement

REQ-077

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-7701-1 - The fixture wrangler.toml carries at least two [[durable_objects.bindings]] blocks (one binding named CELL with class_name SingleCellObject; one binding named HUB with class_name HubObject) and at least one [[migrations]] block with tag "v1" and new_sqlite_classes = ["SingleCellObject", "HubObject"]. The anatomy assertion greps the toml for each literal string and the migrations pair.

    Given the cf-platform fixture wrangler.toml

    When the anatomy assertion greps for the four literal strings and the migrations pair (new_sqlite_classes plus the two class names)

    Then every string is present and the migrations tag "v1" carries the two class names

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-090

REQ-080 T-4 edge-cloudflare-access v1.0.0 blueprint: the Access JWT validator is the sole reader of the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header and reduces principal onto request.auth functional US3 AC3 approved

The applying Workers project reaches Cloudflare Access through a single JWT validator module (src/jwt-validator.mjs) that is the ONLY module dereferencing the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header. The validator fetches the JWKS from the elicited endpoint, caches keys per-kid, verifies the JWT and reduces the principal into request.auth as {email, sub, groups}. Chain: HQ round-6 T-4 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07 (REQ-080..089 / US-80xx..89xx / TS-110..119 / FBS-100..109 / CN-320..349).

capability:edge-security

User stories (3)

US-8001 T-4 JWT validator: fixture-signed JWT validates and principal reduces onto request.auth AC1 draft

US-8001 - T-4 JWT validator: fixture-signed JWT validates and principal reduces onto request.auth

As a: shelf consumer applying the edge-cloudflare-access v1.0.0 blueprint on a Workers project using the cf-edge fixture

I want: the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header validated against the Access JWKS on every request, the principal reduced into request.auth as {email, sub, groups} and the downstream handler observes 200 with the reduced principal fields

So that: the Worker only ever sees authenticated principals and downstream code reads a single stable seam for identity

Requirement

REQ-080

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-8001-1 - The JWT validator reads Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion, verifies against the fixture JWKS (RS256, kid rotation supported by cache), reduces the principal into request.auth as {email, sub, groups} and the downstream handler receives a 200 with the reduced principal fields exposed on request.auth.

    Given a Worker fetch handler wired with the createAccessValidator middleware and a fixture-signed JWT presented in the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header

    When the request dispatches through the validator

    Then the validator resolves, attaches {email, sub, groups} onto request.auth and delegates to the handler which returns 200 with request.auth reflected on the response body

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-100

US-8002 T-4 JWT validator: missing, expired or mis-signed JWT rejects 401 with metadata-only audit event AC1 draft

US-8002 - T-4 JWT validator: missing, expired or mis-signed JWT rejects 401 with metadata-only audit event

As a: shelf consumer applying the edge-cloudflare-access v1.0.0 blueprint on a Workers project using the cf-edge fixture

I want: requests carrying a missing, expired or mis-signed JWT to reject with 401 and emit exactly one metadata-only audit event on the shipped audit sink

So that: unauthenticated traffic cannot reach the downstream handler and every reject is observable without leaking the token value or headers

Requirement

REQ-080

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-8002-1 - The three reject subcases (missing header, expired exp, mis-signed) each return HTTP 401 and emit exactly one audit event whose keys are drawn from {email, outcome, timestamp, path} with no token substring, no header names beyond path, and no additional keys.

    Given a Worker fetch handler wired with the createAccessValidator middleware and one of the three reject subcases

    When the request dispatches through the validator

    Then the validator resolves 401, emits one audit event with outcome in {missing, expired, invalid} and the record body carries only the four allowed keys

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-100

US-8003 T-4 JWT validator is the sole reader of the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header in the applied source tree AC1 draft

US-8003 - T-4 JWT validator is the sole reader of the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header in the applied source tree

As a: shelf consumer applying the edge-cloudflare-access v1.0.0 blueprint on a Workers project using the cf-edge fixture

I want: only src/jwt-validator.mjs to dereference the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header string in the applied source tree

So that: the validator is the single seam and a stray header read in the applied code is a defect the AST scan catches

Requirement

REQ-080

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-8003-1 - The sole-reader scan walks the fixture applied source root (src/**/*.mjs), strips comments and string literals, and finds exactly one live source occurrence of the header string Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion, in src/jwt-validator.mjs. Any other occurrence in a shipped module fails the probe.

    Given the cf-edge fixture applied source tree

    When the sole-reader-scan probe walks src/**/*.mjs

    Then the only live-source hit for Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion is in src/jwt-validator.mjs; SIMULATE_NON_VALIDATOR_HEADER=true injects a second hit and the probe fails

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-100

REQ-081 T-4 edge-cloudflare-access v1.0.0: an Access application is declared with an elicited hostname or self-hosted-app id and an elicited policy shape from the enum functional US1 AC1 approved

The blueprint elicits either an Access application hostname or a self-hosted-app id, plus the JWT audience, JWKS URL and a policy shape from the enum. Applying the blueprint records the values on rcf/blueprints/edge-cloudflare-access.applied.json.

capability:edge-security

User stories (1)

US-8101 T-4 Access application declared with elicited hostname or self-hosted-app id and elicited policy shape AC1 draft

US-8101 - T-4 Access application declared with elicited hostname or self-hosted-app id and elicited policy shape

As a: operator applying the edge-cloudflare-access v1.0.0 blueprint

I want: the blueprint to elicit either an Access application hostname or a self-hosted-app id, plus a policy shape from the enum

So that: the apply record captures the exact Access application declaration the operator will issue in the Zero Trust dashboard or over the API

Requirement

REQ-081

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-8101-1 - blueprint.json elicits access-application-host (kind string) or access-selfhosted-app-id (kind string, one of the two required at apply), plus access-policy-shape (kind enum, options email-domain, service-token-only, service-token-plus-email-domain, group-membership; recommended default email-domain). Applying the blueprint records the elicited values on rcf/blueprints/edge-cloudflare-access.applied.json.

    Given the blueprint.json elicits block

    When the apply verb runs against a fixture project

    Then rcf/blueprints/edge-cloudflare-access.applied.json carries appliedCapabilities=[zeroTrustGate] and elicited values for access-application-host or access-selfhosted-app-id plus access-policy-shape

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-100

REQ-082

REQ-083 T-4 edge-cloudflare-access v1.0.0: the audit event carries metadata-only fields email, outcome, timestamp and path with no token value or headers functional US1 AC1 approved

Every validate outcome emits one audit event on the injected sink with the metadata-only shape {email, outcome, timestamp, path}. The record is Object.frozen at the boundary; no downstream module can enrich it with a stray token slice.

capability:edge-security

User stories (1)

US-8301 T-4 audit event carries only email, outcome, timestamp and path; no token value or headers on any code path AC1 draft

US-8301 - T-4 audit event carries only email, outcome, timestamp and path; no token value or headers on any code path

As a: shelf consumer applying the edge-cloudflare-access v1.0.0 blueprint on a Workers project using the cf-edge fixture

I want: the audit sink to receive only metadata-only records for every validate-pass and validate-reject

So that: the audit trail is observable without leaking the JWT, its signature bytes or any request header value

Requirement

REQ-083

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-8301-1 - After 5 validate-pass and 5 validate-reject requests the audit sink holds 10 records each carrying exactly {email, outcome, timestamp, path}; the serialised JSON of every record contains no substring of the JWT (header, payload or signature), no Authorization value and no header names beyond path.

    Given the shipped createAccessValidator wired with a spy audit sink and 10 requests (5 pass, 5 reject)

    When the requests dispatch through the validator

    Then 10 sink records, each with allowed keys only, none containing forbidden substrings

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-100

REQ-084 T-4 edge-cloudflare-access v1.0.0: break-glass posture with an elicited bypass-service-auth token pair for CI-signed automation functional US1 AC1 approved

The operator elicits a break-glass service-auth id; the paired secret is delegated to the applied secretsManagement companion. Requests presenting the paired CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret headers authenticate with outcome=bypass.

capability:edge-security

User stories (1)

US-8401 T-4 break-glass posture: an elicited bypass-service-auth token pair signs CI automation requests through the validator AC1 draft

US-8401 - T-4 break-glass posture: an elicited bypass-service-auth token pair signs CI automation requests through the validator

As a: operator running CI-signed automation against an Access-gated Worker

I want: an elicited bypass-service-auth token pair that the validator recognises and passes through as an authenticated principal

So that: CI can hit the gated Worker without a browser flow while every bypass leaves a distinct audit trace

Requirement

REQ-084

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-8401-1 - When the request presents the elicited service-auth id and secret (as CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret headers), the validator observes the pair, records outcome=bypass in the audit event with the same metadata-only shape, and delegates to the handler as authenticated with request.auth.email='service:'+id. Break-glass is disabled unless the elicited pair is applied.

    Given the createAccessValidator wired with an elicited bypass-service-auth pair and a request presenting the paired headers

    When the request dispatches through the validator

    Then the handler receives request.auth with the service principal and the audit sink records outcome=bypass, with allowed keys only

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-100

REQ-085 T-4 edge-cloudflare-access v1.0.0: the composition with application-admin-console flips the sign-in surface when the applied capability set contains zeroTrustGate functional US2 AC2 approved

When application-admin-console v1.1.0 is applied alongside edge-cloudflare-access, the admin-console reads appliedCapabilities via readAppliedCapabilities() at apply-time and flips its sign-in surface between Access-gated and local-login.

capability:edge-security

User stories (2)

US-8501 T-4 admin-console composition: the sign-in surface swaps to Access-gated when zeroTrustGate applied and falls back to security-auth-* otherwise AC1 draft

US-8501 - T-4 admin-console composition: the sign-in surface swaps to Access-gated when zeroTrustGate applied and falls back to security-auth-* otherwise

As a: shelf consumer applying both edge-cloudflare-access and application-admin-console v1.1.0

I want: the admin-console sign-in surface to flip to Access-gated when zeroTrustGate is applied, and to fall back to the local security-auth-* surface otherwise

So that: the composition is deterministic and no local login form leaks into an Access-gated deployment

Requirement

REQ-085

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-8501-1 - Two applied combinations are exercised on the extended admin-console fixture: with ?caps=principalDirectory,roleModel,auditLog,zeroTrustGate the sign-in surface renders [data-surface=access-gated] and no [data-surface=local-login] is present; with ?caps=principalDirectory,roleModel,auditLog the sign-in surface renders [data-surface=local-login] and no [data-surface=access-gated] is present. Both combinations exercise the shipped pack check AC-21815-1.

    Given the admin-console pack fixture with the two caps combinations

    When the pack runs against each combination

    Then AC-21815-1 fires on the gated combination and passes; the existing v1.0.0 surface renders on the non-gated combination and its own check passes

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-100

US-8502 T-4 real-account gated URL: a request against a scheduled Access-configured hostname lands the Access UI AC1 draft

US-8502 - T-4 real-account gated URL: a request against a scheduled Access-configured hostname lands the Access UI

As a: HQ operator running the real-account gated-URL smoke against a scheduled Access-configured hostname

I want: the probe to fire against the hostname when the env vars are present and record accountBoundSkipped when not

So that: the mechanism-reach claim is proven on a real Cloudflare Access instance without ever failing the shelf gate on the absence of an account

REQ-085

Without either env var the probe records accountBoundSkipped=true and aggregateVerdict=pass per spec section 3.5.

    Given the run-real-account-gated-url.mjs probe shim and the two env vars

    When the probe runs

    Then in the CI-with-account path the redirect chain reports cloudflareaccess.com as terminal; in the without-env path accountBoundSkipped is true

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-100

REQ-086 T-4 application-admin-console v1.1.0 minor: consume zeroTrustGate optionally, replacing the local sign-in form with an Access-gated surface when the capability is applied functional US2 AC2 approved

application-admin-console v1.1.0 additive minor: consumes zeroTrustGate optionally, replacing the local sign-in form with an Access-gated surface when the capability is applied. Q4 default: consumption is OPTIONAL; principalDirectory remains the sole hard requirement (making Access-gate hard is a v2.0 change).

capability:edge-security

User stories (2)

US-8601 T-4 admin-console v1.1.0: Access-gated sign-in surface with no local login form and principal reads from request.auth AC1 draft

US-8601 - T-4 admin-console v1.1.0: Access-gated sign-in surface with no local login form and principal reads from request.auth

As a: shelf consumer applying application-admin-console v1.1.0 with zeroTrustGate in the applied capability set

I want: the sign-in surface to render as Access-gated with no local login form and to read the principal from request.auth

So that: the admin console composes with edge-cloudflare-access at the sign-in seam and never re-collects credentials in an Access-gated deployment

Requirement

REQ-086

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-8601-1 - The repo-chain AC for the admin-console v1.1.0 Access-gated sign-in surface. The shipped pack check on application-admin-console.pack.mjs (id AC-21815-1 in the blueprint's own band) asserts that when application-admin-console v1.1.0 is applied with zeroTrustGate in appliedCapabilities, GET /admin/sign-in renders a region with [data-surface=access-gated], no [data-surface=local-login] region is present, and a [data-role=principal-read] element renders the principal email read from request.auth.

    Given the extended admin-console pack fixture on ?caps=principalDirectory,roleModel,auditLog,zeroTrustGate

    When the pack drives GET /admin/sign-in

    Then the DOM carries [data-surface=access-gated], no [data-surface=local-login], and a [data-role=principal-read] with the request.auth email

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-101

REQ-090 T-5 edge-cloudflare-turnstile v1.0.0 blueprint: the Turnstile client widget mounts with an elicited sitekey and injects no third-party script beyond Cloudflare Turnstile JS host functional US2 AC2 draft

The applying project reaches Cloudflare Turnstile through a client widget mount that renders on elicited surfaces using the elicited TURNSTILE_SITEKEY. The mount injects only Cloudflare Turnstile JS (challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js) and no other third-party script. On submit the widget populates a hidden Cf-Turnstile-Response token field in the form payload. Chain: HQ round-6 T-5 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07 (REQ-090..099 / US-90xx..94xx / TS-120..129 / FBS-110..119 / CN-350..379).

capability:edge-security

User stories (2)

US-9001 T-5 widget mount: elicited sitekey renders Turnstile widget with token populated on submit AC1 draft

US-9001 - T-5 widget mount: elicited sitekey renders Turnstile widget with token populated on submit

As a: shelf consumer applying the edge-cloudflare-turnstile v1.0.0 blueprint on a Workers project using the probe-pack-edge-cloudflare-turnstile fixture

I want: the Turnstile widget to mount on my public form with the elicited TURNSTILE_SITEKEY, to inject only Cloudflare Turnstile JS (no other third-party script), and to populate the hidden Cf-Turnstile-Response token field on submit

So that: every submit that reaches my server carries a Turnstile response my server-side verifier can check

Requirement

REQ-090

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-9001-1 - When the fixture page loads with the always-pass test sitekey, the Turnstile widget mounts and an iframe is present whose src origin is https://challenges.cloudflare.com; the page loads no third-party script from any other origin; on submit the form payload carries a non-empty Cf-Turnstile-Response value.

    Given the pack fixture form loaded with default sitekey pass and the pinned always-pass test sitekey

    When the widget renders and the operator submits

    Then the Turnstile widget is mounted, its iframe origin is Cloudflare Turnstile only, and the submit payload contains the Cf-Turnstile-Response token

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-110

US-9002 T-5 secret shape: TURNSTILE_SECRET is read only via the applied secrets facade and never inlined in fixture source AC1 draft

REQ-091 T-5 edge-cloudflare-turnstile v1.0.0: server-side siteverify POSTs the response token to challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify with the elicited secret functional US2 AC2 draft

The applying project verifies every Turnstile response token server-side by POSTing {secret: TURNSTILE_SECRET, response: <token>} to https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify per Cloudflare Turnstile documented endpoint. On success:true the handler proceeds; on success:false the handler rejects with 400 and the refusal body carries the error-codes[] value, not the sitekey or secret.

capability:edge-security

User stories (2)

US-9101 T-5 server-side siteverify pass: the always-pass Turnstile secret returns success:true and the handler proceeds with 200 AC1 draft

US-9101 - T-5 server-side siteverify pass: the always-pass Turnstile secret returns success:true and the handler proceeds with 200

As a: shelf consumer whose Worker verifies Turnstile tokens through the shipped verifier

I want: a POST to challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify with the pinned always-pass secret and any response token to return success true and my handler to respond 200

So that: the Turnstile-verified path is exercised end-to-end against the real Cloudflare endpoint

Requirement

REQ-091

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-9101-1 - A live POST to https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify with secret=1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA and any response token returns success:true; the pack-fixture /api/submit handler proceeds with 200. The Node siteverify-fixture probe drives the live endpoint and asserts success:true.

    Given the pack fixture running on 127.0.0.1 with the pinned always-pass secret in the environment

    When a form submit hits /api/submit carrying the always-pass response token

    Then the server-side POST to Cloudflare returns success:true and the handler responds 200

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-110

    When a form submit hits /api/submit and the verifier calls siteverify

    Then siteverify returns success:false, the handler responds 400 with an error-codes body, and every event record carries only sitekeyHash, outcome and timestamp

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-110

REQ-092 T-5 edge-cloudflare-turnstile v1.0.0: refuse-if-token-missing guard on elicited surfaces rejects submit with 400 before any downstream logic functional US1 AC1 draft

The applying project registers a token-required guard at every elicited surface. A submit whose payload lacks the Cf-Turnstile-Response field is rejected with 400 before any downstream handler runs. The refusal body carries a stable error-code, not the sitekey.

capability:edge-security

User stories (1)

US-9201 T-5 refuse-if-token-missing guard: a submit without Cf-Turnstile-Response rejects with 400 before any downstream logic AC1 draft

US-9201 - T-5 refuse-if-token-missing guard: a submit without Cf-Turnstile-Response rejects with 400 before any downstream logic

As a: shelf consumer whose Worker refuses cheap submit-without-token attempts at the earliest possible boundary

I want: the guard to reject every submit whose payload has no Cf-Turnstile-Response field with 400 before the downstream handler is entered

So that: downstream handlers never execute against a missing-token submit

Requirement

REQ-092

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-9201-1 - A source-tree scan of the pack fixture (guard-shape-scan) enumerates every elicited surface and asserts each carries a token-required guard registered at the route level. A live POST to /api/submit without a Cf-Turnstile-Response field is rejected with 400 and no downstream handler side-effect is observable. Refusal body carries a stable error-code, not the sitekey.

    Given the pack fixture running with every elicited surface registered

    When a submit reaches the route without a Cf-Turnstile-Response value

    Then the guard rejects with 400 with an error-code body and no downstream handler runs

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-110

REQ-093 T-5 edge-cloudflare-turnstile v1.0.0: composition with security-auth-magic-link refuses magic-link mint without a valid Turnstile token functional US2 AC2 draft

When both security-auth-magic-link and edge-cloudflare-turnstile are applied, the magic-link mint surface reads through the Turnstile guard: a mint submit without a valid Turnstile response is refused with 400 before the mint fires. Composition uses the TAC-3603 hook on the shipped magic-link mint surface.

capability:edge-security

User stories (2)

US-9301 T-5 composition with security-auth-magic-link: the magic-link mint surface reads through the Turnstile guard AC1 draft

US-9301 - T-5 composition with security-auth-magic-link: the magic-link mint surface reads through the Turnstile guard

As a: shelf consumer applying both security-auth-magic-link and edge-cloudflare-turnstile

I want: the magic-link mint surface to be gated by the Turnstile guard so a mint submit reads through the same token check as any other elicited surface

So that: magic-link mint requests are protected by the same human-check as any other public form on my project

Requirement

REQ-093

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-9301-1 - The blueprint contribution ADR-3601 declares the composition contract on the humanVerificationGate topic; the pack fixture ships a magic-link mint stub route (/api/magic-link) registered with the Turnstile guard. A source-tree read of the composition wire confirms the mint surface calls through the Turnstile guard before invoking the magic-link mint.

    Given the pack fixture with both blueprints applied and /api/magic-link registered with the token-required guard

    When the composition contract is walked in the source tree

    Then the magic-link mint surface reads the Turnstile token check before invoking the mint

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-110

US-9302 T-5 magic-link guard cross-cutting: a magic-link mint submit without a valid Turnstile token is refused with 400 before the mint fires AC1 draft

US-9302 - T-5 magic-link guard cross-cutting: a magic-link mint submit without a valid Turnstile token is refused with 400 before the mint fires

As a: shelf consumer relying on the composition to gate magic-link mint attempts

I want: a magic-link mint POST that carries no Turnstile response, or a mint POST whose Turnstile response fails siteverify, to be refused with 400 before the mint fires

So that: no magic-link is minted for a submitter who did not complete a Turnstile challenge

Requirement

REQ-093

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-9302-1 - A live POST to /api/magic-link on the pack fixture without a Cf-Turnstile-Response field, and a POST carrying the always-fail response token, are both refused with 400 by the Turnstile guard and no magic-link is minted. The Playwright pack check AC-turnstile-magicLinkGuard drives this against the fixture with a real browser.

    Given the pack fixture running with both blueprints applied and a real Playwright browser driving the fixture

    When a magic-link mint submit is issued without a Turnstile response, or with the always-fail response token

    Then the Turnstile guard refuses with 400 and no magic-link mint side-effect is observable

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-110

REQ-094 T-5 edge-cloudflare-turnstile v1.0.0: widget mode is an elicited enum (managed, non-interactive, invisible) per Cloudflare documented modes; recommendedDefault is managed functional US1 AC1 draft

The applying operator elicits one of Cloudflare Turnstile documented widget modes: managed (default; renders challenge only when Cloudflare deems it necessary), non-interactive (always renders a non-interactive challenge) or invisible (mounts an invisible widget). The default mode is managed per the shipped ADR.

capability:edge-security

User stories (1)

US-9401 T-5 widget mode elicit: managed, non-interactive and invisible each render per Cloudflare documented widget modes and the elicited default is managed AC1 draft

US-9401 - T-5 widget mode elicit: managed, non-interactive and invisible each render per Cloudflare documented widget modes and the elicited default is managed

As a: shelf consumer selecting a Turnstile widget mode for my project

I want: to elicit one of managed, non-interactive or invisible at apply time with managed as the recommendedDefault, and to see each mode render as Cloudflare documents

So that: my applied surface matches the operational profile the site needs (interactive challenge, always non-interactive, or invisible background check)

Requirement

REQ-094

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-9401-1 - The blueprint elicit widget-mode contributes an enum with values managed, non-interactive and invisible; recommendedDefault managed. The pack fixture accepts ?mode=<managed|non-interactive|invisible> and mounts the widget with the pinned test sitekeys that match Cloudflare documented mode variants (sitekey 1x0000000000000000000000AA for interactive-pass, 1x0000000000000000000000BB for invisible-pass). Each mode renders the Turnstile iframe from challenges.cloudflare.com and no third-party origin.

    Given the pack fixture loaded with mode set to managed, non-interactive and invisible respectively

    When each variant renders

    Then each renders the Turnstile widget from Cloudflare Turnstile origin only and no third-party script is loaded

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-110

REQ-100 T-6 edge-cloudflare-rate-limiting v1.0.0 blueprint: rate-limit rule manifest committed under cloudflare/rate-limits/, one JSON file per rule, matching the elicited rule shape without plaintext secrets functional US3 AC3 draft

The applying project holds its rate-limit rule set as a set of JSON documents under the elicited rate-limit-rules-dir (default cloudflare/rate-limits/), one file per rule per ADR-3703. Every manifest file declares the seven documented fields the Cloudflare WAF rate-limiting rules contract names per https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/rate-limiting-rules/: id, expression, threshold, period, characteristics, action, duration. The zone id is elicited and stored via secretsManagement; no rule references a secret in plaintext. Chain: HQ round-6 T-6 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07 (REQ-100..109 / TS-130..139 / FBS-120..129 / CN-380..409). Round-6 T-6 track of Cloudflare-round-6-spec-2026-09-06 section 5.6.

capability:edge-security

User stories (3)

US-10001 T-6 rate-limit manifest present in cf-edge cloudflare/rate-limits/ carrying seven required fields without plaintext secrets AC1 draft

US-10001 - T-6 rate-limit manifest present in cf-edge cloudflare/rate-limits/ carrying seven required fields without plaintext secrets

I want: the elicited manifest directory to hold at least one committed JSON file per rate-limit rule, each carrying the seven documented fields and no plaintext secret

So that: the rules are source-controlled and reviewable and the operator has a stable source of truth to apply to the live zone

Requirement

REQ-100

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-10001-1 - The cf-edge fixture's cloudflare/rate-limits/ directory holds at least one JSON file per rule; every file parses; every file carries id, expression, threshold, period, characteristics, action, duration; no file body carries a plaintext bearer token, private key or inline CF_API_TOKEN reference.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-120

REQ-102 T-6 edge-cloudflare-rate-limiting v1.0.0 blueprint: over-threshold behaviour returns 429 with Retry-After and Cf-Ray for the (N+1)th and subsequent requests within the elicited duration functional US1 AC1 draft

Given a rule that permits N requests per period on a characteristic set, when a client sends the (N+1)th request within that period, Cloudflare refuses the request at the edge for the elicited duration. The refusal response is HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header consistent with the elicited duration and a Cf-Ray header identifying the CF edge per https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/rate-limiting-rules/. The origin Worker never sees the refused requests. Chain: HQ round-6 T-6 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07.

capability:edge-security

User stories (1)

US-10201 T-6 real-account burst returns 429 with Retry-After and Cf-Ray on over-threshold requests, or accountBoundSkipped in CI per ruling 6 AC1 draft

US-10201 - T-6 real-account burst returns 429 with Retry-After and Cf-Ray on over-threshold requests, or accountBoundSkipped in CI per ruling 6

As a: operator running the real-account burst probe against a scheduled HQ-owned URL

I want: the probe to fire an undici burst above the rule threshold and observe the (N+1)th and subsequent requests return HTTP 429 with Retry-After and Cf-Ray, or record accountBoundSkipped in CI

So that: the over-threshold behaviour is verified against a real Cloudflare account when the account is available, and CI without an account records the honest verdict per ruling 6

Requirement

REQ-102

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-10201-1 - With CI_HAS_CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT=true and CF_RATE_LIMIT_URL set, the burst probe returns 429 with Retry-After and Cf-Ray on over-threshold requests; without either env var it records accountBoundSkipped: true and aggregates to pass per spec section 3.5 and ruling 6.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-120

REQ-103 T-6 edge-cloudflare-rate-limiting v1.0.0 blueprint: drift-audit runner reads live zone rules via the Cloudflare API and diffs against the local manifest, constructing metadata-only records functional US2 AC2 draft

The blueprint ships a scheduled drift-audit runner (TAC-3703) the applying project can wire behind the elicited rate-limit-drift-audit-cadence per ADR-3704. When enabled, the runner fetches the live rate-limiting rules on the elicited zone via the Cloudflare API, diffs against the local manifest, and constructs one drift-audit record per mismatched rule. Records write through the applied logger with the metadata-only shape {ruleId, clientIpHash, outcome, timestamp, diff}; no record carries a full IP, a request body or a user agent. Chain: HQ round-6 T-6 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07.

capability:edge-security

User stories (2)

US-10301 T-6 drift-audit runner reads live rules and diffs against manifest, constructing metadata-only drift records AC1 draft

US-10301 - T-6 drift-audit runner reads live rules and diffs against manifest, constructing metadata-only drift records

As a: operator on the applying project running the scheduled drift-audit runner behind the elicited cadence

I want: the runner to fetch the live rules via the Cloudflare API and diff each against the local manifest, constructing metadata-only drift records

So that: manifest drift is surfaced through the logging companion rather than lingering unnoticed

Requirement

REQ-103

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-10301-1 - Given a fixture manifest with threshold 60 and a fake live-zone response with threshold 90 on the same rule id, the runner constructs one drift record with {ruleId, clientIpHash, outcome, timestamp, diff:[{field:threshold, manifestValue:60, liveValue:90}]}; no full IP, body or user-agent field is present.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-120

REQ-104 T-6 edge-cloudflare-rate-limiting v1.0.0 blueprint: composition with security-auth-magic-link layers the zone rule over the per-email application rule per ADR-3702 functional US1 AC1 draft

When both edge-cloudflare-rate-limiting and security-auth-magic-link are applied on the same project, the zone-level rate rule sits at the CF edge and refuses the (N+1)th request for the elicited duration before it reaches the origin; the security-auth-magic-link per-email application rate limiter continues to run at the mint-surface. The two rules operate on different characteristic sets (IP-per-URL vs per-email per-minute) and are additive. ADR-3702 records the layering. Chain: HQ round-6 T-6 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07.

capability:edge-security

User stories (1)

US-10401 T-6 composition with security-auth-magic-link: zone rule layers over the per-email application rule per ADR-3702, documented in the guide AC1 draft

As a: operator applying both edge-cloudflare-rate-limiting and security-auth-magic-link on the same project

I want: the guide to name the ADR-3702 layering explicitly with a copy-paste example

So that: I understand the two-rule shape at apply time rather than by trial and error

Requirement

REQ-104

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-10401-1 - The guide contains a Composition with security-auth-magic-link section referencing ADR-3702, naming the two characteristic sets (IP-per-URL and per-email per-minute) verbatim, and showing a copy-paste example of both blueprints applied.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-120

REQ-110 T-1 deploy-hetzner-server v1.0.0 blueprint: provisioner is sole reader of the Hetzner API token, opens on boot, fires provisionerReady event with metadata-only payload functional US1 AC1 draft

The provisioner module wraps the hcloud CLI verbs (or the raw Hetzner Cloud API when provisioningTool=raw-api) and is the sole reader of the Hetzner API token via security-secrets-management. It opens on the applying project's boot path and emits a provisionerReady lifecycle event with metadata-only fields (tool, apiHost, sha of the shim). Chain: HQ round-7 T-1 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07 (REQ-110..119 / TS-140..149 / FBS-130..139 / CN-410..439). Round-7 T-1 track of hetzner-round-7-spec-2026-09-07 section 5.1.

capability:deploy

User stories (1)

US-11001 T-1 provisioner opens on boot with sole HETZNER_ACCOUNT_API_KEY reader and emits provisionerReady with metadata-only payload AC1 draft

US-11001 - T-1 provisioner opens on boot with sole HETZNER_ACCOUNT_API_KEY reader and emits provisionerReady with metadata-only payload

As a: shelf consumer applying the deploy-hetzner-server v1.0.0 blueprint on a Node project that provisions a Hetzner Cloud VM

I want: the provisioner facade to be the sole reader of the Hetzner API token (via security-secrets-management) and to fire provisionerReady with a metadata-only payload when it opens on boot

So that: the applying project has one auditable seam for the token and the observability sink surfaces the ready event without a secret

Requirement

REQ-110

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-11001-1 - On boot of the shared throwaway-Hetzner-server fixture the provisioner facade opens, and (a) only the provisioner module reads HETZNER_ACCOUNT_API_KEY (grep across the fixture source refuses any other reader), (b) the facade emits a provisionerReady event whose payload carries tool and apiHost only (no token, no ssh key, no user data body).

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-130

REQ-111 T-1 deploy-hetzner-server v1.0.0 blueprint: server manifest schema at hetzner/servers/*.json applies to a live Hetzner Cloud server functional US2 AC2 draft

The applying project holds its server declarations as JSON documents under hetzner/servers/<name>.json, one file per server, matching a shipped JSON Schema that names type, location, image, ssh-key ids, firewall id, network id, cloud-init user-data path and labels. Applying the provisioner reads each manifest and creates a matching live server; the hetznerServerProvisioned event carries id, primary IPv4, location and server-type. Chain: HQ round-7 T-1 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07. Round-7 T-1 track of hetzner-round-7-spec-2026-09-07 section 5.1.

capability:deploy

REQ-112 T-1 deploy-hetzner-server v1.0.0 blueprint: cloud-init hardening baseline lands the six documented lines on the provisioned server functional US2 AC2 draft

The cloud-init template shipped with the blueprint renders YAML that lands SSH key-only, root disabled, UFW default-deny incoming, DOCKER-USER iptables chain, fail2ban SSH jail and unattended-upgrades on every provisioned Hetzner server. A local render lint asserts the six baseline blocks are present in the rendered YAML before any provision runs. Chain: HQ round-7 T-1 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07. Round-7 T-1 track of hetzner-round-7-spec-2026-09-07 section 5.1.

capability:deploy

User stories (2)

US-11201 T-1 cloud-init template lands the six hardening baseline blocks in the rendered YAML for every provisioned server AC1 draft

US-11201 - T-1 cloud-init template lands the six hardening baseline blocks in the rendered YAML for every provisioned server

As a: shelf consumer applying the deploy-hetzner-server v1.0.0 blueprint

I want: the shipped cloud-init template to render YAML that lands SSH key-only, root disabled, UFW default-deny incoming, DOCKER-USER iptables chain, fail2ban SSH jail and unattended-upgrades on every server

So that: the operator inherits the six-block hardening baseline without hand-authoring per host

Requirement

REQ-112

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-11201-1 - cloud-init-render-lint.mjs renders the template with the fixture manifest and asserts each of the six baseline blocks (SSH key-only, root disabled, UFW default-deny incoming, DOCKER-USER iptables chain, fail2ban SSH jail, unattended-upgrades) appears in the rendered YAML by grep; a mutation SIMULATE_HARDENING_DRIFT=true removes the unattended-upgrades block and the probe FAILS with a message naming the missing line.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-130

REQ-113 T-1 deploy-hetzner-server v1.0.0 blueprint: firewall shape restricts SSH to operator-nominated prefixes, permits 80/443, denies all else functional US1 AC1 draft

The firewall rule set lives inside the server manifest and is applied to the server at provision time. Rules: 22 permitted only from an operator-nominated set of source-prefix ranges; 80/443 permitted from anywhere for the reverse proxy; all other inbound traffic denied. Manifest schema validation refuses on a rule set that opens 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 or drops the 80/443 rules. Chain: HQ round-7 T-1 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07. Round-7 T-1 track of hetzner-round-7-spec-2026-09-07 section 5.1.

capability:deploy

User stories (1)

US-11301 T-1 firewall rule shape: 22 from operator-nominated prefixes, 80 and 443 open, all other inbound denied, applied at provision time AC1 draft

US-11301 - T-1 firewall rule shape: 22 from operator-nominated prefixes, 80 and 443 open, all other inbound denied, applied at provision time

As a: shelf consumer applying the deploy-hetzner-server v1.0.0 blueprint

I want: the firewall rule set carried in hetzner/servers/name.json to permit 22 only from an operator-nominated set of source-prefix ranges, permit 80 and 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 for the reverse proxy, and deny all other inbound; the provisioner applies the rules at provision time

So that: the operator inherits a documented least-privilege firewall shape on every server without opening ssh to the world

Requirement

REQ-113

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-11301-1 - manifest-schema-validate.mjs asserts every fixture manifest carries a firewall rule set matching the shape (22 permitted only from a nonempty list of source-prefix ranges; 80 and 443 permitted; no other inbound rule); an induced defect (a manifest that opens 22 to 0.0.0.0/0) fails schema validation with a message naming the offending rule.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-130

REQ-114 T-1 deploy-hetzner-server v1.0.0 blueprint: snapshot cadence elicited (weekly default, daily and off alternatives), snapshot-on-demand fires a tagged snapshot functional US2 AC2 draft

The applying project elicits a snapshot cadence per ADR-3802 (default weekly, alternatives daily and off). When non-off, the scheduled snapshot runner fires the hcloud snapshot verb and tags the snapshot with server name and wall-clock time; a snapshot-on-demand verb fires the same shape. The hetznerSnapshotTaken event carries snapshot id and wall-clock time. Chain: HQ round-7 T-1 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07. Round-7 T-1 track of hetzner-round-7-spec-2026-09-07 section 5.1.

capability:deploy

User stories (2)

US-11401 T-1 snapshot cadence file present under the manifest set, cadence value elicited (weekly default, daily and off alternatives) matches the schema AC1 draft

US-11401 - T-1 snapshot cadence file present under the manifest set, cadence value elicited (weekly default, daily and off alternatives) matches the schema

As a: shelf consumer applying the deploy-hetzner-server v1.0.0 blueprint

I want: the elicited snapshot cadence value on hetzner/servers/name.json to match the shipped enum (weekly, daily, off), with weekly the recommended default per ADR-3802

So that: the operator has a single project-wide answer for how often each server snapshots

Requirement

REQ-115 T-1 deploy-hetzner-server v1.0.0 blueprint: four lifecycle events fire with metadata-only payloads and no secret leak functional US1 AC1 draft

The provisioner facade emits four lifecycle events: provisionerReady, hetznerServerProvisioned, hetznerSnapshotTaken and hetznerServerDestroyed. Payloads are metadata-only: id, primary IPv4, location, server-type, snapshot id, wall-clock time. An event-secrecy probe asserts no event body carries the API token, an ssh private key, or a plaintext secret; a mutation that leaks a token into an event body FAILS the probe with a defensive-fake finding. Chain: HQ round-7 T-1 reserved-block per HQ chain-block ruling 2026-09-07. Round-7 T-1 track of hetzner-round-7-spec-2026-09-07 section 5.1.

capability:deploy

User stories (1)

US-11501 T-1 four lifecycle events fire with metadata-only payloads, no secret leaks through any event body AC1 draft
