REQ-156 Nothing leaves the machine unredacted functional US1 AC6 draft

Every issue title, body and evidence pointer that would leave the machine is redacted by a deterministic, rule-based pass and the redactions are disclosed to the operator before consent. The stored entry stays raw; only the rendered issue and bundle are redacted. Project root, other absolute paths, emails, non-allowlisted hostnames and URLs, private and link-local IPs, secret-looking strings, operator identity and the git remote of the reporting project are stripped. A body with a residual secret pattern refuses to submit and the offending line is shown to the operator so the agent can rewrite it.

capability:feedback-loop

User stories (1)

US-15601 Operator sees the exact issue text and what was stripped before consenting AC6 draft

US-15601 - Operator sees the exact issue text and what was stripped before consenting

As a: operator being asked to submit findings

I want: rcf feedback preview to print the exact rendered issue title and body, the destination repo and its visibility, and a redaction ledger that lists every rule-triggered replacement so I can see what was stripped

So that: my yes is informed and nothing surprising leaves the machine

Requirement

REQ-156

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-15601-1 - rcf feedback preview renders each pending entry as the title and body that would be filed on GitHub (using src/feedback/render.js templates from section 4.3 of the design), lists the destination repo and its declared visibility (public, private, or unresolved), and prints the redaction ledger as diff-style lines ("- before + after") with the rule name. --json emits the same as a machine-readable object per entry. No network calls. The kv-secret rule (design section 5 rule 5) is driven by the shared SECRET_KEY_VOCABULARY constant exported from src/feedback/redact.js (design amendment R3a) so the first-pass redactor, the residual safeguard pass and the rule-9 URL-credential scanner cover exactly the same open vocabulary of key stems (secret, token, password, passwd, passphrase, pw, pwd, pass, key, apikey/api_key/api-key, privatekey/private_key/private-key, accesskey/access_key/access-key, clientsecret/client_secret/client-secret, bearer, credential/credentials/cred/creds, session, cookie, signature, sig, salt; hash carries a 16+-value length guard); the match is right-bounded at a word edge so `keyword` and `authors` do not fold but `dbpassword` still does. Design amendment R4 (round 5) extends the rule-5 pass so a vocabulary key labelling a value-shape token of 8+ chars with any separator (markdown table pipes, whitespace runs, tabs, hyphens, arrows, HTML numeric entities, or the prose bridges is / was / set to) also folds, with a mixed-classes gate on the value that keeps ordinary prose (`the password is required`, `the password field is required`) intact.

    Given a fixture project with one entry whose body contains an absolute path, an email, a non-allowlisted hostname, a token-shaped string, a private IPv4 (10.0.5.7), an em-dash, an oversize body block, an operator name that matches a seeded rcf/.identity/profile.md ## Name line, AND at least one shortname-key secret (`pw=`), one URL-embedded credential (a Slack webhook path), one markdown-table row with a vocabulary key and a mixed-class value (`| password | Sup3rSecretV@lue!! |`) and one prose bridge (`the password Sup3rSecretV@lue1234 is bad`)

    When the operator runs rcf feedback preview --json

    Then the JSON output carries titleRendered, bodyRendered, destination { repo, visibility }, and ledger[] entries whose rule names include project-root, absolute-path, email, hostname, secret-token, private-ip, operator-identity, size-shape and url-credential; the rendered body contains none of the original secret substrings (including the shortname-key value, the webhook path segment, the markdown-table value and the prose-bridge value), none of the private IP, none of the operator-name tokens, no em-dash, and is at most 8 KB

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-181

  • AC-15601-2 - When a body still matches a rule-5 secret pattern on the second redaction pass, preview marks the entry as "residual secret at line N" and submit refuses that entry. Other pending entries are unaffected. The exact refusing line is shown to the operator so the agent can rewrite the body.

    Given a fixture project with two entries, one containing a token that survives the first pass through obfuscation and one clean

    When the operator runs rcf feedback preview then rcf feedback submit --yes

    Then the tainted entry is shown with the residual-secret line; submit does not send the tainted entry; the clean entry is submitted (or fallbacks to bundle if that path applies); exit code is 3 while any residual-secret entry is still pending

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-181

  • AC-15601-3 - The stored entries.jsonl body is never mutated by preview. A byte-for-byte comparison of entries.jsonl before and after preview is identical; the redaction lives only in the rendered output.

    Given a fixture project with entries whose bodies contain redactable content

    When the operator runs rcf feedback preview repeatedly

    Then a sha-256 of entries.jsonl before and after each preview run matches

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-181

  • AC-15601-4 - After rendering and normalising the fully assembled issue body (and, for the bundle path, each bundle file), a final whole-text residual-secret pass runs findResidualSecrets over the whole text with multiline patterns. Any hit means the entry stays pending (preview marks it refused-residual and submit refuses that entry with exit 3) and no create/comment/bundle-write occurs for it. The safeguard is defence-in-depth: it catches multiline shapes (e.g. an em-dash-delimited PEM block that survives per-field redaction of a slice-2-style body) that a per-line scan could not see. The safeguard shares the SECRET_KEY_VOCABULARY constant with the first-pass redactor and the rule-9 URL-credential scanner (design amendment R3a), so a shortname-key value (`pw=...`, `pwd=...`) or a webhook-path shape (`/services/<token>`, `/api/webhooks/<token>`, `/bot<token>/method`) that reappears after per-field normalisation is caught by the same set the first pass used.

    Given a fixture project with an entry whose body assembles into a rendered issue body containing a shape a per-line residual scan would miss (a multiline PEM block or a token buried inside a longer identifier)

    When the operator runs rcf feedback preview then rcf feedback submit --yes

    Then preview surfaces the residual line and the tainted entry stays pending; submit exits 3 without a create/comment for that entry and without writing a bundle whose text carries the residual shape

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-181

  • AC-15601-5 - The operator-identity substitution (design section 5 rule 6) applies word-boundary and stopword guards so a common noun that happens to appear in the operator's identity name is not folded. A RESERVED_IDENTITY_TOKENS constant, exported from src/feedback/redact.js and defence-in-depth applied at every operator-name token loop, blocks the fold when the whitespace-separated token (case-insensitive) is one of: agent, agents, user, users, operator, operators, admin, admins, root, client, clients, server, servers, service, services, system, systems, name, main, test, code, api, apis, anon, anonymous, human, humans, dev, ops, sre, docs, developer, developers, engineer, engineers, team, teams. Substitution still fires for a real given name (Alice, Smith) even when the full identity string contains a stopword. The URL and prose canon phrase 'the agent files feedback' survives unmodified when the identity contains 'agent'. Rationale: the rcf-lite ecosystem uses 'agent' as a canonical noun (RULE 17, docs paths); operator-identity folds must be driven by real identity values, never by a bare common noun.

    Given a fixture project whose rcf/.identity/profile.md ## Name reads 'The Agent Alice', and a body containing the docs URL 'https://stravica.ai/docs/rcf/how-the-agent-files-feedback', the prose 'when the agent stops the queue', and the personal name 'Alice reviewed this'

    When the redactor runs over the body with the seeded operator identity

    Then the docs URL survives verbatim; the prose 'when the agent stops the queue' survives verbatim; the personal name 'Alice' folds to <operator>; the ledger records an operator-identity row for 'Alice' but no row for 'agent' or 'the'

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-181

  • AC-15601-6 - The rule-4 bare-hostname redactor treats filename tokens carrying a known file extension as NOT hostnames. A candidate hostname match whose trailing dot-label is in a bundled FILE_EXTENSIONS set (initially md, mdx, json, yml, yaml, txt, js, mjs, cjs, ts, tsx, html, css, png, svg, sh, csv, log, lock) is left intact and no ledger row is written for it (design amendment R5d). The negative lookbehind on the hostname regex additionally excludes '-' so that filename fragments embedded in a larger identifier (`Backstory-product-brief.md`) cannot start a match after a hyphen. The extension shortlist is merged at call time from an `extensions` array on src/feedback/redact-allowlist.json alongside the existing `hosts` field, so operators can extend it the same way they extend hosts. Design amendment R5e (added 0.28.3 per HQ 2026-09-22 ruling on Codex P1-5 deferred from PR #242): candidate hostnames whose trailing dot-label is a single letter are also treated as filename fragments, not hostnames. Rationale: single-letter TLDs are not registrable domains in normal prose and folding them yields more false positives (short identifiers, abbreviated references) than legitimate hostname redactions. Design amendment R5f (added 0.28.3, #243): the rule-3 email regex is bounded so it does not consume the git protocol sentinel `git@<host>` inside a URL whose scheme is `git+ssh://`, `ssh://` or `git://`, nor the bare git-remote shape `git@<host>:<owner>/<repo>` (colon followed by a non-space path). Rationale: `git@<host>` is a URI userinfo construct, not an email; folding it destroys evidence pointers copied from git remotes and clone URLs. Real email addresses in surrounding prose still fold. Design amendment R5g (added 0.28.3, #246): when the operator identity Name (rcf/.identity/profile.md ## Name) is empty, whitespace only, or contains only reserved-noun tokens (RESERVED_IDENTITY_TOKENS from AC-15601-5), buildRedactionContext emits a one-line visible warning to stderr naming the file and stating that identity folding is disabled. The warning is emitted once per redaction context build. Folding still skips (per AC-15601-5) but the operator is no longer left thinking their identity is in force.

    Given a fixture project with a body containing the tokens 'Backstory-product-brief.md', 'intake.json', 'report.log', 'foo.example.com', 'foo.example.com/path', 'Backstory-example.com', 'a.b.c', the URL 'git+ssh://git@github.com/owner/repo.git#v1.0.0', the URL 'ssh://git@example.internal/owner/repo.git', the bare git remote 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git', and a prose email 'alice@example.com'; and a rcf/.identity/profile.md whose ## Name line is either absent, whitespace only, or reads 'The Agent Operator' (stopword-only)

    When the redactor runs over the body with the default allowlist

    Then 'Backstory-product-brief.md', 'intake.json' and 'report.log' survive verbatim with no ledger row for a hostname substitution on their basename; 'foo.example.com' folds to <host> via rule 4; 'foo.example.com/path' folds via rule 4 bare-host (the URL rule requires a scheme; the token here has none); 'Backstory-example.com' folds to '<host>' (the trailing label is not in the extension set); 'a.b.c' survives verbatim with no hostname ledger row (single-letter trailing label per R5e); 'git+ssh://git@github.com/owner/repo.git#v1.0.0' survives verbatim - the `git@` sentinel is NOT rewritten by the email rule (R5f) and github.com is on the allowlist; 'ssh://git@example.internal/owner/repo.git' has the `git@` sentinel preserved (R5f stash) and the host `example.internal` folded to '<host>' by the extended URL rule 4 which now matches ssh/git+ssh/git schemes with optional userinfo; 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git' has the `git@` sentinel preserved (R5f) and github.com is on the allowlist so it survives verbatim; 'alice@example.com' in surrounding prose still folds to '<email>' (rule 3 email); and when the identity Name is empty/whitespace/stopword-only, stderr carries exactly one visible warning line naming rcf/.identity/profile.md and stating that identity folding is disabled. Extending the allowlist with `extensions: ["xyz"]` in redact-allowlist.json (or the operator overlay) makes 'file.xyz' also survive.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-181

REQ-157 One finding, one issue functional US1 AC3 draft

The same defect reported by many users folds into one GitHub issue with additional reporters as +1 comments, not into one issue per user. The fingerprint is deterministic from kind, target key, anchor and symptom class; blueprint version is not part of the fingerprint so a defect that persists across versions folds. Search unavailability falls through to create with a dedupe: unchecked stamp; closed issues are not matched (a recurrence is a regression).

capability:feedback-loop

User stories (1)

US-15701 The same finding from many reporters folds into one issue AC3 draft

US-15701 - The same finding from many reporters folds into one issue

As a: blueprint maintainer receiving reports

I want: ten reporters hitting the same defect on the same anchor to land as one issue with nine +1 comments carrying their environments, not ten separate issues

So that: triage is cheap and duplicate storms do not swamp the tracker

Requirement

REQ-157

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-15701-1 - fingerprint(entry) returns the first 12 hex chars of sha-256 over "<kind>|<targetKey>|<anchor>|<symptomClass>" where targetKey is the effective slug for blueprints (no version) or the verb path for core, anchor is upper-cased or "-" when absent, and symptomClass is one of the closed enum. Same fingerprint across two entries whose blueprint versions differ; different fingerprint when the anchor or class differs.

    Given a fixture corpus of five entries: same-defect different-version, same-defect different-anchor, same-defect different-class, missing-anchor pair (title-only fallback), and one clean

    When fingerprint() is called on each entry

    Then the versioned pair yields identical fingerprints; the anchor and class variants yield different fingerprints; the missing-anchor pair uses the "<kind>|<targetKey>|<symptomClass>|<normalisedTitle>" fallback (first eight tokens, punctuation and stop-words stripped, lower-case)

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-181

  • AC-15701-2 - On submit, per pending entry, gh search issues is called for the destination repo with query "rcf-feedback-fingerprint: <fp>", --match body, --state open, --limit 5. For every returned candidate, submit re-reads the candidate issue body via gh issue view --json body (ghIssueGetBody) and folds ONLY if the body contains a line exactly matching "rcf-feedback-fingerprint: <fp>" on its own; a search hit whose body does not carry that exact line is a NON-MATCH and is discarded. Anchor and target must also match the entry's anchor and target; folding across a differing anchor or target is refused even when the fingerprint lines are equal. Zero verified hits: gh issue create; the stdout row reports "created #N (<title>)". One or more verified hits: gh issue comment on the lowest-numbered verified issue, mention any other verified hits in the comment body, and post the FULL rendered report (title as a "## Report" heading, then the redacted body, then evidence and environment tables, then the fingerprint line), labelled as "Apparent duplicate of the issue subject; posting the full report so a human can judge." The retired "+1 from another reporter." payload is never posted. The stdout row on the fold path reports "commented on #N (fingerprint match: <title>)" so a wrong match is visible on the same line a human already sees.

    Given a fake gh module (via RCF_FEEDBACK_GH_MODULE) whose ghIssueSearch stub yields zero, one and two hits in three sequential invocations, and one pending entry per case; and a second fixture where ghIssueSearch returns a candidate whose ghIssueGetBody body carries a DIFFERENT fingerprint line to the entry; and a third fixture where the candidate body's fingerprint matches but the candidate's anchor or target field differs from the entry's

    When rcf feedback submit --yes runs against each fixture

    Then the zero-hit case creates and prints "created #N (<title>)"; the one-hit case with a verified fingerprint match comments on the returned number, the comment body carries the full rendered report (title + body + evidence + environment + fingerprint), the string "+1 from another reporter." is absent, and the stdout row prints "commented on #N (fingerprint match: <title>)"; the two-hit case comments on the smaller number and mentions the other verified number; the different-fingerprint fixture and the differing-anchor/target fixture both fall through to create rather than comment

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

  • AC-15701-3 - When gh search issues is unavailable or errors (rate-limit, GHES search off, non-zero exit), submit falls through to gh issue create for that entry and the state line stamps dedupe: unchecked. Closed issues are never matched; if --state closed search finds an issue with the same fingerprint the created new issue body carries "previously reported and closed as #<n>".

    Given a fake gh module whose search stub throws for one call and returns a closed match for the next

    When rcf feedback submit --yes runs twice with one pending entry each

    Then the first entry is created with dedupe: unchecked in state; the second is created with a body reference to the previously closed issue number

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

REQ-158 Reports reach the owning repo functional US2 AC6 draft

A finding is filed on the repo that owns the code the finding is about: Stravica/rcf-lite for shelf blueprints and core, and the library-declared repo for library blueprints. Library owners declare their destination via an optional issues field on library.json; the consuming project does not guess. Applied blueprints without a declared destination fall back to derivation from the library git source when unambiguous, else route to the outbox and name the library publisher contact. Doctor lists any registered library missing a destination as a warn-only finding.

capability:feedback-loop

User stories (2)

US-15801 Library owner declares where feedback issues go AC4 draft

US-15801 - Library owner declares where feedback issues go

As a: library owner shipping a blueprint library

I want: to name the reports destination in one field on library.json, snapshotted into the consuming project registry on library add, so every project using my library files reports on my repo

So that: I hear about defects on my library without every consuming project having to be told separately

Requirement

REQ-158

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-15801-1 - library.json accepts an optional issues object with { repo: "OWNER/REPO" (host-qualified HOST/OWNER/REPO permitted for GHES), visibility: "public" | "private" }. Absence is valid; the presence-with-shape is schema-checked (documented in docs/library-authoring.md field table). On rcf library add the value is snapshotted onto the registry entry as issuesRepo and issuesVisibility, alongside publisher. rcf library refresh re-snapshots.

    Given a fixture library.json with { issues: { repo: "wsd-team-dev/rcf-lite-blueprints", visibility: "private" } }

    When rcf library add is run against the fixture

    Then rcf/blueprint-libraries.json:entries[] for the library carries issuesRepo and issuesVisibility with the exact values; the review-on-add card prints "Feedback destination: wsd-team-dev/rcf-lite-blueprints (private)"

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-182

  • AC-15801-2 - The destination resolver (src/feedback/destination.js) walks: entry.target -> rcf/manifest.json:blueprints[] -> if libraryPrefix present, the registry entry issuesRepo; absent on the entry, derives from the library sourceRef when it parses as git+https://github.com/OWNER/REPO(.git)#ref (marked derived: true); otherwise unresolved. Shelf blueprints (no libraryPrefix) and --kind core route to a constant read from package.json:bugs.url (Stravica/rcf-lite).

    Given a fixture with three applied blueprints: one shelf, one library with explicit issues, one library with a github git source and no issues

    When destination.resolve() is called for each

    Then the shelf entry resolves to Stravica/rcf-lite; the explicit-issues library resolves to its declared repo, derived false; the git-source library resolves to the OWNER/REPO parsed from the URL, derived true; a fourth library with no issues and no github source is returned as unresolved

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-182

  • AC-15801-3 - rcf doctor gains a warn-only check feedback-destinations that lists every registered library without a resolvable destination (no issues field and no derivable git source) and every applied blueprint whose destination the resolver returns unresolved. --fix does not touch destinations; the fix is for the library owner or the consuming operator.

    Given a fixture with two registered libraries: one with issues, one with neither issues nor a github source

    When rcf doctor is run

    Then doctor output carries one feedback-destinations warn row naming the second library, --fix is not offered on that row, exit code stays 0

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-182

  • AC-15801-4 - The destination resolver cross-checks the registry BEFORE falling through to the shelf constant for `--kind blueprint` entries whose manifest record has no `libraryPrefix`. If exactly one registered library owns a blueprint with the applied slug AND that library resolves to a destination (issuesRepo, or a derivable git+https://github.com/... sourceRef), the resolver returns that library's destination with source: 'library-slug-inference' (derived: false for the declared case, derived: true for the sourceRef case). Two-or-more matches return unresolved with reason: 'ambiguous-library-slug' and a candidates[] array of library prefixes. Zero matches keep the current shelf-constant fall-through. This never overrides an existing libraryPrefix resolution: it only fires where the resolver would have picked the shelf constant.

    Given a fixture with three registered libraries and a bare-slug manifest record for 'application-spa'; case A: only library 'wsd' owns application-spa and declares issuesRepo 'wsd-team-dev/rcf-lite-blueprints'; case B: libraries 'wsd' and 'ally' both own application-spa and both declare issuesRepo; case C: no registered library owns application-spa

    When destination.resolve() is called for each case

    Then case A resolves to 'wsd-team-dev/rcf-lite-blueprints' with source 'library-slug-inference' and derived false; case B resolves to unresolved with reason 'ambiguous-library-slug' and candidates ['ally','wsd']; case C resolves to Stravica/rcf-lite (shelf-constant fall-through), unchanged from AC-15801-2 shelf behaviour

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-182

US-15802 Findings on shelf blueprints and on rcf-lite itself go to rcf-lite AC2 draft

US-15802 - Findings on shelf blueprints and on rcf-lite itself go to rcf-lite

As a: operator whose agent has logged a finding on a shelf blueprint or on rcf-lite core

I want: those findings routed to Stravica/rcf-lite by default without any per-project configuration

So that: reports about shelf content and core verbs reach the maintainers who own them

Requirement

REQ-158

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-15802-1 - A pending entry with kind blueprint and a target that resolves in the manifest without a libraryPrefix (a shelf blueprint) has destination.repo Stravica/rcf-lite on preview and submit. The constant is sourced from packages/rcf-lite/package.json:bugs.url so a rename ripples through one file. A test pins the constant to the current package.json value.

    Given a fixture project applying application-forms-wizard (shelf blueprint) with one pending entry

    When rcf feedback preview is run

    Then the rendered destination row is "Stravica/rcf-lite (public)"; a unit test asserts the constant equals bugs.url from package.json

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-182

  • AC-15802-2 - A pending entry with kind core (target is a verb path like "define validate" or "docs") has destination.repo Stravica/rcf-lite regardless of any library manifest content; the entry cannot be routed to a library repo even if a library declares the verb name as a target.

    Given a fixture with a library declaring "define validate" as a target and one pending core entry

    When rcf feedback preview is run

    Then the destination.repo is Stravica/rcf-lite for the core entry; the library declaration is ignored for kind core; a warning is not emitted (this is by design)

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-182

REQ-159 Consent-gated submission under the reporter identity functional US2 AC6 draft

Nothing is submitted without an explicit yes. When yes is given, issues are filed under the operator own GitHub login via the ambient gh CLI; the tool never asks for or stores a token, never calls the network for authentication, and never speaks for anyone but the operator. Labels are requested best-effort and per-repo label discovery drops names the destination does not carry; the title prefix and body fingerprint stay load-bearing for triage. Submit refuses without --yes unless a TTY operator confirms.

capability:feedback-loop

User stories (2)

US-15901 Operator yes files issues under the reporter GitHub login AC2 draft

US-15901 - Operator yes files issues under the reporter GitHub login

As a: operator saying yes to the ask

I want: the tool to call gh under my ambient login and file each pending entry as a GitHub issue or +1 comment, mark each entry submitted with the URL, and print the URLs so the agent can relay them

So that: reports are visibly mine, with no relay in between and no token handling in the tool

Requirement

REQ-159

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-15901-1 - rcf feedback submit --yes runs section-7 preflight, section-6 dedupe search, then gh issue create or gh issue comment per entry (through src/feedback/gh.js, or its RCF_FEEDBACK_GH_MODULE stand-in). Each entry state line records status submitted with issueUrl and dedupe (new|comment|unchecked). Stdout prints one line per entry: "<id> -> <url> (<dedupe>)". Exit 0 when every entry ended submitted or bundled; exit 3 when any entry stayed pending (residual secret).

    Given a fixture project with two pending entries and a fake gh module whose create returns an issue URL and whose search returns zero hits

    When the operator runs rcf feedback submit --yes

    Then both entries fold to status submitted with the returned URL and dedupe new; stdout carries two "<id> -> <url> (new)" lines; entries.jsonl is not rewritten (only appended)

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

  • AC-15901-2 - rcf feedback submit without --yes refuses on a non-TTY (exit 2, stderr names the --yes requirement); on a TTY it prompts once and only proceeds on a y answer. The tool never reads GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN itself, never asks for a token, and never spawns gh auth login. A test asserts the process env passed to gh is a copy without any TOKEN mutation.

    Given a fixture project with one pending entry, run under a non-TTY child process

    When rcf feedback submit is run without --yes

    Then exit code 2, stderr names --yes as required; no gh invocation is made; process.env passed through to the fake gh has no synthesised TOKEN key

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

US-15902 Labels are applied where the reporter may set them AC4 draft

US-15902 - Labels are applied where the reporter may set them

As a: maintainer triaging inbound issues

I want: rcf-feedback plus severity:<...> plus area:<...> labels applied by the tool when the destination repo carries them and the reporter has push or triage access

So that: triage queues sort correctly for reporters who have the right, while outside reporters on a public repo still land readable issues (title prefix and body fingerprint remain the load-bearing handles).

Requirement

REQ-159

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-15902-1 - Before create, the tool calls gh label list --json name on the destination repo and intersects the requested labels ("rcf-feedback", "severity:<sev>", "area:<blueprint|core>") with the returned set. Missing labels are dropped from the create call and recorded on the entry state as droppedLabels[] and in the preview ledger.

    Given a fake gh module whose label list returns { rcf-feedback, severity:major } but not area:blueprint

    When submit --yes is run with one pending major-severity blueprint entry

    Then gh issue create is called with labels rcf-feedback, severity:major only; the entry state carries droppedLabels: ["area:blueprint"]

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

  • AC-15902-2 - scripts/bootstrap-feedback-labels.mjs is a one-shot script a repo admin runs to create the six labels in one destination repo: rcf-feedback, severity:blocker, severity:major, severity:minor, area:blueprint, area:core. Idempotent: existing labels are left alone; missing ones are created via gh label create. The script is a maintainer aid, not called from init or doctor.

    Given a fake gh module in the script fixture whose label list starts empty

    When the script is run once, then again

    Then first run creates six labels via gh label create; second run makes zero create calls; exit 0 on both

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

  • AC-15902-3 - The rendered issue title always carries the prefix ("[<effective-slug>] " for blueprints, "[rcf-lite] " for core) and the body always carries the visible rcf-feedback-fingerprint: <fp> line plus the HTML-comment twin. Both are load-bearing triage handles when labels are missing or dropped.

    Given render() is called on a blueprint and a core entry

    When the rendered title and body are compared to templates

    Then blueprint titles start with "[<slug>] "; core titles start with "[rcf-lite] "; each body carries the fingerprint on its own line and inside an HTML comment (fingerprint appears twice on purpose)

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

  • AC-15902-4 - The six-label catalogue (rcf-feedback, severity:blocker, severity:major, severity:minor, area:blueprint, area:core) is exported as a single frozen constant from src/feedback/labels.js (FEEDBACK_LABELS or equivalent). Both scripts/bootstrap-feedback-labels.mjs and the submit-time label pre-check import that constant and refuse to hard-code any of the six names locally. A grep test asserts no string literal for a catalogue label name appears outside src/feedback/labels.js, its own tests, and the bootstrap script that imports it.

    Given a fresh clone of the repo

    When the grep test enumerates string literals for each of the six label names across src/, scripts/, bin/

    Then every hit is either inside src/feedback/labels.js, a test file that imports the constant, or the bootstrap script; there is no bare string literal for any of the six names elsewhere

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

REQ-160 No path leaves the operator stuck functional US1 AC4 draft

Every failure mode of the submit path routes to a local bundle file with a one-line message that names the reason, the repo URL to paste into, and where the bundle was written. gh missing, gh not logged in, repo unreachable, viewerPermission NONE on a private repo, issues disabled, create or comment failure and unresolved destination all map to a bundle rather than a stall. Bundled entries are terminal (not re-asked) so the operator is never nagged about the same finding; a hand-driven re-submit is supported for one entry once access exists.

capability:feedback-loop

User stories (1)

US-16001 No gh, no login or no access still gives the operator a bundle and a URL AC4 draft

US-16001 - No gh, no login or no access still gives the operator a bundle and a URL

As a: operator without gh installed, not logged in, or without access to a private destination repo

I want: submit to write a bundle file with the exact issue text and print the file path and the destination issues/new URL in one line

So that: I can paste or email the report even when the tool cannot file it on my behalf, and I am not asked about the same entries again next session

Requirement

REQ-160

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-16001-1 - Preflight order (per destination): gh on PATH -> gh auth status non-zero -> gh repo view viewerPermission NONE on a private repo -> gh repo view hasIssuesEnabled false. The first failure routes to a bundle for that destination without any further gh call. The bundle path <cwd>/.rcf/feedback/outbox/<ISO-timestamp>-<repo-slug>.md is printed on its own line next to the destination issues/new URL. Each failure kind maps to a distinct one-line message (naming gh, naming "run gh auth login", naming private-access with the library contact, naming issues-disabled).

    Given four fixture cases: gh missing on PATH; gh present but auth status non-zero; repo private with viewerPermission NONE; repo with hasIssuesEnabled false

    When submit --yes is run once per case with one pending entry

    Then each run writes the bundle under outbox with the expected filename shape and prints the URL and path on one line together; entry state is bundled with outboxPath; exit code 0

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

  • AC-16001-2 - If create or comment fails after the label pre-check (network 4xx or 5xx, abuse rate limit, unexpected label rejection), submit retries once without labels and, on a second failure, bundles that entry only. Other entries continue. Exit code is 0 when every entry ended submitted or bundled, and 3 when a residual secret leaves one entry pending.

    Given a fake gh module whose issue create throws with a 429-shaped error on the first two calls and succeeds on the third

    When submit --yes runs with three pending entries

    Then the first entry retries once, then bundles; the second retries once, then bundles; the third submits; exit 0; two bundle files exist and the third entry is submitted

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

  • AC-16001-3 - Bundled entries are terminal for the ask loop: rcf feedback list default (pending) does not show them, the SessionStart hook does not count them into the carry-over ask, and the Stop hook does not re-ask about them. rcf feedback submit <id> re-attempts one bundled entry by hand and moves it to submitted on success.

    Given a fixture with two bundled entries and one pending entry

    When the Stop hook decision function is invoked and rcf feedback list default is called

    Then Stop asks only about the pending entry, list shows only the pending entry, list --all shows the bundled entries with status bundled; submit fb-<id-of-bundle> retries just that one

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

  • AC-16001-4 - When submit encounters an entry whose destination cannot be resolved (library without an issues field and no derivable git source, so destination.resolve() returned unresolved), the entry is written to the bundle at .rcf/feedback/outbox/<ISO-timestamp>-unresolved.md, the publisher contact from the registry entry (if present) is printed on the same line as the outbox path, no gh call is made for that entry, and exit code stays 0. The entry state folds to bundled with outboxPath.

    Given a fixture project with one applied library whose registry entry carries neither issuesRepo nor a derivable github git source but does carry publisher.contact, and one pending blueprint entry against that library

    When submit --yes is run

    Then the outbox file exists with the unresolved-slug filename, stdout carries the publisher.contact on the same line as the outbox path, no gh invocation was made, entry state is bundled, exit code is 0

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-183

REQ-161 One ask per session, at a pause, never automatic functional US4 AC11 draft

The operator is asked at most once per session and only when the agent is genuinely idle: not in the middle of a fix and not on the same day the entry was recorded unless a blocker forces it. The quiet rule (15 minute age or queue complete or carried over or --ask-now) is configurable via quietMinutes in rcf/feedback-settings.json. The ask is offered by the harness hook on Stop and by RULE 17 in the managed block as the belt-and-braces fallback. rcf feedback opt-out silences the ask permanently for a project; RCF_FEEDBACK_ASK=0 silences it per user or per CI run; RCF_FEEDBACK_DISABLE=1 turns even the local log off.

capability:feedback-loop

User stories (4)

US-16101 Operator is asked once, at a pause, with the exact preview text, and never nagged AC3 draft

US-16101 - Operator is asked once, at a pause, with the exact preview text, and never nagged

As a: operator in the middle of getting work done

I want: the ask to arrive at a natural pause (queue complete, an entry older than 15 minutes, a carried-over entry, or a --ask-now blocker), for the ask to carry the exact preview text and destination, and for me never to be asked twice in one session

So that: the ask is welcome rather than an interruption

Requirement

REQ-161

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-16101-1 - The quiet rule in src/feedback/hook.js returns "ask" on stop when ALL hold: not opted out (rcf/feedback-settings.json ask true and RCF_FEEDBACK_ASK unset or 1); at least one pending entry; state.json has no asked record for the incoming session_id; stop_hook_active is false; and one of: an entry carries askNow; the newest pending entry is older than quietMinutes (default 15) minutes; the queue-state cache reports complete or nothing actionable; the entry was carried over. Otherwise returns "silent". A table test walks every named row.

    Given a fixture state file and a table of pending/asked/optOut/stopHookActive/age/queueState/carriedOver/askNow rows

    When shouldAsk(input) is called on each row

    Then every row returns the expected verdict; the asked record is appended to state.json before the emit path in the wrapper (assertable at the caller by observing state mutation before hook stdout is produced)

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-184

  • AC-16101-2 - On Claude Code (--harness claude-code default when CLAUDECODE is set), the stop hook exits 2 with the reason text on stderr. The reason names the exact next-step verbs ("rcf feedback preview", "rcf feedback submit --yes", "rcf feedback defer", "rcf feedback opt-out") and says "Do not ask again this session." On Codex (--harness codex), the hook emits stdout JSON { "decision": "block", "reason": "<same text>" } with exit 0. Both branches append the asked record to state.json exactly once per session_id.

    Given a fixture project with one pending entry, and two mock harness JSON inputs on stdin (Claude Code and Codex shapes)

    When rcf feedback hook stop --harness claude-code and --harness codex are run

    Then Claude Code run: exit code 2, stderr carries the four verb names and the "do not ask again this session" clause; Codex run: exit 0, stdout parses to { decision: "block", reason: ... } with the same clause; state.json in both cases gained exactly one asked record for the input session_id

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-184

  • AC-16101-3 - A second stop invocation with the same session_id is silent (no exit-2, no JSON block emission, exit 0) even when new pending entries arrive after the first ask. A new session_id resets the ledger and asks again per the quiet rule.

    Given a fixture state.json with one asked record, one further pending entry added after the ask

    When rcf feedback hook stop is run twice with the same session_id and then once with a fresh session_id

    Then the two same-session calls are silent (exit 0, no reason emitted); the fresh-session call re-emits the ask per the quiet rule

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-184

US-16102 Operator silences the ask for this project AC2 draft

US-16102 - Operator silences the ask for this project

As a: operator who does not want to be asked about feedback on this project

I want: a one-command opt-out that writes rcf/feedback-settings.json:ask false (checked in), and an env variable that silences the ask per user without touching the file

So that: a shared project silences the ask for everyone, and a CI or per-user preference silences it locally

Requirement

REQ-161

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-16102-1 - rcf feedback opt-out writes rcf/feedback-settings.json with { settingsVersion: 1, ask: false, redaction: { allowHosts: [] }, quietMinutes: 15 } (merging with any prior file). rcf feedback opt-in restores ask true. The hook shouldAsk returns silent when ask is false. rcf feedback add, preview and submit keep working under ask: false (hand-driven flow).

    Given a fresh fixture project

    When rcf feedback opt-out then rcf feedback hook stop with one pending entry, then rcf feedback preview

    Then the settings file contains ask: false; the hook exits 0 silently; preview still renders the entry

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-184

  • AC-16102-2 - RCF_FEEDBACK_ASK=0 forces silent on the hook regardless of file setting. RCF_FEEDBACK_DISABLE=1 makes rcf feedback add a no-op that prints "feedback disabled by env" (no file write, no exit-2). Precedence order: env DISABLE > env ASK=0 > file ask false > file ask true.

    Given a fixture project with ask true in the file, plus each env variable in turn

    When rcf feedback add and rcf feedback hook stop are run under each precedence combination

    Then env DISABLE suppresses add entirely; env ASK=0 keeps add working but silences the hook; file ask false silences the hook and add still works

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-184

US-16103 A carried-over batch is offered next session AC3 draft

US-16103 - A carried-over batch is offered next session

As a: operator whose session ended before the ask fired

I want: the SessionEnd hook to flush a bundle idempotently and the SessionStart hook of the next session to inject a one-line context reminder that pending entries exist

So that: a crash or /clear does not lose findings and the next session's first pause carries the ask

Requirement

REQ-161

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-16103-1 - rcf feedback hook session-end writes the outbox bundle for any pending entries under 1 second (the shared Claude Code SessionEnd budget is 1.5s) and is byte-idempotent (same content hash means no rewrite). Codex SessionEnd runs the same handler; output is discarded either way.

    Given a fixture with two pending entries and a stubbed clock so the elapsed time is measurable

    When rcf feedback hook session-end is run twice back-to-back

    Then the first run writes one bundle file under outbox; the second run runs to completion in under 1 second without rewriting the same-hash file; both exit 0

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-184

  • AC-16103-2 - rcf feedback hook session-start with pending entries and a new sessionId prints one plain line to stdout on Claude Code ("rcf feedback: <n> unsubmitted entr(y|ies) carried over from an earlier session; ask the operator once at a natural pause (RULE 17).") and the Codex-shaped equivalent under --harness codex. The line is what the harness injects as context; it never blocks. If SessionStart on Codex cannot inject context (verified at build time against the current Codex reference), the fallback in RULE 17 ("check rcf feedback status at session start") is what carries the same posture.

    Given a fixture with two pending entries carried over from a prior sessionId

    When rcf feedback hook session-start is run under each harness

    Then the Claude Code stdout matches the exact wording above; the Codex JSON matches the reference shape currently accepted for SessionStart context; both return exit 0; state.json is not mutated (asked is set on Stop, not on session-start)

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-184

  • AC-16103-3 - rcf feedback defer means "not now, ask again next session" (design 3.1). Entries in status deferredUntilSession whose stored sessionId is not the current one are requeued to pending on the SessionStart hook AND on the Stop hook (belt to the SessionStart braces, so the flow works when only Stop is installed). The requeue appends one state-transition line per entry with status pending and no sessionId field, so fold-by-id preserves the entry's prior sessionId and the carry-over gate in both hooks (pending.sessionId !== currentSessionId) fires naturally in the new session. Entries recorded or last deferred under the current sessionId are not re-transitioned (idempotent per session; deferring twice in one session is a no-op on the second call).

    Given a fixture with one pending entry deferred in session A (entries.jsonl carries the deferredUntilSession line with sessionId A)

    When rcf feedback hook session-start --harness claude-code is run with session_id B, then rcf feedback hook stop --harness claude-code is run with the same session_id B

    Then SessionStart appends one { status: pending } transition (no sessionId field) so the entry returns to pending with its sessionId still A; the carry-over line prints to stdout naming the count and RULE 17; the following Stop exits 2 with the ask on stderr and appends exactly one asked record for session B; a second SessionStart in session B is a no-op (no new transition, silent stdout); a further SessionStart in a fresh session_id C after a Stop-only path (no SessionStart wired) still requeues on the Stop hook so the ask fires there

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-184

US-16104 rcf init installs the feedback hooks and rcf doctor keeps them honest AC3 draft

US-16104 - rcf init installs the feedback hooks and rcf doctor keeps them honest

As a: operator running rcf init on a project

I want: the feedback Stop / SessionEnd / SessionStart hook entries merged into .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json (with --no-feedback-hooks to skip), and rcf doctor to report missing-hook (fixable with --fix) and foreign-hook (refused) so the harness config stays honest across clones

So that: every clone gets the same ask behaviour without a per-developer setup step, and drift is surfaced instead of quietly diverging

Requirement

REQ-161

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-16104-1 - rcf init merges three feedback hook entries into .claude/settings.json (Stop -> "npx rcf-lite feedback hook stop --harness claude-code" timeout 10; SessionEnd -> "... hook session-end ..." timeout 5; SessionStart matcher "startup|resume" -> "... hook session-start ...") and three matching entries into .codex/hooks.json (in the Codex schema for the same events). Merge discipline mirrors writeMcpConfig: parse, refuse on invalid JSON with the same message shape as .mcp.json, never clobber other hooks, add ours only if an entry whose command contains "rcf feedback hook" is absent. The "npx rcf-lite" prefix is replaced by binPath when init was called with --bin-path, mirroring the .mcp.json entry pattern.

    Given a fresh fixture project with no .claude/settings.json and no .codex/hooks.json

    When rcf init is run without --no-feedback-hooks

    Then both files contain the three feedback hook entries in the right shape; a second rcf init on the same tree is byte-idempotent; a pre-existing settings.json with an unrelated hook is preserved and the feedback entries are added alongside it

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-184

  • AC-16104-2 - rcf init --no-feedback-hooks writes neither .claude/settings.json nor .codex/hooks.json feedback entries and prints the instruction-only fallback line once (RULE 17 still applies). --no-feedback-hooks composes with --no-playwright-mcp and other init skips without interaction.

    Given a fresh fixture project

    When rcf init --no-feedback-hooks is run

    Then no feedback hook entry is present in either config file; init exits 0; the one-line instruction fallback appears in stdout

REQ-162 Agents know when to log and when to ask functional US1 AC2 draft

RULE 17 in the managed instructions block tells every harness (Claude Code and Codex) when to run rcf feedback add, how to ask exactly once at a natural pause, and which of preview, submit --yes, defer and opt-out to run in each branch. The rule is static text (no versions, no dates) so the block hash moves once on the release that ships it, and it is loaded into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md by rcf init through the existing managed-block mechanism. It names all four verbs and the redaction posture so an agent under pace still follows the shape when the harness hook has not been trusted.

capability:feedback-loop

User stories (1)

US-16201 RULE 17 tells every agent when to log and when to ask AC2 draft

US-16201 - RULE 17 tells every agent when to log and when to ask

As a: harness (Claude Code or Codex) that reads the managed instructions block

I want: a static RULE 17 in guidance/managed/agent-instructions-block.md that names rcf feedback add for logging, describes the one-ask-per-session posture (harness hook or operator wrap-up as trigger, preview then submit --yes or defer or opt-out), and states the redaction posture

So that: an agent under pace still follows the shape when the harness hooks are not trusted, and the same rule serves both harnesses

Requirement

REQ-162

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-16201-1 - guidance/managed/agent-instructions-block.md gains RULE 17 with the wording specified in design section 3.4. pnpm run build:managed regenerates the block hash and harness-template.md so rcf doctor doctor-agent-instructions and gen-managed-artefacts stay byte-consistent. The wording is static (no version numbers, no dates) and names all four verbs (preview, submit --yes, defer, opt-out). A byte-exact template test loads the shipped block and asserts the RULE 17 slice is byte-for-byte identical to the design-section-3.4 fixture stored in test/fixtures/managed/rule-17.md, so a wording drift on ship is caught.

    Given a fixture repository state with RULE 17 not yet added

    When the change is applied, pnpm run build:managed is run, and rcf doctor is run

    Then RULE 17 appears in the block file exactly as specified; the hash file changes on this release; doctor doctor-agent-instructions reports clean; a byte-exact template test asserts the RULE 17 slice of the block matches test/fixtures/managed/rule-17.md byte-for-byte

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-185

  • AC-16201-2 - rcf init writes CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md with the regenerated block (RULE 17 included). The existing managed-block installation path (writeAgentInstructions) is the only touch-point; no init-time flag is added for RULE 17.

    Given a fresh fixture project

    When rcf init is run

    Then CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md both contain the RULE 17 block text between the managed-block markers; the block outside the markers is untouched

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-185

REQ-163 Referee guarantee: `rcf define validate` walks every schema-declared reference field on ADR (supersededBy, relatedAdrs) so the docs-page 'nothing points at nothing' claim holds functional US1 AC2 draft

Referee-guarantees docs page (how-it-works/what-the-referee-guarantees) promises that `rcf define validate` proves every reference in every document resolves, so a walked tree that passes has nothing pointing at nothing. The 0.27.0 walker checks the parent-id fields and the FBS / TS / EVAL / CN cross-links, but two ADR-schema-declared reference fields, supersededBy and relatedAdrs, are declared in the ADR schema without being walked: a bad target passes validate. This train closes the gap by walking both fields inside collectBrokenReferences, keeping the existing brokenReference error kind, and reporting the exact ADR file + field on failure. Chain: referee-guarantees docs claims C-7 and C-38 (audit at reviews/2026-09-15-docs-claims-audit/how-it-works__what-the-referee-guarantees.json). No schema change (the schema already declares both fields); rcf-lite behaviour widens, and any project whose ADRs have stale supersession pointers surfaces the defect the next time validate runs.

capability:verify

User stories (1)

US-16301 US-16301: define validate walks ADR supersededBy; relatedAdrs stays a schemas follow-up (compatibility carry) AC2 draft

US-16301 - US-16301: define validate walks ADR supersededBy; relatedAdrs stays a schemas follow-up (compatibility carry)

As a: beta reader relying on the referee-guarantees page to know what `rcf define validate` proves

I want: a broken ADR supersededBy pointer to be reported as a brokenReference the same way a broken parent link is, and the soft `relatedAdrs` back-reference to stay silent so the ratified blueprint-supersede workflow is not broken

So that: the docs-page promise that every reference in every document resolves is enforced on the strong chain-of-decisions reference (supersededBy), while the soft see-also field stays a schemas follow-up (either value-narrowed or workflow-aware)

Requirement

REQ-163

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-16301-1 - An ADR whose supersededBy names an id with no file on disk (or an id that resolves to a non-ADR kind) surfaces as a brokenReference error naming the ADR file and the field `supersededBy`, and the corresponding target id joins tree.brokenIds. A supersededBy field that is absent or empty is silent.

    Given an initialised RCF project with adr-001.json whose supersededBy is set to a non-existent id ADR-999

    When walkTree runs (as invoked by `rcf define validate`)

    Then errors contain a brokenReference with documentId ADR-001 and field supersededBy naming ADR-999, and tree.brokenIds contains ADR-999

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-186

  • AC-16301-2 - An ADR whose relatedAdrs contains an id with no file on disk stays SILENT under walkTree: the ratified `rcf define blueprint supersede` workflow writes a project ADR whose relatedAdrs lists both the applied blueprint ADR (on disk) and the incoming blueprint ADR (not yet on disk; the incoming add is the closing step of option 3). Walking relatedAdrs would refuse that workflow between the supersede write and the re-add; the compatibility carry keeps the soft back-reference unchecked here. Tightening this is a schemas follow-up (value-narrow to applied ADR ids, or a workflow-aware exception on the supersede write path).

    Given an initialised RCF project with adr-001.json whose relatedAdrs is set to [ADR-777] (a non-existent id, mirroring the transient state between supersede and re-add)

    When walkTree runs (as invoked by `rcf define validate`)

    Then no brokenReference error targets the relatedAdrs field on ADR-001

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-186

REQ-164 Referee guarantee: `rcf audit coverage` is strict-by-default; `--mode shallow-any` is the explicit opt-out; `--strict` remains a no-op alias functional US1 AC3 draft

Referee-guarantees docs page states without qualification that a requirement counts as covered only when every acceptance criterion beneath it has a resolving Test Case, and that a stub or stale pointer fails the coverage gate exactly as a missing test does when the displayed command (`rcf audit coverage`) is run. The 0.27.0 shipped default is shallow-any, so the plain command does not enforce that; strict is per-AC-strict but is opt-in via `--strict`. This train flips the shipped default: strict is the default, `--mode shallow-any` is the explicit opt-out for author-time exploration (prints gaps, exits 0), and the legacy `--strict` flag stays as a no-op alias so existing CI, blueprints and dogfood scripts stay green. `--mode shallow-any --strict` is a usage refusal (exit 2) so a scripted invocation cannot silently disagree with itself. CHANGELOG carries a migration note under [Unreleased]. Repo's own CI dogfood invocation is updated to the shipped default. Closes referee-guarantees docs claims C-11 and C-14 (audit at reviews/2026-09-15-docs-claims-audit/how-it-works__what-the-referee-guarantees.json).

capability:verify

User stories (1)

US-16401 US-16401: strict-by-default coverage with a shallow-any opt-out and a legacy --strict alias AC3 draft

US-16401 - US-16401: strict-by-default coverage with a shallow-any opt-out and a legacy --strict alias

As a: beta reader who typed the command from the referee-guarantees page

I want: `rcf audit coverage` with no flag to fail the gate on a stub or missing test, and `--mode shallow-any` to be the documented escape valve

So that: the docs promise 'a stub or stale pointer fails the gate exactly as a missing test does' holds by construction, and my existing `--strict` invocations do not need rewriting

Requirement

REQ-164

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-16401-1 - The plain `rcf audit coverage` command runs strict (per-AC) mode. On a tree whose ACs are not all covered by resolving TCs, it prints the table and exits 4; on a fully covered tree it exits 0. The default is the same as the legacy `--strict` invocation.

    Given an initialised RCF project with a scaffold AC-101-1 that has no covering TC

    When `rcf audit coverage` is invoked with no strictness flag

    Then the exit code is 4

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-187

  • AC-16401-2 - `--mode shallow-any` reports gaps and exits 0. The output's Coverage-mode line reads `shallow-any` and the table renders the same shape as strict mode; the exit code is 0 even on uncovered ACs.

    Given the same scaffold as AC-16401-1

    When `rcf audit coverage --mode shallow-any` is invoked

    Then the exit code is 0 and the output includes 'Coverage mode: shallow-any'

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-187

  • AC-16401-3 - Conflicting flags exit 2 with a usage message. Passing `--mode shallow-any --strict` (in either order) is refused before running the audit; the error names both flags. `--mode` with an unknown value (e.g. `lenient`) also exits 2 with a usage message.

    Given an initialised RCF project

    When `rcf audit coverage --mode shallow-any --strict` is invoked

    Then the exit code is 2 and stderr matches /--mode shallow-any conflicts with --strict/

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-187

REQ-165 Referee guarantee: `rcf build finalise` refuses UI-BASELINE-UNMET / BROWSER-VERIFICATION-MISSING / SCOPE-MISMATCH; verified traces to a post-merge run; manual override is gated functional US2 AC6 draft

Referee-guarantees docs page promises that `rcf build finalise` is the only path that writes verified, that a chain that says verified traces to an actual post-merge runtime check, and that the finalise gate refuses on the three per-AC verdicts the aggregator already emits: UI-BASELINE-UNMET (docs claim C-28; also covers a block-severity probe-pack failure, C-36), BROWSER-VERIFICATION-MISSING (C-29) and SCOPE-MISMATCH (C-30). The 0.27.0 finalise CLI only branched on MOCK-ONLY-DECLARED / BLOCKED-BY-DECLARATION and EVAL-MISSING / EVAL-BELOW-THRESHOLD; the three new verdicts were derived on the report but did not gate finalise. The manual override path (`rcf define update FBS.executionStatus=verified`) was accepted by the writer, defeating the C-22 promise. This train wires the three per-AC refusals in finalise (no ack path: the refusals are honest; fix the AC or its scope), gates the manual override behind `--acknowledge-verified-override` on `rcf define update` (per the escalation clause: existing WSD projects may still need the escape valve; the writer's default is now the documented behaviour), and adds a git default-branch precondition to finalise with `--allow-pre-merge` as the deliberate pre-merge dry-run opt-out. Closes referee-guarantees docs claims C-22 / C-26 / C-28 / C-29 / C-30 / C-36 (audit at reviews/2026-09-15-docs-claims-audit/how-it-works__what-the-referee-guarantees.json). C-33 (shipWithoutEval manifest field) remains open: the write path already exists (skips schema validation), but the rcf-schemas 0.6.2 manifest schema does not yet declare the field; the exact delta needed lands in the ship-without-eval.js comment and in the report for this dispatch. C-38 (per-check applicable:false in browserVerificationProbePackCheck) is also blocked on the rcf-schemas bump; source comments already flag it.

capability:verify

User stories (2)

US-16501 US-16501: finalise refuses on UI-BASELINE-UNMET, BROWSER-VERIFICATION-MISSING and SCOPE-MISMATCH AC3 draft

So that: a UI baseline violation, a missing browser check on a UI-bearing FBS, a bound TC narrower than its AC scope, or a block-severity probe-pack failure all fail the gate the same way the mock-only and EVAL refusals already do

REQ-165

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-16501-1 - On a verify PASS (exit 0, ship authority) whose report carries at least one per-AC UI-BASELINE-UNMET verdict, `rcf build finalise` exits 4 and leaves the FBS at 'complete'. The stderr message names the AC(s), the count of UI-BASELINE-UNMET verdicts, and the referee-guarantees claim ids C-28 and C-36 (a block-severity probe-pack failure aggregates into UI-BASELINE-UNMET, so the same branch closes both).

  • AC-16501-3 - Same shape for SCOPE-MISMATCH (NV-BL-GATE-01): a bound TC narrower than its AC scope aggregates into a per-AC SCOPE-MISMATCH verdict that finalise refuses. Exit 4, FBS at 'complete', stderr names C-30.

    Given the same scaffold with perAcVerdicts = [{acId, verdict: 'SCOPE-MISMATCH'}]

US-16502 US-16502: finalise is the only path to verified, and it fires only on a default trunk AC3 draft

US-16502 - US-16502: finalise is the only path to verified, and it fires only on a default trunk

As a: beta reader trusting the referee-guarantees page's verified-invariant promise

I want: `rcf define update` to refuse writing FBS.executionStatus=verified by default, and `rcf build finalise` to refuse promotion when the git working tree is not on a default trunk

So that: a chain that says verified traces to an actual post-merge runtime check by construction, and a mid-branch dev-loop finalise cannot stamp verified without the operator's deliberate opt-out

Requirement

REQ-165

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-16502-1 - The writer refuses a define-update patch that sets FBS.executionStatus=verified when `options.allowVerifiedOverride` is not true. The refusal is an RcfError with kind='usage' whose message names the finalise gate and the --acknowledge-verified-override escape flag; the FBS on disk stays unchanged.

    Given an FBS at status 'complete' loaded through walkTree

    When updateDocument is called with sets = [{path:'executionStatus', value:'verified'}] and options = {}

    Then the result is an RcfError with kind='usage' matching /verified is written only by the finalise gate/, and the FBS file on disk still reads status 'complete'

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-189

  • AC-16502-2 - Passing `options.allowVerifiedOverride: true` (the seam that finalise and `rcf define update --acknowledge-verified-override` both use) writes the value: the returned shape carries the doc id and the FBS on disk reads status 'verified'.

    Given the same scaffold as AC-16502-1

    When updateDocument is called with the same sets and options = {allowVerifiedOverride: true}

    Then the result carries an id and the FBS file on disk reads status 'verified'

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-189

  • AC-16502-3 - `rcf build finalise` refuses promotion when the git working tree is not on a default trunk (main or master). Exit 4, FBS at 'complete', stderr names the branch and the referee-guarantees claim C-26. --allow-pre-merge is the deliberate opt-out: on a non-default branch it promotes and logs the pre-merge decision on stdout including the C-26 claim id.

    Given the same scaffold with a spawn seam that returns 'feature/x' as the current branch

    When `rcf build finalise <fbsId> --url ...` is invoked

    Then the exit code is 4 and stderr matches /git working tree is on branch 'feature\/x'/; with --allow-pre-merge appended the exit code is 0 and stdout matches /Referee-guarantees claim C-26 records the pre-merge decision here/

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-189

      "when": "updateDocument is called with sets = [{path:'executionStatus', value:'verified'}] and options = {}",

      "when": "updateDocument is called with the same sets and options = {allowVerifiedOverride: true}",
      "then": "the result carries an id and the FBS file on disk reads status 'verified'",
      "testable": true,
      "scope": "library"

      "id": "AC-16502-3",
      "description": "`rcf build finalise` refuses promotion when the git working tree is not on a default trunk (main or master).       "given": "the same scaffold with a spawn seam that returns 'feature/x' as the current branch",
      "when": "`rcf build finalise <fbsId> --url ...` is invoked",
      "then": "the exit code is 4 and stderr matches /git working tree is on branch 'feature\\/x'/; with --allow-pre-merge appended the exit code is 0 and stdout matches /Referee-guarantees claim C-26 records the pre-merge decision here/",
      "testable": true,
      "scope": "runtime"
    }

  "description": "Referee-guarantees docs page promises that `rcf build finalise` is the only path that writes verified, that a chain that says verified traces to an actual post-merge runtime check, and that the finalise gate refuses on the three per-AC verdicts the aggregator already emits: UI-BASELINE-UNMET (docs claim C-28; also covers a block-severity probe-pack failure, C-36), BROWSER-VERIFICATION-MISSING (C-29) and SCOPE-MISMATCH (C-30). The 0.27.0 finalise CLI only branched on MOCK-ONLY-DECLARED / BLOCKED-BY-DECLARATION and EVAL-MISSING / EVAL-BELOW-THRESHOLD; the three new verdicts were derived on the report but did not gate finalise. The manual override path (`rcf define update FBS.executionStatus=verified`) was accepted by the writer, defeating the C-22 promise. This train wires the three per-AC refusals in finalise (no ack path: the refusals are honest; fix the AC or its scope), gates the manual override behind `--acknowledge-verified-override` on `rcf define update` (per the escalation clause: existing WSD projects may still need the escape valve; the writer's default is now the documented behaviour), and adds a git default-branch precondition to finalise with `--allow-pre-merge` as the deliberate pre-merge dry-run opt-out. Closes referee-guarantees docs claims C-22 / C-26 / C-28 / C-29 / C-30 / C-36 (audit at reviews/2026-09-15-docs-claims-audit/how-it-works__what-the-referee-guarantees.json). REQ-170 Product Map tab on the review surface reviewSurface US8 AC9 draft

The RCF review surface offers a Product Map tab in addition to Overview, Requirements, Architecture and Build sequence. The tab lets a product reader group requirements by shape, status, component (TAC), trace coverage or capability. Every grouping drills group -> requirement (with a status pill) -> its user stories -> acceptance criteria. Groupings and the status filter are hash-addressable so a URL of the form #tab=product-map&group=capability&status=approved is deep-linkable and shareable.

Why: The Requirements tab is a flat REQ list ordered by id. A product reader (operator or reviewer) does not think in that shape - they think in surfaces, capabilities, states, and what has and has not been built yet. The Product Map tab re-buckets the same in-memory tree by the axes the data actually populates (shape 65%, status 100%) and by two derived axes (component-first via TAC, and trace coverage), plus a convention-driven capability grouping. No schema change; all work is a re-bucketing of the tree-model the view already builds.

capability:review-surface product-map view

User stories (8)

US-17001 Product Map: shape grouping AC2 draft

US-17001 - Product Map: shape grouping

As a: a product reader reviewing the requirements chain

I want: the Product Map tab to bucket requirements by shapeClassification.shapes[], with an "Unclassified" bucket for REQs missing the classification and a "Business rules" bucket for the "none" shape

So that: I can see at a glance which requirements sit in each surface area (webUi, httpApi, auth, persistence, notifications, business rules) without reading every REQ body

Description: User story under REQ-170. a product reader reviewing the requirements chain the Product Map tab to bucket requirements by shapeClassification.shapes[], with an "Unclassified" bucket for REQs missing the classification and a "Business rules" bucket for the "none" shape

Requirement

REQ-170

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17001-1 - The rendered review-surface HTML carries a "product-map" tab (data-tab="product-map") in tab order after Build sequence, with a hidden tabpanel id "tab-product-map" containing a shape-grouping section whose bucket headings enumerate every shape the classified REQs use plus "Unclassified" and "Business rules". A REQ classified into two shapes appears in both buckets. Rendering does not require a schema change.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-190

  • AC-17001-2 - Selecting the shape grouping drills each bucket to its REQs (rendered with the same doc-details helper and status pill as the Requirements tab), each REQ to its user stories, and each user story to its acceptance criteria, so the reader can go from a shape bucket to an AC in the same tab. Grouping button clicks and status filter changes push a new history entry (Back/Forward traverse them); top-level tab clicks keep their existing behaviour.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-190

US-17002 Product Map: status filter AC1 draft

US-17002 - Product Map: status filter

As a: a reviewer preparing a sign-off pass

I want: a status filter (all, draft, review, needsRevision, approved, superseded) on the Product Map tab that applies to whichever grouping is active

So that: I can narrow the tab to just the "approved" or just the "needsRevision" REQs without switching tabs or scanning by hand

Description: User story under REQ-170. a reviewer preparing a sign-off pass a status filter (all, draft, review, needsRevision, approved, superseded) on the Product Map tab that applies to whichever grouping is active

Requirement

REQ-170

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17002-1 - The Product Map tab carries a status filter control whose options are the five authoring statuses plus "all", and applies to every grouping on the tab. When "approved" is selected the tab renders only REQs whose status is approved. Buckets that become empty under the current filter are hidden by default with a summary line ("N empty" - clicking reveals them), so the map keeps its shape without rendering a wall of empty headings.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-190

US-17003 Product Map: component-first grouping AC1 draft

US-17003 - Product Map: component-first grouping

As a: a technical reviewer wanting to see requirements from the architecture down

I want: a component grouping rooted at the TAD, showing each TAC (with its dependencies) at level 1, the user stories linked to that TAC at level 2, each story's parent REQ at level 3, and its ACs at level 4, plus an "Unmapped" bucket for REQs no component reaches

So that: I can pivot from a component to the requirements it delivers without leaving the tab

Description: User story under REQ-170. a technical reviewer wanting to see requirements from the architecture down a component grouping rooted at the TAD, showing each TAC (with its dependencies) at level 1, the user stories linked to that TAC at level 2, each story's parent REQ at level 3, and its ACs at level 4, plus an "Unmapped" bucket for REQs no component reaches

Requirement

REQ-170

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17003-1 - When the Product Map is grouped by component, the tab renders the TAD as the root, one section per TAC (with a short dependencies[] list drawn from the TAC document), then the user stories under that TAC (from usByTacId), then their parent REQs (from us.reqId), then the ACs. REQs reachable by no TAC are collected under an "Unmapped" bucket with a count in its heading.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-190

US-17005 - Product Map: capability grouping

As a: a product reader thinking in capabilities rather than technical shape

I want: a capability grouping that reads capability:<slug> entries from REQ.tags[] and buckets requirements per capability

US-17006 Product Map: usable interaction model AC1 draft

US-17006 - Product Map: usable interaction model

As a: a product reader who returns to the Product Map across sessions

I want: collapsed-by-default buckets, a jump-nav index across the top, per-bucket status mini-counts, hash-encoded open-bucket state and compact REQ cards with drill-down (raw JSON stays on the Requirements tab)

So that: the tab scans in under a minute and a bookmarked URL restores tab, grouping, filter and the buckets I had open, and my open state survives a live refresh

Description: a product reader who returns to the tab across sessions collapsed-by-default buckets, a jump-nav index across the top, per-bucket status mini-counts, hash-encoded open buckets so a bookmarked URL restores tab plus grouping plus filter plus open buckets, and compact REQ cards with drill-down (raw JSON stays on the Requirements tab), so the tab scans in under a minute and survives a live-refresh with open state intact

Requirement

REQ-170

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17006-1 - The Product Map tab renders every bucket collapsed by default, with a summary row carrying the bucket label, its total REQ count and a mini count per authoring status (draft / review / needsRevision / approved / superseded). A jump-nav rail across the top of the panel lists every bucket in the active grouping with its count; clicking a chip scrolls to that bucket and opens it. The hash schema `#tab=product-map&group=<g>&status=<s>&open=<id1>,<id2>` restores tab, grouping, status filter AND the set of open buckets on return, and every bucket-toggle pushes a new history entry so Back/Forward traverse them. Per-bucket <details> nodes carry a stable data-doc-id ("pm-bucket:<group>:<id>") so the live-client persists their open state across SSE refreshes.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-192

  "soThat": "the tab scans in under a minute and a bookmarked URL restores tab, grouping, filter and the buckets I had open, and my open state survives a live refresh",
  "acceptanceCriteria": [
    {
      "id": "AC-17006-1",
      "description": "The Product Map tab renders every bucket collapsed by default, with a summary row carrying the bucket label, its total REQ count and a mini count per authoring status (draft / review / needsRevision / approved / superseded). A jump-nav rail across the top of the panel lists every bucket in the active grouping with its count; clicking a chip scrolls to that bucket and opens it. The hash schema `#tab=product-map&group=<g>&status=<s>&open=<id1>,<id2>` restores tab, grouping, status filter AND the set of open buckets on return, and every bucket-toggle pushes a new history entry so Back/Forward traverse them. Per-bucket <details> nodes carry a stable data-doc-id (\"pm-bucket:<group>:<id>\") so the live-client persists their open state across SSE refreshes.",
      "testable": true
    }
  ]
}
US-17007 Product Map: lazy first-load payload AC1 draft

US-17007 - Product Map: lazy first-load payload

As a: a reviewer opening the review surface on a slow link

I want: an initial HTML payload well under 3 MB by rendering only the active grouping fully and hydrating the other groupings on demand from a partial endpoint

So that: first paint is fast and the tab stays interactive on 100-plus REQ trees

Description: a reviewer opening the review surface on a slow link the initial HTML payload well under 3 MB by rendering only the active grouping fully; the other three groupings emit only their bucket headings (label + count) and hydrate the REQ list on demand when the reader switches grouping or opens a bucket, so first paint is fast and the tab stays interactive on 100+ REQ trees

Requirement

REQ-170

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17007-1 - The Product Map first-load payload target is well under 3 MB. The server emits the shape (default) grouping fully; the other three groupings emit only their bucket headings (label + total count + per-status mini counts) and each bucket carries a data-pm-lazy marker naming its grouping and bucket id. When the reader switches to a lazy grouping OR opens a lazy bucket, the client fetches that grouping fully once (from a partial endpoint the server exposes) and hydrates the bucket into the DOM; subsequent switches use the cached partial. The pass doc states the before/after first-load bytes.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-192
