US-17008 Product Map: blueprint badge and by-blueprint grouping AC1 draft

US-17008 - Product Map: blueprint badge and by-blueprint grouping

As a: a product reader auditing what came from applied blueprints vs the project's own requirements

I want: a blueprint badge on every REQ row that was contributed by a blueprint plus a by-blueprint grouping (one bucket per applied blueprint plus an Application bucket) with capability as the second level inside each bucket

So that: I can see at a glance which parts of the tree ride on shared blueprints and which the project owns, and drill from a blueprint to the capabilities it contributed

Description: User story under REQ-170. a product reader auditing what came from applied blueprints vs the project's own requirements a visible blueprint badge on every REQ row an applied blueprint contributed, plus a sixth grouping that buckets requirements by contributing blueprint (with an Application bucket for the project's own (non-blueprint) REQs) and a second-level capability split inside each bucket.

Requirement

REQ-170

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17008-1 - Every REQ row inside the Product Map tab that was contributed by an applied blueprint carries a compact blueprint badge (class pm-blueprint-badge) in its summary row, in every grouping (shape, component, trace coverage, capability, and the new by-blueprint grouping itself). The GROUPINGS list on the panel additionally includes 'blueprint'; the by-blueprint grouping enumerates one bucket per entry in manifest.blueprints[] (label: the blueprint's display name or slug, count: number of contributed REQs) plus an Application bucket for the project's own (non-blueprint) REQs (REQs with no blueprint attribution). Inside each blueprint or Application bucket, requirements are split by capability (existing capability:<slug> convention) as a second level, then the usual REQ->US->AC drill-down. The source of truth for blueprint attribution is manifest.blueprints[].contributions[] (parsed by scope.contributionsForBlueprint); the id-prefix fallback (kebab-slug prefix on reqId) is used only when the manifest carries no contributions record for a given blueprint. The hash schema round-trips as #tab=product-map&group=blueprint&status=<s>&open=<ids>, and the /product-map/blueprint partial endpoint serves the grouping body for the client's lazy-render fetch. A project with no applied blueprints renders a single Application bucket cleanly (not an error, not an empty tab).

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-193

REQ-171 Capability tag convention on requirements requirementsAuthoring US2 AC2 draft

Requirements carry one or more capability slugs on their existing free-form tags array using the convention capability:<kebab-slug>. A capability taxonomy for the rcf-lite product itself is documented in the rcf-lite docs, alongside the rule for adding a new capability. This is a convention that rides on the shipped schema; no schema change. The Product Map by-capability grouping is the consumer that proves the convention works on real data.

Why: Analysis d-019 established that the shipped schema has no capability or feature level between PRD and REQ. The trial answers whether a lightweight convention on the existing tags array carries a usable product taxonomy without a schema change. If the tags and the by-capability view earn their keep, the capability level is promoted to a proper schema field later; if not, nothing was spent.

capability:requirements-authoring capability:review-surface capability-tags-trial

User stories (2)

US-17101 Dogfood chain carries capability tags on every requirement AC1 draft

US-17101 - Dogfood chain carries capability tags on every requirement

As a: the maintainer of the rcf-lite dogfood chain

I want: every REQ under rcf-lite/rcf to carry at least one capability:<slug> tag drawn from the documented taxonomy

So that: the by-capability Product Map view has something to bucket on, and the trial can be evaluated against real data rather than a fixture

Description: User story under REQ-171. the maintainer of the rcf-lite dogfood chain every REQ under rcf-lite/rcf to carry at least one capability:<slug> tag drawn from the documented taxonomy

Requirement

REQ-171

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17101-1 - Every REQ under packages/rcf-lite/rcf/requirements/ carries at least one tag matching the regex ^capability:[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$, and every slug used maps to an entry in the documented capability taxonomy.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-191

US-17102 Capability taxonomy is documented in the rcf-lite docs AC1 draft

US-17102 - Capability taxonomy is documented in the rcf-lite docs

As a: a reader of the rcf-lite docs deciding whether to adopt the convention

I want: the capability:<slug> convention, the initial taxonomy and the rule for adding a new capability documented alongside the rest of the rcf-lite docs

So that: a new capability is added deliberately rather than by drift, and a reader can look up what each slug means

Description: User story under REQ-171. a reader of the rcf-lite docs deciding whether to adopt the convention the capability:<slug> convention, the initial taxonomy and the rule for adding a new capability documented alongside the rest of the rcf-lite docs

Requirement

REQ-171

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17102-1 - packages/rcf-lite/docs contains a capability tags section listing every slug in the initial taxonomy with a one-line meaning, plus the rule for adding a new capability (single-word verb or noun, kebab-case, must map to a product surface). The section is linked from docs/README.md so it is reachable from the docs entry point.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-191

REQ-172 DEFINE delta detection and freeze record foundation defineDetection US1 AC4 draft

rcf-lite gains three pure primitives and one durable record. hashDocument returns a sha256:<hex> hash over the canonical JSON of a parsed document (keys sorted recursively, no whitespace). computeTreeHash hashes the sorted (id, docHash) pairs. computeDelta(tree, freeze, ledgers) returns the whole change model of the proposal (2026-09-22 v3) section 2.2: frozen, frozenAt, treeHash, currentTreeHash, changed, added, removed, briefSince, unchanged. docHashes cover every standalone document the walker exposes on tree.byId (PRD, TAD, BS, REQ, US, TAC, ADR, FBS, TS, CN, EVAL) plus one ledger:<name> entry per sidecar the caller passes in. Before the first freeze the delta is the whole tree (frozen false, everything in added). The freeze record itself sits at rcf/define/freeze.json (owned by rcf-lite, outside the shared rcf-schemas package until 0.7) with a small local schema and a reader/writer module: reading a missing file returns null, a malformed file raises a clear error. No rcf define freeze verb yet; the writer the verb will call is exposed for slice 3.

Why: Barry's backstory dogfood found DEFINE generated too fast with no gates. Baz ruled 2026-09-22 that the fix is detection over configured change records: the freeze remembers what the tree looked like; anything that differs is the change. The delta.js primitives are what every later slice (gates, readiness, freeze verb, bundle read, viewer tab) consumes, so their return shape is a contract worth pinning early. Canonical-JSON hashing (over raw bytes) is the difference between a real change and a hand reformat; document granularity (over criterion granularity) keeps the model cheap while git supplies the criterion-level diff.

capability:define-detection

User stories (1)

US-17201 Delta detection and freeze record land as reusable primitives AC4 draft

US-17201 - Delta detection and freeze record land as reusable primitives

As a: the maintainer of a rcf-lite tree

I want: hashDocument, computeTreeHash, computeDelta and the rcf/define/freeze.json reader/writer to land as pure modules exposed on the query surface, with a documented return shape that later DEFINE slices can call unchanged

So that: the gates, readiness view, freeze verb and bundle-side read all consume the same detection primitives, and a hand reformat of a document never surfaces as a change

Description: User story under REQ-172. The detection-model foundation lands as pure, importable modules and one durable local record.

Requirement

REQ-172

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17201-1 - computeDelta(tree, freeze, ledgers) returns the exact object shape proposal 2026-09-22 v3 section 2.2 specifies (frozen, frozenAt, treeHash, currentTreeHash, changed, added, removed, briefSince, unchanged); given a matching freeze the delta reports empty changed / added / removed and unchanged equal to the number of docHashes; given divergent tree state changed / added / removed classify every id correctly against the freeze record.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-194

  • AC-17201-2 - hashDocument returns a sha256:<64-hex> string over the canonical JSON form of the parsed document (keys sorted recursively, no whitespace), and is invariant under a whitespace-only reformat or a key reorder: two documents that parse to the same object hash identically.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-194

  • AC-17201-3 - Loading rcf/define/freeze.json when the file is absent returns null; loading a malformed file (bad JSON, missing docHashes, non-sha256 hash value, negative briefStatements) raises FreezeRecordError with a code (parseFailure or schemaFailure) and a named field so a caller can log the exact failure.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-194

  • AC-17201-4 - Saving then loading a freeze record round-trips every documented field including extension fields the schema does not police (counts, litmus, versions, note), and saveFreezeRecord refuses to persist an invalid record: no file is written on validation failure.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-194

REQ-173 Sidecar ledgers under rcf/define/ and the rcf define ledger verb defineLedgers US2 AC10 draft

Four sidecars live under rcf/define/, each one JSON file, each with one numbered sequence for the life of the project (proposal 2026-09-22 v3 section 2.5, 3.2, 8.2). Names and shapes: brief-ledger.json (statements[] kinded from a closed set), decisions-ledger.json (decisions[] in the numbered #241 format), concern-ledger.json (concerns[] with disposition applied or waived), probe-ledger.json (probes[] with severity low, medium, high). A local schema in rcf-lite validates every write until schemas 0.7. Reading a missing ledger file returns an empty ledger so callers can compose without a per-file null check; a malformed file raises a clear error. The rcf define ledger name verb pattern (brief, decisions, concerns, probes; add, resolve, list) is the operator surface. brief add --from <file> splits statements one per non-empty line, mints sequential ids and writes; the intake-scan-against-frozen-statements hook is a named seam this slice leaves for a later one. decisions list prints the #241 numbered format (one decision per item, options with letters, the default, what it blocks). The walker never reads under rcf/define/ so the sidecars stay invisible to every existing tree consumer. Every ledger supports `update <id>` with field patches validated as `add` validates; `resolvedBy` on a brief statement is a closed pointer grammar (REQ-nnn, TAD.entity:<name>, PRD.user:<name>, TAD.system:<name>, TAC-nnnn, omitted:<reason>) validated by D2.

Why: The proposal (2026-09-22 v3, section 8.2) makes ledgers the seam every later DEFINE stage draws from: D1 reads the brief ledger, D5 the concern ledger, D6 the probe ledger, D7 the decisions ledger, and D2's greenfield resolution walks the brief statements. Building the sidecars and the CLI now, before any gate reads them, keeps slice 2 free of write-side surprises. Baz's ruling of 2026-09-22 (decision 5) fixed the ownership: sidecars in rcf-lite until schemas 0.7 promotes them to manifest records. Precedent: .rcf/preflight-secrets.local.json is an rcf-lite-owned file outside the shared schema; rcf/define/ follows the same shape.

capability:define-ledgers

User stories (2)

US-17301 rcf define ledger reads and writes the four sidecars under rcf/define/ AC4 draft

US-17301 - rcf define ledger reads and writes the four sidecars under rcf/define/

As a: an operator staging or reviewing a DEFINE change

I want: rcf define ledger to author brief statements, decisions, concern dispositions and probe findings under rcf/define/ with numbered ids stable for the life of the project, and to leave every ledger invisible to the walker

So that: the freeze record's high-water mark, the D7 decisions list, D5 concern coverage and D6 probe findings all have a written record and every later DEFINE slice reads the same seam without discovering a second source of truth

Description: User story under REQ-173. The operator-facing CLI for the four sidecar ledgers lands with add / resolve / list on every ledger name.

Requirement

REQ-173

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17301-1 - rcf define ledger brief add --kind <k> --text <t> appends a numbered statement to rcf/define/brief-ledger.json, mints the next id (highest current + 1), stamps status open and addedAt (ISO-8601), refuses an unknown kind with a usage-class error, and refuses --text combined with --from with a usage-class error.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-195

  • AC-17301-2 - rcf define ledger decisions list prints the numbered #241 format: one decision per item (id. question), options rendered as 'letter) text', the default letter labelled 'default:', and what it blocks labelled 'blocks:'. rcf define ledger <name> list --json emits the machine-readable envelope { ledger, <arrayKey>: [...] }.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-195

  • AC-17301-3 - rcf define ledger brief add --from <file> reads the file, splits it into one statement per non-empty line (stripping leading '- ', '* ' or '<n>. ' bullets), mints sequential ids for every statement, refuses if the file produced zero non-empty lines, and stamps the file path as source unless --source overrides it. The intake-scan-against-frozen-statements hook is a named seam in the writer, not called in this slice.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-195

  • AC-17301-4 - walkTree run over a project that carries rcf/define/freeze.json, all four ledger files, and a bug-bait file named req-999.json under rcf/define/ never surfaces any rcf/define/ file as a tree.byId document and reports no walker error naming a rcf/define/ path. The sidecar directory is invisible to every consumer of walkTree.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-195

US-17302 update and the pointer grammar AC6 draft

US-17302 - update and the pointer grammar

As a: harness

I want: to patch a statement's kind, text or resolution

So that: a correction does not mint a duplicate

Description: User story under REQ-173. Every ledger supports `update <id>` with field patches validated as `add` validates; `resolvedBy` on a brief statement is a closed pointer grammar validated by D2.

Requirement

REQ-173

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17302-1 - [happy] given statement 7, when rcf define ledger brief update 7 --kind constraint --resolved-by REQ-003 runs, then the statement carries kind constraint and resolvedBy REQ-003 and its id and addedAt are unchanged.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-17302-2 - [happy] given decision 2 with one option, when rcf define ledger decisions update 2 --option a:x --option b:y --default a runs, then decisions:wellFormed passes it.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-17302-3 - [happy] given each pointer form REQ-nnn, TAD.entity:<name>, PRD.user:<name>, TAD.system:<name>, TAC-nnnn and omitted:<reason> resolving on the fixture, when D2 runs, then skeleton:resolvedBy passes the statement.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-17302-4 - [failure] given --resolved-by "loan thing", when update runs, then it exits 2 naming the grammar and writes nothing.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-17302-5 - [failure] given --resolved-by REQ-999 on a tree with no REQ-999, when D2 runs, then skeleton:resolvedBy fails the statement with "pointer does not resolve".

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-17302-6 - [must-not] given a statement whose text contains an existing REQ title and no resolvedBy, when D2 runs in 0.30.0, then skeleton:resolvedBy does not pass it on the title hit.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  "description": "Four sidecars live under rcf/define/, each one JSON file, each with one numbered sequence for the life of the project (proposal 2026-09-22 v3 section 2.5, 3.2, 8.2). Names and shapes: brief-ledger.json (statements[] kinded from a closed set), decisions-ledger.json (decisions[] in the numbered #241 format), concern-ledger.json (concerns[] with disposition applied or waived), probe-ledger.json (probes[] with severity low, medium, high). A local schema in rcf-lite validates every write until schemas 0.7. Reading a missing ledger file returns an empty ledger so callers can compose without a per-file null check; a malformed file raises a clear error. The rcf define ledger name verb pattern (brief, decisions, concerns, probes; add, resolve, list) is the operator surface. brief add --from <file> splits statements one per non-empty line, mints sequential ids and writes; the intake-scan-against-frozen-statements hook is a named seam this slice leaves for a later one. decisions list prints the #241 numbered format (one decision per item, options with letters, the default, what it blocks). The walker never reads under rcf/define/ so the sidecars stay invisible to every existing tree consumer. Every ledger supports `update <id>` with field patches validated as `add` validates; `resolvedBy` on a brief statement is a closed pointer grammar (REQ-nnn, TAD.entity:<name>, PRD.user:<name>, TAD.system:<name>, TAC-nnnn, omitted:<reason>) validated by D2.",

REQ-174 DEFINE stage gates D1..D8 as pure check functions defineDetection US3 AC25 draft

rcf-lite gains src/query/gates.js with one check function per stage D1..D8. Each function takes (tree, ledgers, profile, scope) and returns { stage, gate, state, checks[] } where every check is { name, ok, over: 'delta'|'tree', pass, total, failing: [{ id, why }] }. Stage state is 'passed' | 'failing' | 'acknowledged' (only for D3, D5, D6 and only when the freeze record acknowledges that gate at the current hash) | 'notApplicable' (the stage decides that itself from the scope per the proposal 2026-09-22 v3 section 3.2 rules and the summary table in section 2.7). Blocking in 0.29.0: D1 brief, D2 skeleton, D4 floors (every REQ in scope has a US; every US in scope has a testable AC, a failure AC and a must-not AC, or a reasoned opt-out per class; tacIds non-empty and resolving; no scaffold placeholder), D7 decisions, D8 freeze (prior gates passed or acknowledged at the current hash, every AC owned by exactly one FBS, queue head actionable and not a placeholder, validate clean; preflight and ui-baseline presence as the section 3.2 rules specify). Warn-with-ack in 0.29.0: D3, D5, D6 build only the cheap data-backed checks (D3: every TAC in scope has at least one interface and each interface kind is in the closed vocabulary of section 5.2; D5: TAD securityArchitecture present when any auth or httpApi REQ exists, operationalConcerns present when deployed-scope ACs exist, concern-ledger entries applied or waived where they exist; D6: validate clean tree-wide plus open probe-ledger count). The D3 template parser, entity join, D5 catalogue, D6 contradiction and unsatisfiable scans, and the probe runner are 0.30 and left as named seams. AC class is a bracketed prefix on AC description ('[failure] ...', '[must-not] ...', '[happy]', '[edge]', '[non-functional]', decision 6); opt-out per class reuses the existing manifest.baselineAcOptOuts[] array with a baselineKey of the shape 'defineD4:failure' or 'defineD4:mustNot' (recorded in ADR-4122). No storage state, no 'stale' state. ADR-4126 (0.29.0) amendment: every gate check declares an owning persona, `productOwner` or `engineer`, and a one-sentence `question` in that persona’s register. A check that would need both personas is split so every check is homogeneous: `skeleton:reqFields` becomes `skeleton:reqIntent` (productOwner: description + domain) + `skeleton:reqShape` (engineer: shapeClassification.shapes); `decisions:allAnswered` becomes `decisions:wellFormed` (productOwner: enumerated per #241 format) + `decisions:allAnswered` (engineer: zero open). A new D3 check `shapes:draftSettled` fails every interface whose description still carries the leading `[draft]` marker so an L1-pre-populated interface stays distinguishable from one the engineer has settled.

Why: Baz ruled on 2026-09-22 (proposal section 9, decision 2) that gates block where the data exists and warn-with-ack for D3, D5 and D6 until 0.31 (Baz ruled 2026-09-24 that 0.31 renumbers to 0.30, so this train ships D3/D5/D6 as warn-with-ack in 0.29.0). One check function per stage is the seam every later consumer reads: the readiness view (REQ-175) composes them, the freeze verb (slice 3) refuses on any failing stage, the viewer's Readiness tab (slice 5) prints the same checks[]. Building the check functions now, with cheap data-backed checks only, keeps 0.29.0 shippable while leaving named seams for 0.30's template parser, entity join, catalogue walk, probe runner and consistency scans.

capability:define-detection

User stories (3)

US-17401 Stage gates land as pure check functions with per-stage state AC10 draft

US-17401 - Stage gates land as pure check functions with per-stage state

As a: a downstream consumer of DEFINE gates (readiness, freeze, viewer)

I want: gates.js to expose one pure check function per stage D1..D8, each returning a { stage, gate, state, checks[] } object with checks in the { name, ok, over: 'delta'|'tree', pass, total, failing: [{ id, why }] } shape

So that: computeReadiness composes the eight checks, the freeze verb refuses on any failing state, and the viewer's Readiness tab prints the same rows the CLI does with no schema translation

Description: User story under REQ-174. Eight stage-gate check functions land in src/query/gates.js with a stable per-stage return shape that computeReadiness and every later slice can consume unchanged.

Requirement

REQ-174

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17401-1 - src/query/gates.js exports one check function per stage D1..D8 (checkD1Brief, checkD2Skeleton, checkD3Shapes, checkD4Stories, checkD5Crosscut, checkD6Consistency, checkD7Decisions, checkD8Freeze), each taking (tree, { ledgers, profile, scope, freeze, delta, validateErrors, probeOpenCount, coverageTree }) and returning { stage, gate, state, checks[] }; every entry in checks is { name, ok, over: 'delta'|'tree', pass, total, failing: [{ id, why }] } (failing empty on ok).

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-196

  • AC-17401-2 - Blocking stages in 0.29.0 (D1, D2, D4, D7, D8) report state 'passed' when every check ok is true, 'failing' when any check ok is false; warn-with-ack stages (D3, D5, D6) report 'passed' when every check ok is true, 'failing' when any check ok is false and the freeze record does NOT acknowledge that gate at the current tree hash, and 'acknowledged' when the freeze.gates[<gate>] entry names state 'acknowledged' and at.hash === currentTreeHash and any check ok is false.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-196

  • AC-17401-3 - notApplicable is decided per stage per proposal section 3.2: D2 notApplicable when no statement of a resolving kind (capability, constraint, entity, actor, externalSystem, surface) is in the delta AND no REQ, PRD or TAD is in scope; D3 notApplicable when no TAC and no shaped REQ (httpApi/persistence/auth) is in scope; D5 notApplicable when no REQ is in scope; D7 notApplicable when no open decisions exist AND the profile sets skipReviewFor: singleDocument AND the delta holds exactly one document; D4 and D6 use their own rules; D1 and D8 never notApplicable.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-196

  • AC-17401-4 - checkD4Stories enforces the D4 floors: every REQ in scope has a US (fail: 'no owning user story'), every US in scope has a testable AC ('missing testable AC'), a failure AC (parsed by the bracketed [failure] prefix on AC description) or a reasoned opt-out per class (manifest.baselineAcOptOuts[] entry with baselineKey 'defineD4:failure' and matching scope), a must-not AC (parsed by [must-not] prefix) or a reasoned opt-out per class (baselineKey 'defineD4:mustNot'), tacIds non-empty and every named tac resolving to a real TAC, and no AC description contains the scaffold TODO placeholder.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-196

  • AC-17401-5 - checkD3Shapes runs only cheap data-backed checks in 0.29.0: every TAC in scope has at least one interface (fail: 'no interfaces authored'), and every interface's kind is in the closed vocabulary { recordShape, httpRoute, event, cliCommand, uiRoute, port, fileFormat, fixture, other } (fail: 'unknown interface kind <k>'). The template parser, entity-name join, ownerRef and path resolution are named seams (not called this slice) and D3 stays warn-with-ack.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-196

  • AC-17401-6 - checkD5Crosscut runs only cheap data-backed checks in 0.29.0: TAD.securityArchitecture non-empty when the tree carries any REQ whose shapeClassification.shapes includes 'auth' or 'httpApi'; TAD.operationalConcerns non-empty when any AC description carries the '[deployed]' marker (a cheap presence signal proposal section 3.2 D5 lists as 'deployed-scope AC'); concern-ledger entries in scope disposed as 'applied' or 'waived' (no dangling 'open' concerns on REQs in scope). The full catalogue and per-pair enumeration are named seams for 0.30.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-196

  • AC-17401-7 - checkD6Consistency runs only cheap data-backed checks in 0.29.0: validate is clean tree-wide (validateErrors is empty; the caller passes the walker + validator's error list), and probe-ledger holds zero 'open' probe entries. Contradiction-lite, unsatisfiable-lite, duplicates and orphan-interface scans, plus the probe runner, are named seams for 0.30.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-196

  • AC-17401-8 - checkD8Freeze enforces the tree-wide gate: every prior stage state (D1..D7 as computeReadiness composes them) is passed or acknowledged at the current hash; every AC id in the tree is bound by exactly one FBS (walker's fbsByAcId map has length 1); the queue head (computeQueue.nextActionable) is not null; validateErrors is empty. The stage is never notApplicable.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-196

  • AC-17401-9 - checkD2Skeleton reads tad.dataArchitecture.dataStores and tad.dataArchitecture.coreEntities (not top-level) when evaluating skeleton:tadPersistence; a tree whose TAD places both arrays under dataArchitecture per rcf-schemas 0.6.3 passes the check and a tree with the arrays missing or empty under dataArchitecture fails with { id: 'TAD.dataArchitecture.dataStores' } / { id: 'TAD.dataArchitecture.coreEntities' }.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-196

  • AC-17401-10 - src/setup/identity-seed.js IDENTITY_TEMPLATE seeds a '## Surface' section containing one line that is one of 'viewer' | 'runningApp' | 'prDiff' (default 'prDiff' with explanatory text matching the Register section's style) so that a project immediately after 'rcf init' passes checkD1Brief's profile:surface check without further operator action. The seed stays idempotent (an existing profile.md is left byte-identical, per the slice-1 'kept' contract).

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-196

US-17402 Persona tag on every gate check AC7 draft

US-17402 - Persona tag on every gate check

As a: an engineer reading a readiness report

I want: every failing check to say whose question it is

So that: product-owner questions reach the product owner and engineering gaps stay with me

Description: User story under REQ-174. Every entry in stages[].checks[] carries an owning persona (productOwner | engineer) declared in code next to the check, so readiness consumers (the CLI, the viewer tab, delivery-stream artefacts) can route a failing check to whoever is actually blocked.

Requirement

REQ-174

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17402-1 - [happy] Given any tree, when readiness is computed, then every entry in stages[].checks[] carries persona equal to 'productOwner' or 'engineer' and a non-empty question string.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17402-2 - [happy] Given the D1 checks, when readiness is computed, then brief:sinceFreeze, brief:kinds, brief:openQuestions and brief:profile carry persona 'productOwner'.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17402-3 - [happy] Given the D2 checks, when readiness is computed, then skeleton:resolvedBy and skeleton:reqIntent carry persona 'productOwner' and skeleton:reqShape, skeleton:tadPersistence and skeleton:deployAdr carry persona 'engineer'.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17402-4 - [happy] Given the D4 and D7 checks, when readiness is computed, then stories:reqHasUs and decisions:wellFormed carry persona 'productOwner' and stories:usFloors and decisions:allAnswered carry persona 'engineer'.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17402-5 - [happy] Given the D3, D5, D6 and D8 checks, when readiness is computed, then every check carries persona 'engineer'.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17402-6 - [must-not] Given any check, when readiness is computed, then no check carries a persona value other than 'productOwner' or 'engineer', and no failing item carries its own persona.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17402-7 - [failure] Given a notApplicable stage, when readiness is computed, then its stage:<D>:scope placeholder check carries the stage's STAGE_FALLBACK_PERSONA and ok true.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

US-17403 Split heterogeneous checks and detect the D3 draft marker AC8 draft

US-17403 - Split heterogeneous checks and detect the D3 draft marker

As a: an engineer

I want: the mixed checks split and a draft interface distinguishable from a settled one

So that: a shape the L1 agent pre-populated never reads as my finished work

Description: User story under REQ-174. skeleton:reqFields and decisions:allAnswered split into homogeneous checks (per persona), and a new D3 shapes:draftSettled flags any interface whose description still carries the leading [draft] marker. L1 pre-populated shapes stay distinguishable from engineer-settled ones.

Requirement

REQ-174

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17403-1 - [happy] Given a REQ in scope with a TODO description and no shapeClassification, when D2 runs, then skeleton:reqIntent fails the REQ for the description and skeleton:reqShape fails the same REQ for the missing shapes.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17403-2 - [happy] Given a REQ in scope with a description and shapes but no domain, when D2 runs, then skeleton:reqIntent fails the REQ with 'domain missing' and skeleton:reqShape passes it.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17403-3 - [happy] Given a TAC in scope whose only interface description starts with [draft], when D3 runs, then shapes:tacHasInterface passes the TAC and shapes:draftSettled fails <tacId>:<name> with 'draft interface pre-populated at L1, not yet settled'.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17403-4 - [happy] Given the same TAC after the [draft] marker is removed, when D3 runs, then shapes:draftSettled passes it.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17403-5 - [failure] Given a [draft] interface whose kind is not in INTERFACE_KINDS, when D3 runs, then shapes:kindVocabulary fails it exactly as it would a settled interface.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17403-6 - [happy] Given a decisions ledger with one open entry that has a question, two options and a default, when D7 runs, then decisions:wellFormed passes and decisions:allAnswered fails the entry.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  "description": "rcf-lite gains src/query/gates.js with one check function per stage D1..D8. Each function takes (tree, ledgers, profile, scope) and returns { stage, gate, state, checks[] } where every check is { name, ok, over: 'delta'|'tree', pass, total, failing: [{ id, why }] }. Stage state is 'passed' | 'failing' | 'acknowledged' (only for D3, D5, D6 and only when the freeze record acknowledges that gate at the current hash) | 'notApplicable' (the stage decides that itself from the scope per the proposal 2026-09-22 v3 section 3.2 rules and the summary table in section 2.7). Blocking in 0.29.0: D1 brief, D2 skeleton, D4 floors (every REQ in scope has a US; every US in scope has a testable AC, a failure AC and a must-not AC, or a reasoned opt-out per class; tacIds non-empty and resolving; no scaffold placeholder), D7 decisions, D8 freeze (prior gates passed or acknowledged at the current hash, every AC owned by exactly one FBS, queue head actionable and not a placeholder, validate clean; preflight and ui-baseline presence as the section 3.2 rules specify). Warn-with-ack in 0.29.0: D3, D5, D6 build only the cheap data-backed checks (D3: every TAC in scope has at least one interface and each interface kind is in the closed vocabulary of section 5.2; D5: TAD securityArchitecture present when any auth or httpApi REQ exists, operationalConcerns present when deployed-scope ACs exist, concern-ledger entries applied or waived where they exist; D6: validate clean tree-wide plus open probe-ledger count). The D3 template parser, entity join, D5 catalogue, D6 contradiction and unsatisfiable scans, and the probe runner are 0.30 and left as named seams. AC class is a bracketed prefix on AC description ('[failure] ...', '[must-not] ...', '[happy]', '[edge]', '[non-functional]', decision 6); opt-out per class reuses the existing manifest.baselineAcOptOuts[] array with a baselineKey of the shape 'defineD4:failure' or 'defineD4:mustNot' (recorded in ADR-4122). No storage state, no 'stale' state. ADR-4126 (0.29.0) amendment: every gate check declares an owning persona, `productOwner` or `engineer`, and a one-sentence `question` in that persona’s register. A check that would need both personas is split so every check is homogeneous: `skeleton:reqFields` becomes `skeleton:reqIntent` (productOwner: description + domain) + `skeleton:reqShape` (engineer: shapeClassification.shapes); `decisions:allAnswered` becomes `decisions:wellFormed` (productOwner: enumerated per #241 format) + `decisions:allAnswered` (engineer: zero open). A new D3 check `shapes:draftSettled` fails every interface whose description still carries the leading `[draft]` marker so an L1-pre-populated interface stays distinguishable from one the engineer has settled.",

REQ-175 computeReadiness and the rcf define readiness CLI verb defineDetection US3 AC23 draft

rcf-lite gains src/query/readiness.js with computeReadiness(tree, { freeze, ledgers, profile, testPointers }) returning the exact section 2.4 shape { tree, delta, stages, nextAction, coverage, decisions, freezeable }. computeReadiness composes computeDelta (slice 1), calls computeImpact once per id in changed union added (the union is the fan-out; impacted names every id, impactedFbs names the re-execute subset), runs the gates D1..D8 over scope = changed union added union impacted ids, calls computeCoverage tree-wide plus per REQ ancestor of the delta (using the testPointers map the CLI produces exactly as src/cli/coverage.js builds it), lists open decisions (in the #241 numbered format from the decisions ledger), derives a nextAction { stage, check, ids, command } from the first failing gate, and reports freezeable when every stage state is passed, acknowledged or notApplicable. rcf-lite also gains src/cli/readiness.js implementing rcf define readiness [--json] [--check <stage>|all] (stage accepts D1..D8 or the gate short name: brief, skeleton, shapes, stories, crosscut, consistency, decisions, freeze). Text output: tree line, next action, stage chips, delta list, failing items. --check exits 0 green, 4 red (matching coverage refusal exit); warn-with-ack stages failing but unacknowledged exit 0 with a visible warning. The producer is wrapped with runWithAdmissibilityGate as the ruleset toolScope requires. loadAllLedgers (src/define/ledgers.js) is corrected so a project that never authored a ledger does not get ledger:<name> hashes in the docHashes map (slice-1 P3 resolution: code and JSDoc agree that absent ledger files contribute no docHash). ADR-4126 (0.29.0) amendment: the readiness object carries two computed levels on the one ladder. `levels.intentComplete.ok` is true when every `productOwner` check is ok across every stage (stage state ignored); `levels.readyToBuild.ok` equals `freezeable`. Neither is recorded. `personas.productOwner.blockers` deep-equals `levels.intentComplete.blockedBy`; `personas.engineer.blockers` is the failing engineer checks in failing stages. `deriveNextAction(stages, persona?)` gains an optional persona filter; the productOwner next-action command carries `--level intent`. `formatVerdictLines(result)` builds the two verdict strings the CLI (PR B) and the Readiness tab (PR C) share so they cannot disagree.

Why: Baz ruled on 2026-09-22 (proposal section 2.4, section 6, section 9 decision 4) that Readiness is one object rendered by two consumers (the CLI and the viewer tab) so the two cannot disagree. The Product Map precedent (PR #238) established the shape: one pure compute, one JSON envelope, two renderers. computeReadiness is the object; rcf define readiness is the CLI twin the viewer tab (REQ-180, slice 5) will render unchanged. Slice 3 (rcf define freeze) reads freezeable and the per-stage state and refuses on any failing stage; slice 4's bundle --next reads the same object; slice 6's guidance points at the CLI as the one 'am I ready to build' surface. Fixing the slice-1 P3 in the same slice as the reader that consumes it keeps the ledger docHash contract single-sourced before it stabilises across the fleet.

capability:define-detection

User stories (3)

US-17501 computeReadiness and rcf define readiness render the same object AC6 draft

US-17501 - computeReadiness and rcf define readiness render the same object

As a: an operator asking 'can I build, and if not what is in the way'

I want: one pure compute that composes delta, fan-out, gates, coverage and decisions into a single object, and one CLI that prints it in a compact form or emits it as JSON

So that: the tree line, next action, stage chips, delta list and failing items are the same wherever they are shown, and slice 3's rcf define freeze refuses on the same freezeable flag the CLI reports

Description: User story under REQ-175. computeReadiness lands as a pure module and rcf define readiness as its CLI twin. The viewer's Readiness tab (slice 5) will render the same object with no schema translation.

Requirement

REQ-175

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17501-1 - computeReadiness(tree, { freeze, ledgers, profile, testPointers }) returns the exact section 2.4 shape: tree { frozen, frozenAt, treeHash, currentTreeHash, buildAt, fbsTotal }, delta { changed, added, removed, briefSince, impacted, impactedFbs }, stages [{ stage, gate, state, checks }], nextAction { stage, check, ids, command } or null, coverage { tree, delta }, decisions [...open in #241 format], freezeable boolean. freezeable is true when every stage state is 'passed', 'acknowledged' or 'notApplicable'.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-197

  • AC-17501-2 - Fan-out is computed by calling computeImpact once per id in the union of changed and added; impacted is the union of every impact node id excluding the pivots; impactedFbs is the subset whose kind is 'fbs' and actionNeeded is 're-execute'. Gates run over scope = changed union added union impacted (with duplicates removed).

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-197

  • AC-17501-3 - Coverage is tree-wide plus per REQ ancestor of the delta: coverage.tree is computeCoverage(tree, { testPointers, strict: true }) once over the whole tree; coverage.delta is an array with one CoverageResult per unique REQ id reachable by walking back from every delta id (changed union added) through parentByChild until the reqId is found, using scopeId per invocation. testPointers is the map the CLI produced with resolveTestPointers.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-197

  • AC-17501-4 - nextAction picks the first stage in D1..D8 order whose state is 'failing', then the first failing check in that stage's checks[] (or the check with the largest failing.length when tie); it names the stage id, the check name, the failing ids (deduped), and a command string like 'rcf define readiness --check <stage-short-name> after editing'. nextAction is null when every stage is passed / acknowledged / notApplicable.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-197

  • AC-17501-5 - rcf define readiness prints a text summary: the tree line ('Frozen at <shortHash> on <frozenAt>. N documents changed since, M impacted. Build at <fbsId> of <total>; K FBS impacted.' or 'Unfrozen. N documents; the whole tree is the delta.'), the next action line, a chip line 'D1:passed D2:failing D3:acknowledged D4:notApplicable ...', and the failing-items list per stage. --json emits the full computeReadiness object under `${JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)}\n`. --check <stage> (D1..D8 or short name brief|skeleton|shapes|stories|crosscut|consistency|decisions|freeze) prints only that stage and exits 0 when its state is 'passed' or 'acknowledged' or 'notApplicable', exit 4 on 'failing' for blocking stages (D1, D2, D4, D7, D8), exit 0 with a visible '[warn]' line on 'failing' for warn-with-ack stages (D3, D5, D6). The verb wraps its producer with runWithAdmissibilityGate and, on admissibility refusal, prints the refusal on stderr and exits 4.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-197

  • AC-17501-6 - loadAllLedgers({ projectRoot }) returns a LedgerBundle that OMITS a ledger key when the sidecar file does not exist (ENOENT), so computeDelta records no docHash for absent ledgers; the docstring on computeDelta (LedgerBundle typedef) and the loader implementation agree. A project that has authored a brief ledger and no others sees exactly one 'ledger:brief' entry in the delta docHashes; a project that has authored no ledgers sees zero 'ledger:*' entries.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-197

US-17502 Two levels folded on one readiness object AC8 draft

US-17502 - Two levels folded on one readiness object

As a: a delivery stream

I want: `rcf define readiness --level intent --json` at a tree hash to be the artefact that says the product owner's part is done

So that: I can pick a tree up without a hand-over meeting

Description: User story under REQ-175. computeReadiness folds levels (intentComplete, readyToBuild) and personas (productOwner, engineer) from stages[].checks[] on every read; nothing new is written. The `rcf define readiness --level intent --json` output at a tree hash is the artefact a delivery stream picks up.

Requirement

REQ-175

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17502-1 - [happy] Given a tree where every productOwner check is ok and at least one engineer check fails, when readiness is computed, then levels.intentComplete.ok is true and levels.readyToBuild.ok is false.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17502-2 - [happy] Given a tree where freezeable is true, when readiness is computed, then levels.readyToBuild.ok is true and levels.intentComplete.ok is true.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17502-3 - [failure] Given a tree where brief:profile fails, when readiness is computed, then levels.intentComplete.ok is false and levels.intentComplete.blockedBy holds one blocker for D1 brief:profile with persona productOwner and ids profile:surface and profile:register.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17502-4 - [happy] Given a D3 stage acknowledged at the current hash with a failing engineer check, when readiness is computed, then that check is absent from levels.readyToBuild.blockedBy.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17502-5 - [happy] Given any tree, when readiness is computed, then personas.productOwner.blockers deep-equals levels.intentComplete.blockedBy and levels.readyToBuild.nextAction deep-equals nextAction.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17502-6 - [happy] Given failing engineer checks in D2 and D4 and a failing productOwner check in D4 only, when readiness is computed, then personas.productOwner.nextAction names D4 and personas.engineer.nextAction names D2.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17502-7 - [must-not] Given any invocation of `rcf define readiness`, when it completes, then no file under rcf/ has been created or modified.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

  • AC-17502-8 - [must-not] Given the 0.28.4 JSON consumer fields (tree, delta, stages, nextAction, coverage, decisions, freezeable), when readiness is emitted under 0.29.0, then every one of them is present with its 0.28.4 type.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-199

US-17503 Level and persona flags on rcf define readiness AC9 draft

US-17503 - Level and persona flags on rcf define readiness

As a: an operator

I want: --level intent|build and --persona on rcf define readiness

So that: a script exits on the verdict it cares about and a person sees their own questions first

Description: User story under REQ-175. The verb exposes the two levels folded in US-17502 through --level intent|build and groups the text report by persona via --persona productOwner|engineer. --level drives the exit code against levels.<which>.ok (stricter than --check all on warn-with-ack failures per ADR-4126 and decision 4 of the step 2 spec); --persona is a display filter and never affects the exit code or JSON content. The JSON gains a _meta.level marker when --level is set; both verdict lines always print at the top of the text report. See the DEFINE step 2 persona-levels spec dated 2026-10-01 (section 3) for the full flag table and exit matrix.

Requirement

REQ-175

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17503-1 - [happy] Given no --level and no --check, when the verb runs on a failing tree, then it prints both verdict lines and exits 0.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-200

  • AC-17503-2 - [happy] Given --level intent on a tree where only engineer checks fail, when the verb runs, then it prints 'Intent-complete: yes.' and exits 0.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-200

  • AC-17503-3 - [failure] Given --level intent on a tree where a productOwner check fails, when the verb runs, then it exits 4.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-200

  • AC-17503-4 - [failure] Given --level build on a tree with an unacknowledged D3 failure and every blocking stage passed, when the verb runs, then it prints the [warn] line and exits 4.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-200

  • AC-17503-5 - [happy] Given --check all on the same tree, when the verb runs, then it exits 0, unchanged from 0.28.4.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-200

  • AC-17503-6 - [happy] Given --persona productOwner, when the verb runs in text mode, then the engineer block is one line with its check count and the exit code is the same as without the flag.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-200

  • AC-17503-7 - [failure] Given --level ship or --persona architect, when the verb runs, then it exits 2 with a usage line naming the accepted values.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-200

  • AC-17503-8 - [happy] Given --json --level intent, when the verb runs, then _meta.level is 'intent' and the object carries levels and personas.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-200

  • AC-17503-9 - [happy] Given the text report on a failing tree, when it renders, then the product-owner block precedes the engineer block and each failing check line carries its persona inside the parenthesis after over.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-200

REQ-176 rcf define freeze verb writes freeze.json and closes the change defineDetection US1 AC8 draft

rcf-lite gains src/cli/freeze.js implementing 'rcf define freeze [--ack <gate> --reason <text>]... [--litmus-attested <D3,D6>] [--note <text>] [--status] [--json]'. The verb runs computeReadiness (REQ-175) once over the live tree, freeze record and four ledgers; refuses with exit 4 when any stage state is 'failing' after applying any --ack argument, printing the failing gates and their first failing ids; and, on success, writes rcf/define/freeze.json via saveFreezeRecord (REQ-172) with { frozenAt, treeHash, docHashes, briefStatements, gates, counts, litmus, versions, note, override } and prints the proposal section 2.5 one-line summary derived from the pre-freeze delta ('frozen at <short treeHash>: <n> REQ, <n> stories, <n> criteria, <n> interfaces added; <ids> amended; ...'; first freeze reports 'first freeze: <whole-tree counts>'). --ack is accepted only for the three warn-with-ack gates (define.shapes, define.crosscut, define.consistency; short names shapes / crosscut / consistency; readiness's stage aliases); ack on any other gate is a usage refusal (exit 2), ack without --reason is a usage refusal. An acked gate lands in freeze.gates as { state: 'acknowledged', at: { hash: <currentTreeHash>, reason: <text> }, failing: [<id>, ...] }. --litmus-attested records the operator's per-decision attestation (Baz decision 7: default { attestedAt: [], readers: 0 }); the numbered --litmus <n> dispatch is NOT built (slice-6 seam). counts derives req/us/ac/tac/adr/fbs from tree.byId groupings, acByClass by parsing bracketed class markers on AC.description, and interfaces by kind from every TAC's interfaces[]. versions reads rcfLite from package.json, ruleset from src/ruleset/ruleset.json, and schemas from the installed @stravica-ai/rcf-schemas. --status prints the current freeze record (short hash, frozenAt, note, counts, acknowledged gates + reasons, litmus, versions, override) plus the live delta summary; --status --json emits the record and computeDelta object. The producer is wrapped with runWithAdmissibilityGate (ADR-4123: refusal is informational, the freeze still runs). Same slice: (a) src/define/freeze-record.js is corrected so the local schema requires override as a nullable field and every writer stamps override: null on a fresh freeze; loadFreezeRecord tolerates older records that lack the key by defaulting to null on load; (b) the ' -- ' double-dash in the readiness CLI stage header and the CHANGELOG regex line is replaced with a colon.

Why: Baz ruled on 2026-09-22 (proposal section 2.5) that closing a change is freezing again: the freeze verb is the only close verb, nothing is minted, and the one-line summary is what the operator signs off. Slice 3 is the smallest coherent seam between the pieces slices 1 and 2 built (delta, freeze-record writer, gates, computeReadiness) and the readers slices 4 and 5 will add (bundle --next, viewer Readiness tab). Warn-with-ack ack is accepted only on D3 / D5 / D6 per proposal section 9 decision 2 (Baz 2026-09-24) so the escape hatch matches the fold rule in gates.js. The freeze verb is also the only writer of freeze.gates and freeze.litmus, so writing them in the same slice that ships the writer keeps the record's schema surface single-sourced before slice 4 reads it. Bundling the slice-1 override-nullable P3 and the double-dash hygiene here is the same reasoning: the freeze verb is now the only writer of the record, so making override always-written is a one-touch change; the readiness CLI header's ' -- ' pattern is a small blast radius carried across the slice boundary.

capability:define-detection

User stories (1)

US-17601 rcf define freeze runs readiness, refuses on failing, writes freeze.json and prints the section 2.5 summary AC8 draft

US-17601 - rcf define freeze runs readiness, refuses on failing, writes freeze.json and prints the section 2.5 summary

As a: an operator wrapping up a change on the tree

I want: one command that says 'yes freezeable and I have written the record' or 'no here is the gate that blocks and its first failing ids', accepts --ack on the three warn-first gates with a mandatory reason, and prints a summary line I can paste into a commit message

So that: the freeze record is authoritative for slice 4's bundle --next and slice 5's viewer, and the same rules that gate readiness also gate the freeze

Description: User story under REQ-176. The freeze verb is the only close verb: no change-object is minted, nothing else changes state. It reads the live tree via computeReadiness, refuses on any failing stage (accepting acks only on the three warn-with-ack gates), and writes the freeze record slice 4's bundle --next and slice 5's viewer will read.

Requirement

REQ-176

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-17601-1 - [happy] rcf define freeze runs computeReadiness once over walkTree(projectRoot) plus loadFreezeRecord and loadAllLedgers. When result.freezeable is true, it writes rcf/define/freeze.json via saveFreezeRecord with these fields: frozenAt (ISO UTC now), treeHash (result.tree.currentTreeHash), docHashes (delta.js currentHashes over the live tree plus 'ledger:<name>' for each ledger present), briefStatements (the count of statements in the brief ledger, ledgers.brief.statements.length or 0), gates (one entry per stage-gate with { state, at: { hash, at, reason?, by? } | null, failing: [{ id, why }] } from the live readiness plus any --ack entries), counts { req, us, ac, acByClass: { happy, edge, failure, mustNot, nonFunctional, unclassified }, tac, interfaces: { <kind>: n, ... }, adr, fbs }, litmus { attestedAt, readers: 0 }, versions { rcfLite, ruleset, schemas } read from package.json, src/ruleset/ruleset.json and node_modules/@stravica-ai/rcf-schemas/package.json, note (--note argument or null), override (always null on a fresh freeze). The verb exits 0. Immediately after the write, calling computeDelta over the live tree + the new freeze reports every list empty (changed / added / removed / briefSince).

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-198

  • AC-17601-2 - [failure] When result.freezeable is false and no --ack argument covers the failing stage, the verb exits 4 without writing the freeze record. It prints the failing gates (one per line: '<stage> (<gate>): failing (<first check name>); failing ids: <id1>, <id2>, ...' capped at 20 ids per gate) to stderr, followed by the exact rcf define readiness --check <shortName> command that will re-print the same block for each failing stage. The file at rcf/define/freeze.json is not created or modified (a pre-existing file is byte-identical after the refusal).

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-198

  • AC-17601-3 - [failure] --ack <gate> --reason <text> is accepted only for the three warn-with-ack gates: define.shapes / D3 / shapes, define.crosscut / D5 / crosscut, define.consistency / D6 / consistency (the same STAGE_ALIASES readiness accepts). --ack on any other gate name is a usage refusal (exit 2) with a stderr message naming the accepted set. --ack without a matching --reason argument is a usage refusal (exit 2). Multiple --ack / --reason pairs may be passed together (parseArgs multiple: true) as long as the count matches; a mismatch is a usage refusal. An acked gate lands in the written freeze.gates entry as { state: 'acknowledged', at: { hash: <currentTreeHash>, at: <frozenAt>, reason: <text>, by: <freezerId or null> }, failing: [<id>, ...] } and its acknowledgement carries into the next computeReadiness run (which reports the stage state as 'acknowledged').

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-198

  • AC-17601-4 - [happy] The stdout summary derived from the delta BEFORE the freeze matches proposal section 2.5: 'frozen at <shortHash>: <n> REQ, <n> stories, <n> criteria, <n> interfaces added; <ids> amended; <impactedFbs> re-execute.' Counts of added come from delta.added grouped by tree.kindById; amended is delta.changed (US ids in the amended list per the proposal's example wording); impactedFbs is delta.impactedFbs. On the first freeze (freeze record absent before the run), the summary is 'first freeze at <shortHash>: <req> REQ, <us> stories, <ac> criteria, <interfaces> interfaces, <tac> TAC, <adr> ADR, <fbs> FBS.' --json emits { record, summary, delta } where record is the just-written freeze record body and delta is the pre-freeze DeltaResult.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-198

  • AC-17601-5 - [happy] --status prints the current record and the live delta summary, exit 0. Text: 'Frozen at <short> on <frozenAt>. Note: <note|(none)>. Counts: <req> REQ / <us> US / <ac> AC / <tac> TAC / <adr> ADR / <fbs> FBS. Acknowledged: <gate1> ("<reason>"); <gate2> ...(none). Litmus: attestedAt [<D3>, <D6>], readers <n>. Versions: rcfLite <v> / ruleset <v> / schemas <v>. Override: <null|<reason by at>>.' followed by the live delta summary line: '<changed> changed, <added> added, <removed> removed, <impacted> impacted, <impactedFbs> FBS re-execute.' --status --json emits { record: <freeze body>, delta: <computeDelta output> }. --status when no record exists prints 'never frozen' and exits 0 (--json: { record: null, delta: <computeDelta output over unfrozen tree> }). --status never runs the gates and never writes anything.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-198

  • AC-17601-6 - [happy] The freeze producer is wrapped with runWithAdmissibilityGate the same way readiness is (ADR-4124 carrying ADR-4123): the wrap runs first so the ruleset toolScope guard is honoured, and on a refused-admissibility verdict the CLI prints the refusal envelope to stderr as a [warn] line and the freeze compute still runs and writes if freezeable. The verb never exits 4 solely because of a refused-admissibility verdict.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-198

  • AC-17601-7 - [must-not] src/define/freeze-record.js is updated so validateFreezeRecord REQUIRES the override key (nullable): a body without override throws FreezeRecordError with field 'override'. loadFreezeRecord tolerates older records that lack the key by defaulting to null (never fails on ENOKEY). saveFreezeRecord validates first and refuses to write a body that omits override. Every existing test fixture that omits override still loads (either the loader default fills it in, or a targeted fixture update writes override: null; no legacy fixture becomes unreadable).

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-198

  • AC-17601-8 - [non-functional] The src/cli/readiness.js stage header line no longer contains a double-dash: it uses a colon between the stage id and the state label ('D1 (define.brief): failing'). The CHANGELOG.md line 'The regex is now `/\bTODO:/` -- case-sensitive uppercase `TODO`' is likewise rewritten to a colon. Any golden fixture that captured the old header text is updated. `grep -R ' -- ' src/ test/ CHANGELOG.md` returns no matches under text this slice added or edited (the grep is scoped to added lines; unrelated pre-existing occurrences elsewhere in the tree stay out of scope of the AC).

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-198

The verb runs computeReadiness (REQ-175) once over the live tree, freeze record and four ledgers; refuses with exit 4 when any stage state is 'failing' after applying any --ack argument, printing the failing gates and their first failing ids; and, on success, writes rcf/define/freeze.json via saveFreezeRecord (REQ-172) with { frozenAt, treeHash, docHashes, briefStatements, gates, counts, litmus, versions, note, override } and prints the proposal section 2.5 one-line summary derived from the pre-freeze delta ('frozen at <short treeHash>: <n> REQ, <n> stories, <n> criteria, <n> interfaces added; <ids> amended; ...'; first freeze reports 'first freeze: <whole-tree counts>'). --ack is accepted only for the three warn-with-ack gates (define.shapes, define.crosscut, define.consistency; short names shapes / crosscut / consistency; readiness's stage aliases); ack on any other gate is a usage refusal (exit 2), ack without --reason is a usage refusal. An acked gate lands in freeze.gates as { state: 'acknowledged', at: { hash: <currentTreeHash>, reason: <text> }, failing: [<id>, ...] }. --litmus-attested records the operator's per-decision attestation (Baz decision 7: default { attestedAt: [], readers: 0 }); the numbered --litmus <n> dispatch is NOT built (slice-6 seam). counts derives req/us/ac/tac/adr/fbs from tree.byId groupings, acByClass by parsing bracketed class markers on AC.description, and interfaces by kind from every TAC's interfaces[]. versions reads rcfLite from package.json, ruleset from src/ruleset/ruleset.json, and schemas from the installed @stravica-ai/rcf-schemas. --status prints the current freeze record (short hash, frozenAt, note, counts, acknowledged gates + reasons, litmus, versions, override) plus the live delta summary; --status --json emits the record and computeDelta object. The producer is wrapped with runWithAdmissibilityGate (ADR-4123: refusal is informational, the freeze still runs). Same slice: (a) src/define/freeze-record.js is corrected so the local schema requires override as a nullable field and every writer stamps override: null on a fresh freeze; loadFreezeRecord tolerates older records that lack the key by defaulting to null on load; (b) the ' -- ' double-dash in the readiness CLI stage header and the CHANGELOG regex line is replaced with a colon.",

REQ-180 Readiness tab as tab 1 and the Overview-to-PRD rename defineDetection US1 AC7 draft

src/view/readiness.js lands and html-page.js wires it as the first tab. The former Overview tab becomes PRD (same panel content; the rename is label-only). The Readiness panel renders the computeReadiness object top-to-bottom in the layout the DEFINE step 2 spec section 5 pins: tree line (formatTreeLine), two verdict pills with formatVerdictLines strings as the labels and blockedBy.length as the count, two per-persona next-action lines anchored into the stage detail, D1..D8 state chips with reason/acknowledgement text on hover, blockers grouped by persona (profile register orders the pair; the non-register group collapses with its count visible, never omitted), delta list grouped by REQ ancestor with a document-level diff on changed items (criterion-level diff deferred to the UX review per ADR-4127), per-stage check detail with persona pill and findings list when not ok, coverage tree-versus-delta with re-verify and re-execute counts, decisions outstanding in the #241 numbered format, a Freeze now control enabled iff levels.readyToBuild.ok (showing the `rcf define freeze` command and what it will record; disabled it names the failing gates from levels.readyToBuild.blockedBy; no intent-complete button), and the loaded freeze record (hash, when, note, counts, acknowledged gates with reasons). The view is pure: it never recomputes readiness, so the tab and `rcf define readiness --json` cannot disagree on the same tree hash.

Why: Baz ruling 2026-09-22 (DEFINE step 2 spec section 2.4, decision 2): one object, two renderers. The CLI (REQ-175, PR B) and the tab (REQ-180, PR C) read the same computeReadiness result so they cannot disagree. Readiness is where an operator starts, so it must be tab 1. The Overview panel is just the PRD body today (phase 3.6 dropped the diagram) so the rename is honest; keeping the hash-anchor `#tab-overview` preserves every existing link into the surface. The L1 pre-population posture (ADR-4126) requires the tab to visibly distinguish [draft] shapes from settled ones, which the shapes:draftSettled check row makes legible.

capability:define-detection

User stories (1)

US-18001 Readiness as the first tab in the viewer AC7 draft

US-18001 - Readiness as the first tab in the viewer

As a: an operator opening the viewer

I want: Readiness as the first tab with the two verdict pills and persona-grouped blockers

So that: the first thing I see is whether I can build and whose questions stand in the way

Description: User story under REQ-180. Opening the viewer puts Readiness first (default active tab), the former Overview tab is renamed PRD with its content preserved, the two level verdict pills carry the formatVerdictLines strings as labels, blockers group by persona ordered by the profile.md register (the non-register group collapses with its count visible, never omitted), and the Freeze now control is enabled iff levels.readyToBuild.ok. See the DEFINE step 2 spec dated 2026-10-01 (section 5) for the layout.

Requirement

REQ-180

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-18001-1 - [happy] Given any project, when the viewer renders, then the first tab is Readiness and the second is PRD with the former Overview content unchanged.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-201

  • AC-18001-2 - [happy] Given a failing tree, when the Readiness tab renders, then it shows two verdict pills whose labels equal the formatVerdictLines strings for the same tree.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-201

  • AC-18001-3 - [happy] Given personas.productOwner.blockers non-empty, when the tab renders, then each blocker is a findings list headed by its question with its ids as anchor links into the document tabs.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-201

  • AC-18001-4 - [happy] Given a profile register of productOwner, when the tab renders, then the product-owner group is expanded first and the engineer group is collapsed with its count visible.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-201

  • AC-18001-5 - [must-not] Given any profile register, when the tab renders, then no blocker id of either persona is omitted from the DOM.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-201

  • AC-18001-6 - [failure] Given a tree where levels.readyToBuild.ok is false, when the tab renders, then the Freeze now control is disabled and names the failing gates from levels.readyToBuild.blockedBy.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-201

  • AC-18001-7 - [happy] Given the tab and the CLI --json output for the same tree hash, when compared, then every id rendered on the tab appears in the JSON for that hash.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-201

REQ-181 Shared pill, findings-list and diff view components defineDetection US1 AC3 draft

src/view/components/{pill,findings-list,diff}.js land as three stable modules every tab can call. pill({ value, variant, title?, href? }) returns a span (or anchor when href is set) with the vocabulary class `rcf-pill--<variant>` for the vocabulary family (gate state green/amber/red; level verdict yes/no; persona po/eng; AC class) and `rcf-pill--<normalisedValue>` for the specific value, so one call site renders one markup shape across every family. findingsList({ heading, count, items }) returns a heading plus an ordered id list, each item an anchor into the document tabs with a one-line `why` string, ids capped at 20 and a `... N more suppressed` tail beyond. diff(before, after) returns a two-column rendering of two document bodies for the delta list. Readiness is the first consumer in 0.29.0; Product Map and Requirements are re-pointed only where the swap is mechanical in this PR (otherwise their markup stays and the swap is a follow-up), so no existing Product Map or Requirements test expectation changes.

Why: Three tabs today each ship their own markup for the same visual roles (status pill, items list, before-after). The hand-rolled copies drift so a gate state on one tab reads differently from the same gate state on another. Factoring to three shared components makes gate state, persona, level verdict and AC class read the same everywhere and is the smallest surface the Readiness tab needs. The spec is explicit (section 5): one module each, same markup shape across callers; existing tab tests change only where the PR explicitly re-points.

capability:define-detection

N more suppressed` tail beyond. diff(before, after) returns a two-column rendering of two document bodies for the delta list. REQ-186 guided product-owner elicitation define US3 AC18 draft

rcf-lite computes, from the readiness object, the ordered set of questions one persona can answer, each with the write-back that answers it, so that a harness can conduct the intent-complete loop without an engineer. Nothing is stored; the loop ends when `levels.intentComplete.ok` is true.

Why: Spec 2026-10-01 (DEFINE step 3) section 1 pins the loop as harness-driven. rcf-lite supplies the questions, the write-backs and the verdict; the harness holds the conversation. One new read verb `rcf define questions` turns every failing product-owner check into a per-item plain-sentence question carrying its exact write-back; `levels.intentComplete.ok === true` terminates the loop. The engineer register rides the same mechanism with `--persona engineer`.

capability:define-intent

User stories (3)

US-18601 the question set AC7 draft

US-18601 - the question set

As a: harness serving a product owner

I want: computeQuestions to turn every failing product-owner item into one plain question with its write-back

So that: I can ask without reading gate internals

Description: User story under REQ-186. computeQuestions turns every failing product-owner item into one plain question with its write-back, so the harness can ask without reading gate internals.

Requirement

REQ-186

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-18601-1 - [happy] given a tree where brief:openQuestions, skeleton:resolvedBy and stories:reqHasUs each fail at least one item, when computeQuestions runs with persona productOwner, then questions[] holds exactly one entry per failing item with id, stage, check, itemId, heading, ask, answerKinds, writeBack and blocks intent.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18601-2 - [happy] given the same tree, when computeQuestions runs twice, then the two questions[] arrays are deep-equal and ordered D1, D2, D4, D7 then by source span.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18601-3 - [happy] given an open decision with two options and a default, when computeQuestions runs, then it appears in optional[] with blocks build and not in questions[].

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18601-4 - [happy] given a tree where levels.intentComplete.ok is true, when computeQuestions runs with persona productOwner, then questions[] is empty and ok is true.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18601-5 - [happy] given persona engineer, when computeQuestions runs, then questions[] holds one entry per failing engineer item in failing stages and blocks is build.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18601-6 - [failure] given a persona value outside productOwner and engineer, when computeQuestions runs, then it throws a usage error naming the accepted values.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18601-7 - [must-not] given any tree, when computeQuestions runs, then no file under rcf/ is created or modified and no question carries a writeBack command whose verb is not registered in the CLI help.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

US-18602 the verb and the tools AC6 draft

US-18602 - the verb and the tools

As a: operator or harness

I want: the verb and the MCP tool to return the same object

So that: the two loops cannot disagree

Description: User story under REQ-186. `rcf define questions` and `rcf_define_questions` return the same object, so the CLI loop and the MCP loop cannot disagree.

Requirement

REQ-186

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-18602-1 - [happy] given a failing tree, when rcf define questions --json runs, then stdout is the computeQuestions object and the exit code is 0.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18602-2 - [happy] given no --persona, when the verb runs on a profile whose register is engineer, then persona is engineer; with no profile it is productOwner.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18602-3 - [happy] given --stage skeleton and --limit 2, when the verb runs, then questions[] holds at most two D2 entries and remaining counts every D2 item.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18602-4 - [happy] given the MCP tool rcf_define_questions with the same arguments, when it is called, then structuredContent deep-equals the verb's --json output.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18602-5 - [failure] given --persona architect, when the verb runs, then it exits 2 with the usage line naming productOwner and engineer.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18602-6 - [must-not] given any invocation of rcf define questions, when it completes, then no file under rcf/ has been created or modified.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

US-18603 write-back and termination AC5 draft

US-18603 - write-back and termination

As a: product owner

I want: every answer to land through a verb and the loop to end at the computed verdict

So that: nothing about my intent lives only in a chat

Description: User story under REQ-186. Every answer lands through a verb and the loop ends at the computed verdict, so nothing about intent lives only in a chat.

Requirement

REQ-186

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-18603-1 - [happy] given the scripted loop fixture, when every writeBack the question set returns is applied and readiness recomputed each turn, then the question count strictly decreases every turn and reaches zero.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18603-2 - [happy] given a statement resolved to a newly created REQ carrying description and domain, when readiness recomputes, then skeleton:reqIntent passes that REQ and stories:reqHasUs asks for it once.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18603-3 - [happy] given a tree at L1, when [draft] entities, TAC stubs and interfaces are added, then levels.intentComplete.ok stays true and the product-owner question set stays empty.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18603-4 - [failure] given an openQuestion promoted to a decision with one option and no default, when readiness recomputes, then decisions:wellFormed asks once and brief:openQuestions does not.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18603-5 - [must-not] given any product-owner check, when readiness recomputes after an engineer-only edit, then no product-owner check changes from ok to failing.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

REQ-187 document intake into brief statements define US2 AC12 draft

A submitted document reaches the brief ledger as kinded statements with source spans through `brief add --from`, the intake scans run over the new statements against the existing ones, and every finding becomes an open question the loop asks.

Why: Spec 2026-10-01 (DEFINE step 3) section 2.1 splits intake into two halves. The harness writes a statement file beside each source and the operator corrects it. rcf-lite mints the statements, runs the intake scans over the new statements against the existing ones, and appends one openQuestion statement per finding. This is the seam decision 4 pins down: scan findings become brief statements so the loop reads one check (brief:openQuestions) and the owner answers in one place.

capability:define-intake

User stories (2)

US-18701 the statement file AC6 draft

US-18701 - the statement file

As a: harness

I want: a line grammar for kind and source

So that: the split I propose to the owner is what gets minted

Description: User story under REQ-187. The harness writes a statement file beside each source with a leading bracketed kind and a trailing (source: ...) marker; `brief add --from` parses the markers and mints the statements.

Requirement

REQ-187

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-18701-1 - [happy] given a line "- [constraint] A loan on hold must not accrue late fees. (source: briefs/x.md:15)", when brief add --from runs, then one statement is minted with kind constraint, that text and that source.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18701-2 - [happy] given a line with no markers under --kind actor --source doc.md, when brief add --from runs, then the statement has kind actor and source doc.md.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18701-3 - [happy] given a line ending with "?" and no kind marker, when brief add --from runs, then the statement has kind openQuestion.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18701-4 - [happy] given a 0.29.0 line-per-statement file, when brief add --from runs, then the minted statements equal the 0.29.0 output.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18701-5 - [failure] given a line "[gadget] text", when brief add --from runs, then it exits 2 naming the accepted kinds and writes nothing.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18701-6 - [must-not] given --dry-run, when brief add --from runs, then rcf/define/brief-ledger.json is not created or modified.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

US-18702 scans into open questions AC6 draft

US-18702 - scans into open questions

As a: product owner

I want: contradictions and gaps the tool can see to reach me as questions

So that: the first readiness run tells me what is still mine

Description: User story under REQ-187. The intake scans run inside `brief add --from` over the new statements against every existing statement, and every finding becomes an openQuestion statement with source `scan:<name>:<ids>`.

Requirement

REQ-187

Acceptance criteria

  • AC-18702-1 - [happy] given two new statements the contradiction scan flags, when brief add --from runs with scans on, then one openQuestion statement is appended with source scan:contradiction:<id>,<id> and brief:openQuestions fails it.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18702-2 - [happy] given a --findings file with two findings, when brief add --from runs, then two openQuestion statements are appended with source scan:<name>.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18702-3 - [happy] given a frozen tree, when brief add --from runs, then the scans compare the new statements against every existing statement.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18702-4 - [happy] given --json, when brief add --from runs, then stdout holds added[] and findings[].

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18702-5 - [failure] given --no-scan together with --findings, when brief add runs, then it exits 2.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202

  • AC-18702-6 - [must-not] given --text, when brief add runs, then no scan runs and no openQuestion statement is appended.

    Testable: true - Covered by FBS-202
