Architecture

TAD-001 draft 52 components - 55 decisions

Technical architecture (TAD)

System overview Build Lite is a Node 24 ESM toolset whose core is a set of local filesystem operations over a project's RCF do...

Build Lite is a Node 24 ESM toolset whose core is a set of local filesystem operations over a project's RCF documents. CRUD, query, view, the build loop and the MCP surface are all thin layers over a shared document store that reads and writes the on-disk rcf tree and validates against the published schemas at every boundary.

Purpose

Run the full RCF method over in-repository documents and surface it through deterministic, structured operations for a non-engineering owner and for AI tooling.

Approach

Layered. A document-store core owns load, validate and persist. A CLI binary, a view renderer, a query engine, a build adapter and an MCP server are all consumers of that core. No layer reaches the filesystem except through the store.

Key capabilities

  • Filesystem-backed RCF document store with schema validation at boundaries
  • Deterministic CRUD verbs over every document type
  • Diagram and HTML rendering of the whole tree
  • Traceability and query over the chain
  • Build-specification to implementation-prompt assembly
  • Local stdio MCP surface over the whole feature set
Architecture principles 4 principles: Filesystem is the source of truth, Validate at every boundary, Adapters are thin, Harness-agnost...
  • Filesystem is the source of truth. Every read and write goes to the local rcf tree; no other store mirrors it.
    Rationale: Guarantees the in-repository differentiator and keeps the tool harness-agnostic.
  • Validate at every boundary. Documents are validated against the published schemas on load and before persist.
    Rationale: A non-coder cannot catch a malformed document by eye; the tool must refuse to write invalid state.
  • Adapters are thin. CLI, MCP and the build loop carry no business logic the core does not already own.
    Rationale: One behaviour, many surfaces; no drift between how a verb behaves on the CLI versus over MCP.
  • Harness-agnostic. The tool runs the same against any AI harness because behaviour lives on the local filesystem and not in a hosted surface.
    Rationale: Survives a change of AI harness without re-implementation or migration.
Integration architecture The store exposes a typed-by-convention internal API of document operations. The CLI maps verbs to those opera...

API design

The store exposes a typed-by-convention internal API of document operations. The CLI maps verbs to those operations and renders results for a terminal. The MCP server maps tools to the same operations and returns structured results. No HTTP API is exposed.

Event model

None. Operations are synchronous filesystem reads and writes.

Operational concerns Not applicable for a local binary; a validate command reports project health by validating every document and ...

Health checks

Not applicable for a local binary; a validate command reports project health by validating every document and listing broken references.

Logging

Human-readable terminal output by default; a quiet flag for scripting and a verbose flag for diagnostics.

Data architecture Nothing written yet empty

Nothing written yet. Author it with rcf define update TAD-001 --set dataArchitecture.dataStores="..." (fields: dataStores, coreEntities); this section fills in live.

TAC-001 Document store interfaces3 deps1 draft

TAC-001 - Document store

Purpose: Own all reads, validation and writes of RCF documents on the local filesystem, and be the only component that touches the rcf tree.

Responsibilities

  • Resolve a document file path from a document id by convention
  • Load and parse a document and validate it against its schema
  • Walk from the roots to assemble the full in-memory tree
  • Persist a document only after it validates
  • Surface broken references and schema failures as structured errors

Internal structure: A loader resolves ids to paths and parses JSON. A validator wraps the published schema bundle and is registered once at start-up. A writer serialises and persists. A tree walker reads the manifest roots and follows the parent id lists to build the full document set in memory.

Interfaces

  • loadDocument (function) - Resolve an id to a path, parse and validate, return the document or a structured error.
  • saveDocument (function) - Validate then persist a document; refuse to write if validation fails.
  • walkTree (function) - From the manifest roots, resolve every child by id and return the full tree.

Dependencies

  • rcf-schemas (external) - The published schema package the validator registers at start-up.

Trade-offs: Centralising all filesystem access in one component costs a small amount of indirection but guarantees that no consumer can write an unvalidated document or bypass the source-of-truth rule.

Notes: The store is intentionally synchronous where possible; a local CLI does not benefit from streaming and synchronous code is easier for contributors to follow.

TAC-002 CLI binary interfaces11 deps5 draft

TAC-002 - CLI binary

Purpose: The rcf command-line entry point. Map verbs to store, query, view or build operations and render results and errors for a terminal.

Responsibilities

  • Parse command-line arguments and route each verb to the matching core operation
  • Render results as readable terminal output by default
  • Honour quiet and verbose flags for scripting and diagnostics
  • Surface structured errors as human-readable messages with the underlying detail available

Internal structure: A small command router maps each verb (init, view, read, create, update, delete, coverage, trace, impact, build, validate) to a function in the store, query, view or build adapter. A formatter renders results for a terminal.

Interfaces

  • init (command) - Initialise a new RCF project on disk.
  • view (command) - Generate the diagram and the static page.
  • read (command) - Read a document by id.
  • create (command) - Create a document with parent linkage.
  • update (command) - Update fields on a document.
  • delete (command) - Delete a document with reference safety.
  • coverage (command) - Report coverage gaps across the tree.
  • trace (command) - Trace forward or back along the intent chain.
  • impact (command) - Report what is affected by a document change.
  • build (command) - Assemble a build prompt or mark a slice done.
  • validate (command) - Validate every document and list broken references.

Dependencies

  • Document store (tac) - All filesystem access goes through the store.
  • View renderer (tac) - The view verb routes to the renderer.
  • Query engine (tac) - The coverage, trace and impact verbs route to the query engine.
  • Build adapter (tac) - The build verbs route to the build adapter.
  • Error and reporting (tac) - Structured errors are rendered consistently.

Trade-offs: A single binary keeps the install and discovery story simple; a fragmented set of binaries would be more orthogonal but is overkill for a single project.

Notes: Verbs are kept close to the spoken vocabulary of the method so a non-coder can guess the command from the document type.

  ],
  "tradeoffs": "A single binary keeps the install and discovery story simple; a fragmented set of binaries would be more orthogonal but is overkill for a single project.",
  "notes": "Verbs are kept close to the spoken vocabulary of the method so a non-coder can guess the command from the document type.",
  "createdAt": "2026-06-25T00:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-06-25T00:00:00Z"
}
TAC-003 View renderer interfaces2 deps1 draft

TAC-003 - View renderer

Purpose: Produce the diagram source and the static browsable page from a loaded RCF tree, with broken references marked visibly and no server required.

Responsibilities

  • Build a diagram from the chain edges between documents
  • Render each document as a readable section, not raw JSON
  • Mark broken references visibly in both diagram and page
  • Write static output files that open in a browser with no server process

Internal structure: A diagram builder walks the loaded tree and emits Mermaid source. A page builder renders each document into a templated HTML section and links between them by id. Output is written to a fixed view directory at the project root.

Interfaces

  • renderDiagram (function) - Emit the diagram source for the whole tree.
  • renderPage (function) - Write the static browsable page to the view output directory.

Dependencies

  • Document store (tac) - The renderer reads the loaded tree only through the store.

Trade-offs: Mermaid is locked as the diagram format because it renders without a runtime and ships everywhere; a pluggable renderer would add an interface for a benefit the product does not yet need.

Notes: The fixed output directory keeps the configuration surface zero and the output discoverable.

TAC-004 Query engine interfaces4 deps1 draft

TAC-004 - Query engine

Purpose: Answer traceability questions over a loaded RCF tree without ever traversing the FBS layer.

Responsibilities

  • Compute coverage gaps across requirements, stories, criteria and tests
  • Trace forward from any document to its descendants along the intent chain
  • Trace back from any document to its ancestors along the intent chain
  • Compute impact sets across the intent chain and the architecture references on FBS
  • Never walk the FBS layer when computing intent-chain traces

Internal structure: A walker traverses the chain (PRD to REQ to US to AC to TS to TC) by id. Coverage and trace operations are layered over the walker. Impact analysis additionally inspects FBS contextRequirements references.

Interfaces

  • coverage (function) - Report coverage gaps across the tree.
  • traceForward (function) - Trace from a document to its descendants along the intent chain.
  • traceBack (function) - Trace from a document back to its ancestors along the intent chain.
  • impact (function) - Compute the impact set of a change to a given document.

Dependencies

  • Document store (tac) - All traversal reads through the store.

Trade-offs: A general graph engine would be more expressive but the intent chain is small and a hand-rolled walker is easier to reason about and to keep correct.

Notes: Keeping the FBS out of intent traces is a load-bearing design rule, not an optimisation.

TAC-005 Build adapter interfaces3 deps2 draft

TAC-005 - Build adapter

Purpose: Walk an FBS and its references to assemble an implementation prompt, compute the dependency-respecting build order, and mark slices done.

Responsibilities

  • Walk acceptance criteria in acIds to their parent user stories
  • Walk referenced TACs and ADRs and include their relevant content
  • Assemble a single markdown prompt for the named FBS
  • Topologically sort the FBS dependency graph and detect cycles
  • Advance FBS execution status and the matching Build Sequence slot status when a slice is marked done

Internal structure: A prompt assembler composes a markdown document from the FBS, its acceptance criteria and the referenced architecture documents. A sorter computes the build order from FBS dependency lists. A mark-done operation updates execution status fields and writes through the store.

Interfaces

  • assemblePrompt (function) - Assemble the implementation prompt for a named FBS.
  • buildOrder (function) - Compute the dependency-respecting order and parallel-safe groups.
  • markDone (function) - Advance the FBS and slot status when a slice is finished.

Dependencies

  • Document store (tac) - Read FBS, AC, TAC and ADR through the store; write status updates through the store.
  • Query engine (tac) - Reuse the walker to resolve AC to parent user stories.

Trade-offs: The prompt is assembled as a single markdown document for simplicity and portability; a richer structured payload would be more flexible but would lock the consumer to a non-portable shape.

Notes: Mark-done is an explicit command so the tool stays offline and harness-agnostic; no PR-watching daemon is required.

TAC-006 MCP server interfaces10 deps5 draft

TAC-006 - MCP server

Purpose: Expose store, query, view and build operations as local stdio MCP tools so an AI harness can drive the whole feature set without shelling out to the CLI.

Responsibilities

  • Register tools with structured input and output for every CRUD, query, view and build operation
  • Route each tool to the same core operation the CLI uses
  • Communicate over local stdio only and open no network listener
  • Serialise structured errors so an AI tool can act on them

Internal structure: A thin MCP adapter registers each tool with a schema for its input and output and maps each tool to a core function. Errors are converted to structured objects via the error and reporting component.

Interfaces

  • rcf.read (mcpTool) - Read any RCF document by id over MCP.
  • rcf.create (mcpTool) - Create a document with parent linkage over MCP.
  • rcf.update (mcpTool) - Update fields on a document over MCP.
  • rcf.delete (mcpTool) - Delete a document with reference safety over MCP.
  • rcf.coverage (mcpTool) - Report coverage gaps over MCP.
  • rcf.trace (mcpTool) - Trace forward or back over MCP.
  • rcf.impact (mcpTool) - Report impact over MCP.
  • rcf.view (mcpTool) - Generate the diagram and the static page over MCP.
  • rcf.build.assemble (mcpTool) - Assemble a build prompt over MCP.
  • rcf.build.markDone (mcpTool) - Mark a slice done over MCP.

Dependencies

  • Document store (tac) - CRUD tools route through the store.
  • View renderer (tac) - The view tool routes to the renderer.
  • Query engine (tac) - Coverage, trace and impact tools route to the query engine.
  • Build adapter (tac) - Build tools route to the build adapter.
  • Error and reporting (tac) - Structured errors are serialised for the MCP client.

Trade-offs: Local stdio sacrifices the convenience of a hosted MCP but is the only transport that preserves filesystem access; the trade is locked by the differentiator.

Notes: The MCP surface mirrors the CLI verb set so behaviour is identical across surfaces.

TAC-007 Error and reporting interfaces3 deps0 draft

TAC-007 - Error and reporting

Purpose: The structured error type and the consistent rendering of errors across CLI and MCP surfaces.

Responsibilities

  • Define a structured error type carrying the offending field, the rule broken and the document id
  • Render errors as readable terminal output for the CLI
  • Serialise errors as structured objects for MCP clients
  • Aggregate multiple validation failures so all are reported together

Internal structure: A small error type and a pair of renderers (terminal and structured). The renderers are pure functions over the error type.

Interfaces

  • RcfError (type) - The structured error type used throughout the tool.
  • renderForTerminal (function) - Render an RcfError as human-readable terminal output.
  • renderForMcp (function) - Serialise an RcfError as a structured object for an MCP client.

Trade-offs: A single error type across surfaces costs a small loss of surface-specific detail but guarantees that error reporting does not drift between CLI and MCP.

Notes: Validation failures aggregate; the renderers preserve the full list, not just the first.

TAC-008 Agent guidance pack interfaces3 deps2 draft

TAC-008 - Agent guidance pack

Purpose: Ship the agent-facing method layer - the elicitation and build-cycle playbooks, the reference docs and the harness fragment - that teaches an AI agent how to run the RCF method well, served over MCP as resources and prompts and readable in place under guidance/.

Responsibilities

  • Carry the elicitation method (question frames, AC-depth bar, deploy-target elicitation, hosting-choice guidance) the eliciting agent runs with a human
  • Carry the build-cycle method (five stages, local-preview default outcome, runtime-provenance discipline, interim self-review) the operating agent runs per FBS
  • Carry the harness fragment rcf init writes into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, whose RULE blocks foreclose observed failure modes
  • Keep every shipped claim, verb and channel address mechanically agreed with the tool via the drift tests

Internal structure: Static markdown files under guidance/, indexed by guidance/manifest.json which maps each file to one canonical MCP address (resources for reference docs, prompts for the playbooks). The harness fragment is a fenced block in harness-template.md that src/setup extracts and writes into agent-instructions files. Drift tests (test/guidance) assert content-and-inventory invariants so the pack and the tool cannot silently diverge.

Interfaces

  • rcf_elicit_requirements (prompt) - The elicitation playbook, served as an MCP prompt to the eliciting agent.
  • rcf_execute_build_cycle (prompt) - The build-cycle playbook, served as an MCP prompt to the operating agent.
  • harness fragment (artifact) - The RULE-bearing block rcf init writes into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.

Dependencies

  • MCP server (tac) - Serves the pack's docs as resources and playbooks as prompts over local stdio.
  • Build adapter (tac) - The build-cycle method the pack teaches is executed against the bundles the build adapter assembles.

Trade-offs: The pack is prose served to a model, not enforced code: it can teach a property (local preview, provenance labelling) but cannot mechanically compel it the way a schema compels document shape. Drift tests hold the pack honest against the tool's verbs and inventory; the method's behavioural properties are held by the RULE blocks and the ACs that require them, not by a runtime gate. The productised independent gate is out of scope here (see ADR-009).

Notes: Modelled as a component for the first time by the Tier-1 hardening set; the pack existed and shipped before this TAC captured it.

TAC-3801... deploy-hetzner-server provisioner module: sole reader of the Hetzner API token, hcloud shell path and raw-api fork interfaces0 deps0 draft

TAC-3801-deploy-hetzner-server-provisioner - deploy-hetzner-server provisioner module: sole reader of the Hetzner API token, hcloud shell path and raw-api fork

Purpose: T-1 repo-chain TAC mirror for the shipped blueprints/deploy-hetzner-server/contributions/tacs/tac-3801-deploy-hetzner-server-provisioner.json contribution. Defines the provisioner Node module that wraps hcloud CLI verbs (create server, apply firewall, take snapshot, list snapshots, destroy server) and, under provisioningTool=raw-api, wraps the equivalent Hetzner Cloud REST endpoints. Sole-reader guarantee: only this module reads the HETZNER_ACCOUNT_API_KEY via security-secrets-management (or the project-scoped alternative). Anchors AC-11001-1 (repo chain).

Responsibilities

  • Wrap hcloud CLI verbs (create server, apply firewall, take snapshot, list snapshots, destroy server) and the raw Hetzner Cloud REST endpoints behind one facade (AC-11001-1, AC-11102-1, AC-11402-1).
  • Be the sole reader of HETZNER_ACCOUNT_API_KEY via security-secrets-management; every other module reads from the facade (AC-11001-1).
  • Emit provisionerReady, hetznerServerProvisioned, hetznerSnapshotTaken and hetznerServerDestroyed with metadata-only payloads (AC-11001-1, AC-11501-1).

Internal structure: One module blueprints/deploy-hetzner-server/contributions/tacs/tac-3801-deploy-hetzner-server-provisioner.json plus the provisioner facade proto shipped in the fixture (packages/rcf-lite/test/fixtures/hetzner-throwaway-server/src/provisioner-facade.mjs) reading the token from a single seam and firing provisionerReady on ready().

TAC-3804... deploy-hetzner-server firewall rule shape: 22 from operator-nominated prefixes, 80/443 open, deny all else, applied at provision time interfaces0 deps0 draft

TAC-3804-deploy-hetzner-server-firewall-shape - deploy-hetzner-server firewall rule shape: 22 from operator-nominated prefixes, 80/443 open, deny all else, applied at provision time

Purpose: T-1 repo-chain TAC mirror for the shipped blueprints/deploy-hetzner-server/contributions/tacs/tac-3804-deploy-hetzner-server-firewall-shape.json contribution. Defines the Hetzner Cloud firewall rule shape carried inside the server manifest: 22 permitted only from an operator-nominated set of source-prefix ranges; 80/443 permitted from 0.0.0.0/0 for the reverse proxy; all other inbound denied. Manifest schema refuses on a rule set that opens 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 or drops 80/443. Anchors AC-11301-1 (repo chain).

Responsibilities

  • Define the firewall rule shape inside the manifest: 22 permitted only from a nonempty list of source-prefix ranges; 80 and 443 permitted; all other inbound denied (AC-11301-1).
  • Refuse (via manifest-schema-validate) on a manifest that opens 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 or drops 80/443.

Internal structure: Rule shape carried inside the same hetzner-server.schema.json used by TAC-3802; the applyFirewall verb on the provisioner facade consumes the parsed rule set.

TAC-3901-platform-docker-compose-host-compose-layout - T-2 platform-docker-compose-host compose layout

Purpose: The applying project ships one compose.yaml at the repo root whose services key names every container the stack runs. Every entry is one image running one container; networks and volumes are top-level named entries; a colocated .env carries non-secret configuration values (never inline). The container host reads compose.yaml as the runtime topology source and refuses to bring the stack up on layout drift.

Responsibilities

  • Serve compose.yaml at the repo root as the sole topology surface (AC-12001-1, AC-12202-1).
  • Guarantee service-per-container: each entry under services: runs one image (AC-12001-1).
  • Declare all networks and volumes as top-level named entries: no bare defaults (AC-12001-1).
  • Bind non-secret configuration through a colocated .env: no inline literals (AC-12001-1).

TAC-3902-platform-docker-compose-host-secrets-mount - T-2 platform-docker-compose-host secrets mount

Purpose: The compose file declares each secret under its top-level secrets: key with a file: source. Services reference secrets through their service-level secrets: array so docker mounts them as files at 0o400 inside the container. When security-secrets-management is applied, the source path resolves through that facade; when it is not, the guide names a file-based fallback. No plaintext secret literal appears anywhere in compose.yaml or a referenced service config (grep-refuse).

Responsibilities

  • Declare every secret through a compose secrets: file mount (AC-12101-1, AC-12102-1).
  • Refuse a plaintext secret literal anywhere in compose.yaml (AC-12102-1).
  • Mount each secret file at 0o400 inside the container (AC-12101-1).
  • Bind to security-secrets-management when applied; document the file-based fallback (AC-12101-1).

TAC-3903-platform-docker-compose-host-healthcheck-lint - T-2 platform-docker-compose-host healthcheck and lifecycle lint

Purpose: A lint pass runs before docker compose up. It asserts every HTTP-terminating service declares a healthcheck: block; every service declares a restart: policy whose value is one of unless-stopped or on-failure; every service declares a logging: driver: entry whose value is one of journald or loki. The lint refuses on any missing or unclassified line, naming the service and the offending field.

Responsibilities

  • Assert every HTTP-terminating service declares a healthcheck: block (AC-12201-1).
  • Assert every service declares a restart policy in the allowed set (AC-12301-1).
  • Assert every service declares a logging driver in the allowed set (AC-12501-1).
  • Refuse on missing or unclassified fields, naming the service (AC-12201-1, AC-12301-1, AC-12501-1).

TAC-3904-platform-docker-compose-host-reverse-proxy-artefact - T-2 platform-docker-compose-host reverse-proxy artefact

Purpose: The reverse-proxy config file (caddy/Caddyfile when reverseProxy=caddy, traefik/traefik.yaml when reverseProxy=traefik) lives as a first-class checked-in artefact under the applying repo. The compose file bind-mounts the artefact read-only into the proxy service. The gate runs the vendor validator against the artefact and refuses on an invalid directive. Under the reload verb (docker compose exec caddy caddy reload or the Traefik equivalent), a burst against the proxy inside the elicited window sees no non-2xx and no dropped connection.

Responsibilities

  • Ship the reverse-proxy config as a checked-in artefact bind-mounted into the proxy (AC-12401-1).
  • Validate the artefact with the vendor validator at gate time (AC-12401-1).
  • Prove zero-downtime reload with a real-account burst (AC-12402-1).
  • Name the reload verb per proxy in the guide and the fixture README (AC-12401-1, AC-12402-1).

TAC-4001... edge-cloudflare-tunnel TAC interfaces0 deps0 draft

TAC-4001-edge-cloudflare-tunnel-connector-shape - edge-cloudflare-tunnel TAC

Purpose: The cloudflared connector installs in one of two runtime shapes as selected by ADR-4002 from the applied capability set. When containerHost is applied (T-2 platform-docker-compose-host on top of T-1 deploy-hetzner-server) the connector ships as a compose service alongside the applying project services on the same web-net network with no host ports and a healthcheck. When the host runs bare (only T-1 applied) the connector ships as a systemd unit per the vendor local-configuration-file docs. Either shape emits cloudflaredReady on boot with connector id, region and version metadata (metadata only).

Responsibilities

  • Ship the compose-service variant under packages/rcf-lite/test/fixtures/hetzner-throwaway-server/cloudflared/compose-service/ (AC-13001-1).
  • Ship the systemd-unit variant under packages/rcf-lite/test/fixtures/hetzner-throwaway-server/cloudflared/systemd-unit/ (AC-13001-1).
  • Emit cloudflaredReady on boot with connector id, region and version metadata (AC-13002-1).
  • Never expose an origin port on the host firewall (AC-13201-1).

TAC-4002... edge-cloudflare-tunnel TAC interfaces0 deps0 draft

TAC-4002-edge-cloudflare-tunnel-manifest-schema - edge-cloudflare-tunnel TAC

Purpose: The tunnel manifest at cloudflare/tunnels/<name>.yaml under the applying project is the sole runtime source of truth for what the cloudflared connector serves. The shipped JSON schema requires a uuid-shaped tunnel id, a secretRef credentials reference (never a literal path or JSON body inline), and an ingress rules array whose last entry is a catch-all rule returning http_status 404. The schema refuses ingress rules whose service URL binds to a host public interface (only internal addresses reachable through the compose network or a loopback interface are allowed).

Responsibilities

  • Ship the JSON schema at blueprints/edge-cloudflare-tunnel/contributions/probes/tunnel-manifest.schema.json (AC-13101-1).
  • Validate the fixture manifests at cloudflared/*/cloudflare/tunnels/probe.yaml on every reviewer boot (AC-13101-1, AC-13102-1).
  • Refuse ingress rules that bind to a host public port (AC-13201-1).
  • Refuse a manifest whose credentials reference is not a secretRef (AC-13101-1, AC-13401-1).

TAC-4101... Feedback CLI verb family interfaces2 deps7 draft

TAC-4101-feedback-cli - Feedback CLI verb family

Purpose: Own the rcf feedback core verb and its sub-dispatcher (add, list, preview, submit, defer, discard, opt-in, opt-out, hook, status), exposing the surface the agent, the operator and the harness hooks all call.

Responsibilities

  • Register feedback in bin/rcf.js CORE map alongside init, doctor, guidance, mcp, version
  • Parse and validate sub-verb flags and enums before touching store or network
  • Return the documented exit codes per sub-verb (0 success, 2 usage, 3 outcome with residual pending)
  • Export HELP text for the help-parity test and mirror the core verb help conventions
  • Route each sub-verb to store, redact, render, destination, gh, hook without any cross-module state

Internal structure: src/cli/feedback.js is a sub-dispatcher with a HELP export and one handler per sub-verb; each handler reads flags, calls into src/feedback/* pure modules, and prints the shaped result. Handlers never shell out directly; the gh call sits behind src/feedback/gh.js.

Interfaces

  • feedbackMain (function) - Argv-driven main; matches the core-verb signature the top-level dispatcher expects.
  • HELP (constant) - Static help text asserted by the help-parity test.

Dependencies

  • TAC-4102-feedback-store (tac) - All state reads and writes.
  • TAC-4103-feedback-redact (tac) - Preview and submit pipelines.
  • TAC-4104-feedback-fingerprint (tac) - Fingerprint per entry.
  • TAC-4105-feedback-render (tac) - Title, body and bundle rendering.
  • TAC-4106-feedback-destination (tac) - Destination resolution.
  • TAC-4107-feedback-gh (tac) - The single gh shell-out seam.
  • TAC-4108-feedback-hook (tac) - Hook handler; called by hook sub-verb.

Trade-offs: A single core verb keeps the surface easy to reference in RULE 17 and in docs; the cost is a moderately sized sub-dispatcher, matched by preflight and other multi-verb families already in the tree.

Notes: The verb is core, not grouped, because it spans discover-to-audit and is invoked from harness hooks; OLD_FLAT_MAP is untouched (no legacy form existed). Design section 9 decision: no MCP tool for feedback in v1 (rejected: an rcf_feedback_add MCP tool, adds a second code path to test before the first has users; add when an MCP-only harness appears).

TAC-4102... Feedback local store interfaces4 deps1 draft

TAC-4102-feedback-store - Feedback local store

Purpose: Own the on-disk feedback log at .rcf/feedback/entries.jsonl (append-only, one JSON object per line, folded by id), the per-session ask ledger at .rcf/feedback/state.json, and the outbox bundle directory .rcf/feedback/outbox/. Contribute the gitignore entry so the store never rides a git push.

Responsibilities

  • Append entry and state lines atomically with no reader ever seeing a partial line
  • Fold entries.jsonl by id, last line wins, when returning current state
  • Export feedbackGitignoreEntry so managed-gitignore aggregation picks up the path on doctor --fix
  • Refuse a first write when the gitignore does not cover .rcf/feedback/ and --force is absent
  • Provide state helpers for asked-records, deferred-until-session, discarded, submitted and bundled transitions

Internal structure: src/feedback/store.js exposes readEntries(root), appendEntry(root, entry), appendState(root, transition) and readSettings(root); a small ensureGitignore(root, opts) enforces the pre-write check. Outbox writes go through a separate helper that computes the filename from the destination slug and the ISO timestamp.

Interfaces

  • readEntries (function) - Load and fold the JSONL log to current-state entries.
  • appendEntry (function) - Append one entry object as a JSONL line.
  • appendState (function) - Append one state-transition line for an existing id.
  • feedbackGitignoreEntry (constant) - Managed-gitignore contribution consumed by src/setup/managed-gitignore.js.

Dependencies

  • node:fs/promises (external) - Filesystem I/O; the store is deliberately synchronous where safe.

Trade-offs: Append-only JSONL is trivial to write correctly and to inspect by eye; the cost is a fold on every read, which is negligible at the entry counts a single project will ever see.

Notes: Gitignored, not committed. Raw entries can hold what redaction removes; committing them would leak on the next push for a public project.

TAC-4103... Feedback redactor interfaces2 deps1 draft

TAC-4103-feedback-redact - Feedback redactor

Purpose: Rule-based, deterministic redaction of any string that would leave the machine (issue title, body, evidence pointers). No LLM anywhere; the ledger of every replacement is what the operator sees on preview.

Responsibilities

  • Apply the eight redaction rules from design section 5 to title, body and evidence strings
  • Return a ledger of { rule, before, after, count } entries for the operator disclosure
  • Refuse on residual-secret matches (second pass) with a line pointer so the offending body is not sent
  • Ship a bundled allowlist of vendor hosts and an `extensions` shortlist on src/feedback/redact-allowlist.json (Barry ruling 2026-09-21); the operator's rcf/feedback-settings.json may still supply additional host and extension entries which are merged at call time (design amendment R5d)
  • Guard operator-identity substitution with a RESERVED_IDENTITY_TOKENS stopword list (agent, user, admin, api, code, system, etc.) so a common noun in the operator's identity name never folds; substitution still fires for real given names in the identity

Internal structure: src/feedback/redact.js is a pure module: redact(text, context) -> { text, ledger[] } plus small per-rule helpers. src/feedback/redact-allowlist.json ships the vendor host set; the extension array is merged at call time.

Interfaces

  • redact (function) - Redact one string with the eight rules; return the redacted text and the ledger.
  • RedactionContext (type) - projectRoot, projectName, operatorName, gitRemote, allowHosts.

Dependencies

  • node:crypto (external) - Entropy heuristic implementation for rule 5 (secret-looking strings).

Trade-offs: Rule-based redaction is testable with a fixture corpus and deterministic under review; the cost is that it will occasionally over-redact (a benign name that matches an entropy rule), which is what the disclosure ledger exists to catch.

Notes: The stored entry is never mutated by redaction; the rendered output is what leaves.

TAC-4104... Feedback fingerprint interfaces1 deps1 draft

TAC-4104-feedback-fingerprint - Feedback fingerprint

Purpose: Deterministic 12-hex fingerprint per entry that keys the same-defect fold on issue create.

Responsibilities

  • Compute the first 12 hex characters of sha-256 over the canonical fingerprint input
  • Exclude blueprint version from the input so a defect across versions folds
  • Fall back to normalised-title tokens when the anchor is absent, and warn in preview

Internal structure: src/feedback/fingerprint.js is pure and tiny: fingerprint(entry) -> hex12 plus normaliseTitle(title) helper for the fallback.

Interfaces

  • fingerprint (function) - Compute the entry fingerprint from its canonical input.

Dependencies

  • node:crypto (external) - sha-256 for the fingerprint hash.

Trade-offs: A tiny fingerprint (12 hex = 48 bits) risks a collision at very large corpuses; at the scale of a single blueprint tracker it is safe, and issues carry the full-anchor context in the body so a maintainer resolves a rare collision by hand.

Notes: The fingerprint appears twice in the body (visible line and HTML comment) so maintainer edits do not lose it.

TAC-4105... Feedback renderer interfaces3 deps1 draft

TAC-4105-feedback-render - Feedback renderer

Purpose: Deterministic templates for issue title and body, the +1 comment body, and the outbox bundle file. The output is what preview shows and what leaves on submit.

Responsibilities

  • Render the issue title as "[<effective-slug>] <title>" for blueprints and "[rcf-lite] <title>" for core
  • Render the body with the Evidence and Environment tables, the visible fingerprint line and its HTML-comment twin
  • Render the outbox bundle header and one section per entry (title first, then body) so a paste is one-shot
  • Consume redacted strings and the redaction ledger; never re-run redaction itself

Internal structure: src/feedback/render.js exposes renderIssue(entry, redacted), renderComment(entry, redacted, deltaOnly), renderBundle(destinationInfo, entries). All output is UTF-8, LF line endings, ASCII hyphens only (register rule and fingerprint stability).

Interfaces

  • renderIssue (function) - Return { title, body, labels[] } for a create call.
  • renderComment (function) - Return the comment body for a +1 add.
  • renderBundle (function) - Return the markdown bundle string for outbox files.

Dependencies

  • TAC-4103-feedback-redact (tac) - The renderer consumes redacted strings the caller supplies.

Trade-offs: Static templates keep the shape reviewable by eye and byte-comparable in tests; the cost is that template drift requires golden updates, which is exactly the discipline the tests exist for.

Notes: The docs-site "submit a blueprint idea" form reuses these templates verbatim so triage sees one shape from both producers.

TAC-4106... Feedback destination resolver interfaces2 deps1 draft

TAC-4106-feedback-destination - Feedback destination resolver

Purpose: Resolve a pending entry to its destination repo and visibility, using the library.json issues field, the rcf/blueprint-libraries.json snapshot, the manifest sourceRef derivation, and the shelf-and-core constant.

Responsibilities

  • Walk entry.target -> manifest.blueprints[] -> registry entry -> issuesRepo, with sourceRef derivation as fallback
  • Return a { repo, visibility, derived, reason } shape; unresolved carries a reason for the doctor row
  • Route --kind core and shelf blueprints to the constant sourced from package.json:bugs.url (a test pins the constant)
  • Report the doctor feedback-destinations warn row for every registered library without a resolvable destination
  • Cross-check the registry BEFORE the shelf-constant fall-through for --kind blueprint entries with no libraryPrefix on the manifest record: one library owns the slug and resolves -> library destination (source: library-slug-inference); two-or-more libraries own the slug and resolve -> unresolved with reason ambiguous-library-slug and a candidates[] array; zero libraries own the slug -> shelf constant

Internal structure: src/feedback/destination.js is a pure resolver; the constant lives at the top of the module and is exported for the test to compare against package.json.

Interfaces

  • resolve (function) - Given an entry and the manifest+registry, return the destination shape.
  • CORE_REPO (constant) - The Stravica/rcf-lite constant; pinned to package.json:bugs.url in a test.

Dependencies

  • src/blueprint/library-registry.js (external) - RegistryEntry read for issuesRepo and issuesVisibility fields.

Trade-offs: A declared destination on library.json requires library owners to author one field; the cost is a one-time PR per library, in exchange for correctness on every consuming project.

Notes: A library mirrored from a fork would have derivation pointing at the fork; the declared issues field is why derivation is only a fallback.

TAC-4107... Feedback gh adapter interfaces3 deps1 draft

TAC-4107-feedback-gh - Feedback gh adapter

Purpose: The single place that shells out to gh. Named seam via RCF_FEEDBACK_GH_MODULE so every test replaces gh with a fake that records calls.

Responsibilities

  • Provide ghLabelList, ghIssueSearch, ghIssueCreate, ghIssueComment, ghRepoView (viewerPermission, visibility, hasIssuesEnabled), ghAuthStatus
  • Never read GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN; never spawn gh auth login; never mutate process.env
  • Return typed results, not raw shell output; errors carry the classified reason (network, 4xx, 5xx, ratelimit, notFound)

Internal structure: src/feedback/gh.js exports the interface; RCF_FEEDBACK_GH_MODULE names an alternative module (import() at test time) that exports the same signatures. This mirrors the verifier launchAgent override in src/verify/engine/launcher.js.

Interfaces

  • ghIssueCreate (function) - Create one issue on a repo with title, body and labels; return { url, number }.
  • ghIssueSearch (function) - Search issues on a repo by body query; return matches.
  • ghIssueComment (function) - Comment on an issue; return { url }.

Dependencies

  • gh (external) - The GitHub CLI; the tool never handles tokens itself.

Trade-offs: gh is a dependency the reporter chooses to install; the cost is a fallback bundle path when gh is missing, which the design considers a feature rather than a bug.

Notes: A future MCP-only harness would call the CLI too; a native gh-lib port is not planned for v1.

TAC-4108... Feedback harness hook interfaces3 deps1 draft

TAC-4108-feedback-hook - Feedback harness hook

Purpose: The single hook handler for both Claude Code and Codex, exposing the quiet rule as a pure function and the per-harness output shape as a thin wrapper.

Responsibilities

  • Read harness JSON from stdin (session_id, cwd, hook_event_name, stop_hook_active, last_assistant_message) and never block longer than 1 second
  • Apply the quiet rule (design section 3.5) and return ask or silent
  • Emit the exit-2-plus-stderr shape for Claude Code and the JSON block shape for Codex
  • Install itself under .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json via a mergeable installer that never clobbers other hooks
  • Report missing-hook and foreign-hook conditions to doctor and repair missing hooks under --fix

Internal structure: src/feedback/hook.js exports shouldAsk(state) -> "ask"|"silent" (pure) and emit(harness, decision, entries) (side-effect). src/setup/feedback-hooks.js merges the entries into .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json; doctor reuses the installer helpers for the report.

Interfaces

  • shouldAsk (function) - Pure decision on the quiet rule; unit-tested across the full table.
  • emit (function) - Per-harness output; exit code and shape.
  • installHooks (function) - Merge the hook entries into the two harness config files.

Dependencies

  • TAC-4102-feedback-store (tac) - Read state and settings; write the asked ledger.

Trade-offs: Two harness config files to maintain and one handler; the cost is small (one merge pattern per file) and the benefit is one implementation of the quiet rule for both harnesses.

Notes: The asked record is appended before the emit path, so a crash between emit and reply cannot cause a second ask.

TAC-4109... referee-validate ADR cross-link walker interfaces0 deps0 draft

TAC-4109-referee-validate-adr-crosslinks - referee-validate ADR cross-link walker

Purpose: Extend the load-then-invert walker's referential-integrity pass (`collectBrokenReferences` in `packages/rcf-lite/src/core/store/walker.js`) to walk the strong ADR cross-link the 0.27.0 walker skipped: `supersededBy` (single ADR id). A present target must resolve to a loaded ADR; a mismatch surfaces as a `brokenReference` error named to the ADR file, keyed by field. An absent or empty field is silent. The soft back-reference `relatedAdrs` is deliberately left unwalked at this phase (AC-16301-2 compatibility carry) so the ratified `rcf define blueprint supersede` workflow keeps working; tightening it is a schemas follow-up.

Responsibilities

  • Inside `collectBrokenReferences`, after the existing ADR->TAD parent check, walk `supersededBy` when it is a non-empty string and delegate to the existing `check` helper with expectedKind `adr` (AC-16301-1).
  • Leave `relatedAdrs` unwalked here (AC-16301-2 compatibility carry): the ratified `rcf define blueprint supersede` workflow writes a project ADR whose `relatedAdrs` lists both the applied blueprint ADR and the not-yet-on-disk incoming blueprint ADR, so walking would refuse the workflow between the supersede write and the closing re-add. Tightening moves to the schemas follow-up (value-narrow to applied ADR ids, or a workflow-aware exception on the supersede write path).
  • Reuse the existing `brokenReference` error shape (kind, documentId, filePath, field, rule) so downstream consumers of `formatErrors` need no change.
  • Ensure the widened check contributes to `tree.brokenIds` exactly the way the existing checks do.

Internal structure: One additional call block appended to the existing ADR loop inside `collectBrokenReferences`, delegating `supersededBy` to the `check` helper. The `check` helper is unchanged. `supersededBy` is not required by the ADR schema, so an omitted or empty field never emits an error; the check runs only on a present target. `relatedAdrs` is intentionally not walked at this phase (see responsibilities and AC-16301-2).

Notes: Existing WSD projects that carry stale `supersededBy` pointers will start failing validate on upgrade; that is the intended behaviour (the referee-guarantees docs page promises exactly this refusal). Failures name the ADR file and the field so the fix is a one-line edit or a `define update` write. `relatedAdrs` is untouched by this train and is picked up in the schemas follow-up.

Tightening moves to the schemas follow-up (value-narrow to applied ADR ids, or a workflow-aware exception on the supersede write path).",
    "Reuse the existing `brokenReference` error shape (kind, documentId, filePath, field, rule) so downstream consumers of `formatErrors` need no change.",
    "Ensure the widened check contributes to `tree.brokenIds` exactly the way the existing checks do."
  ],
  "internalStructure": "One additional call block appended to the existing ADR loop inside `collectBrokenReferences`, delegating `supersededBy` to the `check` helper.   "interfaces": [],
  "notes": "Existing WSD projects that carry stale `supersededBy` pointers will start failing validate on upgrade; that is the intended behaviour (the referee-guarantees docs page promises exactly this refusal). Failures name the ADR file and the field so the fix is a one-line edit or a `define update` write. `relatedAdrs` is untouched by this train and is picked up in the schemas follow-up."
}
TAC-4110... coverage --mode selector interfaces0 deps0 draft

TAC-4110-referee-coverage-mode-selector - coverage --mode selector

Purpose: Add an explicit `--mode <strict|shallow-any>` option to `rcf audit coverage` in `packages/rcf-lite/src/cli/coverage.js`, resolve the strictness in one place before invoking `computeCoverage`, and keep the legacy `--strict` flag as a no-op alias for the new default. The plain command runs strict-by-default; `--mode shallow-any` is the explicit opt-out; `--mode shallow-any --strict` is a usage refusal (exit 2).

Responsibilities

  • Extend OPTION_SPEC with `mode: { type: 'string' }` and keep `strict: { type: 'boolean' }` for backward compatibility (AC-16401-1, AC-16401-2).
  • Validate `--mode` against the enum {strict, shallow-any}; reject unknowns with exit 2 (AC-16401-3).
  • Refuse `--mode shallow-any --strict` with exit 2 and a usage message that names both flags (AC-16401-3).
  • Resolve strictness once: `strict = flags.mode === 'shallow-any' ? false : true`. Pass the resolved value into `computeCoverage` and the strict-gate exit-4 branch, and into the strict-only verification-integrity matrix (AC-16401-1, AC-16401-2).
  • Update the HELP block, the module-level comment, and the human-readable error messages so the flag family and its default are self-documenting.

Internal structure: One-shot resolution in main(). No changes to `computeCoverage` or the query layer. The legacy `--strict` flag routes through the same resolver as absence-of-flag, so existing CI invocations (including the repo's own dogfood step) are byte-forward-compatible.

Notes: The repo's own CI dogfood step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is updated to the shipped default (plain `rcf audit coverage`) so the referee-guarantees page and the CI match. Existing blueprints and downstream projects that still spell `--strict` keep working.

TAC-4111... finalise per-AC refusals for UI-BASELINE-UNMET / BROWSER-VERIFICATION-MISSING / SCOPE-MISMATCH interfaces0 deps0 draft

TAC-4111-referee-finalise-per-ac-refusals - finalise per-AC refusals for UI-BASELINE-UNMET / BROWSER-VERIFICATION-MISSING / SCOPE-MISMATCH

Purpose: Add three refusal branches to `packages/rcf-lite/src/cli/finalise.js` that read `passLoaded.report.perAcVerdicts[]` after the existing MOCK-ONLY and EVAL branches and refuse promotion (exit 4) when any per-AC verdict matches one of {UI-BASELINE-UNMET, BROWSER-VERIFICATION-MISSING, SCOPE-MISMATCH}. Each refusal leaves the FBS at its current status, prints a stderr message that names the AC(s), the count and the referee-guarantees claim ids, and appends the `summariseReport` block for context. The three ingest helpers land in `packages/rcf-lite/src/finalise/ingest.js` as `findUiBaselineUnmetAcs` / `reportHasUiBaselineUnmet` and `findBrowserVerificationMissingAcs` / `reportHasBrowserVerificationMissing`; `findScopeMismatchAcs` / `reportHasScopeMismatch` already exist and are reused as-is. All three helpers and the finalise-side booleans are re-exported through `src/finalise/index.js`.

Responsibilities

  • Add findUiBaselineUnmetAcs and reportHasUiBaselineUnmet to ingest.js (AC-16501-1, AC-16501-3).
  • Add findBrowserVerificationMissingAcs and reportHasBrowserVerificationMissing to ingest.js (AC-16501-2).
  • Add three finalise refusal branches after the EVAL refusal branch, in the order UI-BASELINE-UNMET, BROWSER-VERIFICATION-MISSING, SCOPE-MISMATCH; each names the referee-guarantees claim ids in the stderr message so a downstream reader can trace the refusal to the docs promise it enforces (AC-16501-1, AC-16501-2, AC-16501-3).
  • Re-export the new helpers through src/finalise/index.js.
  • The refusals do NOT expose a --ship-without-* opt-out: the docs page names no sister opt-out for these three (unlike MOCK-ONLY / EVAL). If a project needs to ship anyway, the fix is on the tree (widen the TC, land the browser check, fix the baseline).

Internal structure: Three straight-line branches modelled on the existing MOCK-ONLY / EVAL refusal shape. Each reads perAcVerdicts, filters by verdict, prints a message, appends summariseReport, and returns 4. Graceful on the pre-0.7.0 report shape (no perAcVerdicts): the helpers return an empty array and the branches fall through to the next check.

Notes: Behavioural addition, not a change: existing verify reports that never emit these verdicts are unaffected. Existing WSD projects whose verify layer already emits UI-BASELINE-UNMET / BROWSER-VERIFICATION-MISSING / SCOPE-MISMATCH will see finalise refuse where it previously silently promoted; that is the referee-guarantees claim holding.

TAC-4112... finalise verified-invariant: writer refusal + merge-state precondition interfaces0 deps0 draft

TAC-4112-referee-finalise-verified-invariant - finalise verified-invariant: writer refusal + merge-state precondition

Purpose: Gate the two paths that let the 0.27.0 chain say verified without an actual post-merge runtime check. (a) Refuse a define-update patch that writes FBS.executionStatus=verified unless the caller passes options.allowVerifiedOverride=true; the finalise CLI is the sole caller that sets that seam. The define-update CLI exposes the escape valve as --acknowledge-verified-override, matching the escalation clause on this train (existing WSD projects may still need a manual escape hatch for repair scenarios). (b) In `packages/rcf-lite/src/cli/finalise.js`, spawn a git rev-parse subprocess just before the executionStatus write and refuse promotion (exit 4) when the branch is not one of {main, master}. --allow-pre-merge is the deliberate pre-merge dry-run opt-out; the decision is logged on stdout so the operator sees it. Absent a git checkout the check degrades to a warn line rather than a hard fail.

Responsibilities

  • Add the FBS.executionStatus=verified refusal to updateDocument in `packages/rcf-lite/src/core/store/writer.js`, gated on options.allowVerifiedOverride (AC-16502-1, AC-16502-2).
  • Add --acknowledge-verified-override to the define-update CLI, threading options.allowVerifiedOverride through (AC-16502-1).
  • Wire the finalise CLI's own updateDocument call to pass options.allowVerifiedOverride:true (backward compatibility for the finalise happy path).
  • Add resolveGitBranch helper in finalise.js as a testable seam (deps.spawn) around child_process.spawn (AC-16502-3).
  • Add the branch-name refusal branch just before the executionStatus write; support --allow-pre-merge and degrade to a warn line when the branch cannot be resolved (AC-16502-3).
  • Update HELP for both CLIs so the flags and their intent are self-documenting.

Internal structure: Writer refusal fires at the very top of the patch-apply path in updateDocument, before deep-merge and dot-path assignments run, so no partial state ever lands. The finalise-side branch check uses child_process.spawn (imported at module top) with the deps.spawn seam consumers can override in tests; the shape mirrors spawnVerify's own seam. The default-branch set is small and conventional ({main, master}) rather than reading the git remote's symbolic ref (which fails offline and adds a round-trip on every finalise).

Notes: Behavioural addition, not a change on the finalise happy path (finalise passes the override flag through). Downstream projects that ran `rcf define update <fbs> --set executionStatus=verified` without --acknowledge-verified-override will see the write refused; the fix is either finalise or the new opt-out flag. Downstream projects whose finalise ran off a non-default branch will see the pre-merge refusal; --allow-pre-merge is the documented dry-run seam.

TAC-4120... define delta compute and freeze record interfaces0 deps0 draft

TAC-4120-define-delta-and-freeze - define delta compute and freeze record

Purpose: The detection-model primitives (hashDocument, computeTreeHash, computeDelta) live in a new pure module src/query/delta.js, exported from src/query/index.js alongside computeTrace, computeImpact and computeCoverage. The freeze record I/O sits in a new module src/define/freeze-record.js with a small local schema (until schemas 0.7 promotes it to manifest.freeze per ADR-4121). Both modules are pure per call: no filesystem I/O beyond the freeze reader / writer, no state, no time. Canonical JSON is defined on the parsed body, not the raw bytes: keys sorted recursively, no whitespace, JSON.stringify escaping. A whitespace-only reformat of a document produces the same hash; two objects that parse to the same value produce the same hash. Delta granularity is the standalone document: every id in tree.byId (PRD, TAD, BS, REQ, US, TAC, ADR, FBS, TS, CN, EVAL) contributes one docHash; inline AC / TC ride inside the parent's hash; the criterion-level diff is git's job (proposal section 2.2). Ledger docHashes are added under a ledger:<name> id per sidecar the caller passes in.

Responsibilities

  • src/query/delta.js: canonicaliseJson, hashDocument, computeTreeHash and computeDelta pure functions; JSDoc on computeDelta names the exact return shape AC-17201-1 pins.
  • src/query/index.js: re-export canonicaliseJson, hashDocument, computeTreeHash and computeDelta so every consumer imports through one seam.
  • src/define/freeze-record.js: FREEZE_RECORD_REL_PATH (rcf/define/freeze.json), FreezeRecordError, validateFreezeRecord, loadFreezeRecord (returns null on ENOENT, throws FreezeRecordError on parse or schema failure), saveFreezeRecord (validates then writes pretty JSON with trailing newline; creates rcf/define/ on demand).
  • Every hash is a 'sha256:<64-hex>' string; the record's docHashes values and treeHash are validated against that shape and rejected with a named field otherwise.
  • Extension fields (counts, litmus, versions, note, override, gates) survive a save / load round trip; the writer refuses to persist an invalid record so a bad in-memory value never lands on disk.

Internal structure: canonicaliseJson recurses over parsed values: object keys sorted lexicographically, arrays kept in source order, JSON.stringify handles string / number / boolean escaping (non-finite numbers coerce to 'null' as JSON does), undefined is omitted from objects and arrays (matches JSON.stringify semantics). computeTreeHash normalises the input (Map or plain object) into sorted (id, docHash) pairs, canonically encodes the pair array, and hashes the resulting string; the tree hash is thereby order-independent by construction. computeDelta walks tree.byId once, hashes each doc, adds one ledger:<name> entry per non-nullish ledger the caller passes, then either returns the whole-tree 'added' shape (freeze absent) or classifies every id against freeze.docHashes; briefSince walks the brief ledger's statements[] and reports ids above freeze.briefStatements.

Notes: Slice-2 hook: the readiness module will call computeDelta once per render, pass the result through computeImpact per changed id, and hand the union of changed + added + fan-out to every gate check. Slice 3 (the freeze verb) is the only caller of saveFreezeRecord in the shipped path; this slice ships the writer so the verb can be built without a second refactor.

TAC-4121... define ledgers module and rcf define ledger CLI interfaces2 deps0 draft

TAC-4121-define-ledgers - define ledgers module and rcf define ledger CLI

Purpose: The four sidecar ledgers land under rcf/define/ as one JSON file each, with one numbered sequence per ledger for the life of the project. The pure module src/define/ledgers.js exposes LEDGER_NAMES (the four allowed values), BRIEF_KINDS, LedgerError, emptyLedger, ledgerRelPath, ledgerPath, loadLedger, saveLedger, validateLedger, addEntry, resolveEntry, nextIdFor, parseBriefFromFile and loadAllLedgers (returns a LedgerBundle for computeDelta). The CLI verb src/cli/ledger.js wraps the module with parseArgs, wires under bin/rcf.js's define group as GROUPS.define.ledger, and prints usage text also mounted in src/cli/help.js's HELP_MAP.define.ledger so `rcf help define ledger` and `rcf define ledger --help` render the same block by construction.

Responsibilities

  • src/define/ledgers.js: LEDGER_NAMES = ['brief','decisions','concerns','probes']; per-ledger config maps a name to its filename (brief-ledger.json, decisions-ledger.json, concern-ledger.json, probe-ledger.json) and its body array key (statements | decisions | concerns | probes).
  • loadLedger returns emptyLedger(name) on ENOENT; a malformed file raises LedgerError with a code ('parseFailure' | 'schemaFailure' | 'ioFailure' | 'usage') and a named field.
  • addEntry mints the next id (highest current + 1), stamps addedAt and defaults status open, validates the resulting body before returning it, refuses unknown BRIEF_KINDS at validation.
  • resolveEntry flips status to resolved, stamps resolvedAt, throws LedgerError code 'usage' when the id is unknown, is idempotent-ish (resolving twice refreshes resolvedAt).
  • parseBriefFromFile splits by non-empty lines, strips leading '- ', '* ' or '<n>. ' bullets, defaults kind to 'capability', and threads --source through to every draft.
  • src/cli/ledger.js: `rcf define ledger <name> <verb>` argv parsing; verbs add / resolve / list; ledger-specific flags for each; renderDecisionsList formats the #241 numbered layout; list --json emits { ledger, <arrayKey>: [...] }.
  • bin/rcf.js: register GROUPS.define.ledger; src/cli/help.js: import LEDGER_HELP and wire into HELP_MAP.define.ledger + DEFINE_HELP + top-level DEFINE listing so per-verb help stays single-sourced.
  • `update <id>` subverb patches named fields and re-runs full-body validation; `resolvedBy` is a closed pointer grammar (REQ-nnn, TAD.entity:<name>, PRD.user:<name>, TAD.system:<name>, TAC-nnnn, omitted:<reason>) validated by D2.

Internal structure: The walker never reads under rcf/define/: subdirFor in src/core/store/loader.js returns null for anything that is not a known child kind (requirements, user-stories, tacs, adrs, fbs, test-suites, code-nodes, evals), so a ledger file sitting under rcf/define/ is never enumerated for schema validation. The walker-invisibility invariant is proved by a dedicated test that seeds the four ledger files plus a bug-bait req-shaped file under rcf/define/ and asserts zero walker error paths starting with rcf/define/ and no matching id in tree.byId. Validation is JSON-schema-shaped inline (no ajv, no @stravica-ai/rcf-schemas dependency) because the sidecars ride outside the shared schema until schemas 0.7 (ADR-4121).

Interfaces

  • rcf define ledger <name> update <id> (cliCommand) - Patch named fields on an existing ledger entry (brief, decisions, concerns or probes); full-body validation runs as `add` validates. On brief, `--resolved-by` must match the closed pointer grammar.
  • parseResolvedBy (other) - Parse a resolvedBy pointer against the tree; returns { ok, kind, target } on a resolved form (REQ-nnn, TAD.entity:<name>, PRD.user:<name>, TAD.system:<name>, TAC-nnnn, omitted:<reason>) and { ok: false, why } otherwise.

Notes: The intake-scan-against-frozen-statements hook on brief add --from is a named seam this slice leaves for a later one: 'rcf discover intake' is the intended caller in slice 2's D1 gate check, and this slice ensures the CLI has one place to inject that seam without a second refactor. `list --json` is a keep-alive for slice 5's viewer, which will render the same object over http.

TAC-4122-define-gates - define stage gates D1..D8

Purpose: src/query/gates.js lands as a new pure module beside delta.js. Every stage has one exported check function that takes (tree, context) and returns the { stage, gate, state, checks[] } shape section 2.4 pins. computeReadiness (TAC-4123) is the composer; every gate function is otherwise consumable in isolation for tests and for future viewers that render one stage. No I/O, no state, no time: the caller supplies ledgers, profile, freeze, delta, validate errors, probe count and coverage rollups.

Responsibilities

  • src/query/gates.js: STAGE_ORDER = ['D1','D2','D3','D4','D5','D6','D7','D8']; STAGE_GATES map (D1 -> 'define.brief' etc.); INTERFACE_KINDS closed set matching proposal section 5.2; STAGE_SHORT_NAMES map (D1 -> 'brief' etc.).
  • checkD1Brief: intake acknowledged (brief-ledger has at least one statement since the freeze high-water mark), every statement kinded from BRIEF_KINDS, every openQuestion statement resolved or promoted to a decisions-ledger entry, profile.md carries surface (viewer | runningApp | prDiff) and register (productOwner | engineer | unstated) markers.
  • checkD2Skeleton: every 'capability' and 'constraint' statement in scope resolves to a REQ (via a REQ id in the statement's resolvedBy field OR by name-match against a REQ title, cheap check); every REQ in scope has non-TODO description, shapeClassification and domain; TAD.dataArchitecture.dataStores and TAD.dataArchitecture.coreEntities non-empty when any persistence REQ exists (per rcf-schemas 0.6.3 tad.schema.json; the top-level path was a slice-2 drift corrected under w-2026-09-25-dave-004); exactly one deploy or deferral ADR tree-wide (title prefix 'Deploy target:' or 'Deploy deferral:').
  • checkD3Shapes: every TAC in scope has at least one interface; every interface's kind is in INTERFACE_KINDS. Template markers, entity join, ownerRef resolution and path resolution are seams (0.30).
  • checkD4Stories: every REQ in scope has at least one US (fbsByAcId inversion via reqByUs is enough); every US in scope has a testable AC (ac.testable !== false and description non-empty), a failure AC or a project-scoped or req-scoped opt-out with baselineKey 'defineD4:failure', a must-not AC or an opt-out with baselineKey 'defineD4:mustNot', tacIds non-empty and every id resolving to a walker-known TAC, and no AC description containing the scaffold TODO placeholder pattern (case-sensitive uppercase 'TODO:' with a colon -- the literal shape src/core/store/init.js writes; incidental prose mentioning 'todo' does NOT trip the gate, and the validate CLI's broader whole-word notice stays separate).
  • checkD5Crosscut: TAD.securityArchitecture non-empty when tree carries any REQ with shape 'auth' or 'httpApi'; TAD.operationalConcerns non-empty when any AC description carries the '[deployed]' marker; every concern-ledger entry on a REQ in scope has disposition applied or waived (no status 'open').
  • checkD6Consistency: caller-supplied validateErrors is empty (tree-wide); caller-supplied probeOpenCount is zero.
  • checkD7Decisions: no decisions-ledger entry with status 'open'.
  • checkD8Freeze: prior stages passed | acknowledged at the current tree hash; every AC id owned by exactly one FBS (walker.fbsByAcId length 1); computeQueue.nextActionable is not null (queue head actionable) and the head's title is not 'TODO' or empty; validateErrors empty.
  • src/setup/identity-seed.js IDENTITY_TEMPLATE seeds a '## Surface' section carrying one of 'viewer' | 'runningApp' | 'prDiff' (default 'prDiff') so a fresh 'rcf init' project satisfies checkD1Brief's profile:surface marker without the operator editing profile.md first.
  • ADR-4126 (0.29.0): own the per-check persona and question map; export `CHECK_PERSONA`, `CHECK_QUESTION`, `STAGE_FALLBACK_PERSONA`, `checkPersona(name)`, `checkQuestion(name)` and `parseInterfaceDraft(iface)`. Every entry in `stages[].checks[]` carries `persona` (productOwner | engineer) and a non-empty `question`; the `stage:<D>:scope` placeholder uses `STAGE_FALLBACK_PERSONA`.
  • ADR-4126 (0.29.0): split `skeleton:reqFields` into `skeleton:reqIntent` (productOwner: description without TODO and domain, evaluated per REQ independently) and `skeleton:reqShape` (engineer: shapeClassification.shapes). Split `decisions:allAnswered` into `decisions:wellFormed` (productOwner: non-empty question + two or more options + a default naming one of them) and `decisions:allAnswered` (engineer: zero open).
  • ADR-4126 (0.29.0): new D3 check `shapes:draftSettled` fails any interface whose `description` starts with `[draft]` (whitespace tolerated), id `<tacId>:<name>`, over delta, total = interfaces on TACs in scope; `tacHasInterface` counts a draft as present; `kindVocabulary` applies to drafts.

Internal structure: Every stage function follows the same shape: 1) decide notApplicable per section 3.2 and return { state: 'notApplicable' } with a single-check summary; 2) build checks[] as a list of { name, ok, over, pass, total, failing: [{ id, why }] }; 3) fold to state: 'passed' if every ok is true; 'failing' otherwise, unless the stage is D3/D5/D6 AND freeze.gates[<gate>].state === 'acknowledged' AND freeze.gates[<gate>].at.hash === currentTreeHash, in which case state is 'acknowledged'. Blocking-vs-warn is a property of the stage, not of the state: D3/D5/D6 use the acknowledged fold, D1/D2/D4/D7/D8 do not. The caller (readiness) folds the array of stage results into freezeable and nextAction.

Interfaces

  • CHECK_PERSONA (other) - [draft] Owning persona map (productOwner | engineer) for every stage-gate check in 0.29.0 (ADR-4126).
  • CHECK_QUESTION (other) - [draft] Per-check heading question in the owning persona's register; the report and the Readiness tab print it as the heading of each check's findings list.
  • STAGE_FALLBACK_PERSONA (other) - [draft] Per-stage fallback persona for the `stage:<D>:scope` placeholder check that `notApplicable` envelopes carry.
  • checkPersona (other) - [draft] Look up the owning persona for a check name; returns 'productOwner' | 'engineer' | null.
  • checkQuestion (other) - [draft] Look up the question heading for a check name; returns the empty string when no question is registered.
  • parseInterfaceDraft (other) - [draft] True when an interface's `description` carries the leading `[draft]` marker (whitespace tolerated).

Notes: Slice-3 hook (rcf define freeze): reads state to refuse on any 'failing'; --ack <gate> --reason <text> writes freeze.gates[<gate>] = { state: 'acknowledged', at: { hash: <currentTreeHash>, reason: <text>, by: <id> } } and re-runs computeReadiness to check freezeable. Slice-5 hook (viewer): reads the same object end-to-end.

TAC-4123... computeReadiness compute and rcf define readiness CLI interfaces6 deps0 draft

TAC-4123-define-readiness - computeReadiness compute and rcf define readiness CLI

Purpose: src/query/readiness.js and src/cli/readiness.js land as a matched pair. The pure module composes computeDelta, computeImpact, the eight gate check functions from TAC-4122, computeCoverage, and the decisions ledger into the single-object contract section 2.4 pins; the CLI is its twin. Text output for readable status; --json for machine consumers and the viewer slice; --check <stage>|all for targeted inspection with the same 0-green / 4-red exit shape rcf audit coverage uses.

Responsibilities

  • src/query/readiness.js: computeReadiness(tree, { freeze, ledgers, profile, testPointers }) returns { tree, delta, stages, nextAction, coverage, decisions, freezeable } exactly as section 2.4 specifies; internal computeScope collects changed + added + impacted ids into a Set; internal composeStages calls each check function in D1..D8 order; internal computeNextAction picks the first failing stage and check; internal deriveTreeSummary shortens the tree hash to eight characters for the tree line.
  • src/query/readiness.js: computeImpact is called once per id in changed union added; impacted is the deduplicated union of every impact node id excluding the pivots; impactedFbs is the subset with kind 'fbs' AND actionNeeded === 're-execute'.
  • src/query/readiness.js: computeCoverage is called once tree-wide (strict per-AC, testPointers threaded through) for coverage.tree; coverage.delta is one CoverageResult per unique REQ ancestor of the delta ids (via tree.parentByChild walk to the reqId, or the doc's own reqId field).
  • src/query/readiness.js: freezeable is true when every stage state in ['passed', 'acknowledged', 'notApplicable'] and false otherwise; nextAction is null when freezeable is true.
  • src/cli/readiness.js: parseArgs on --json, --check, --help; findProjectRoot; walkTree; loadFreezeRecord; loadAllLedgers; resolveTestPointers; runWithAdmissibilityGate wraps a producer that invokes computeReadiness; on refuse the CLI prints an informational '[warn] readiness: chain admissibility refused (informational; the readiness compute still ran).' on stderr and STILL runs the compute so the diagnostic reports which stage blocks (readiness is a diagnostic, not a gate that hides its answer); the top-level exit stays 0 in that case and --check <stage> follows its normal per-stage exit rule; on ok the CLI renders text (default) or JSON.
  • src/cli/readiness.js: text output = tree line, next-action line, chip line (D1..D8 with state color words), stage-by-stage failing items (checks with failing ids); --check exits 4 for a blocking stage that is failing, 0 with a stderr [warn] for a warn-with-ack stage that is failing but not acknowledged, 0 otherwise.
  • src/define/ledgers.js (P3 resolution): loadAllLedgers checks each ledger file's existence with statPath and omits missing files from the returned bundle; loadLedger keeps returning an empty ledger on ENOENT so single-ledger callers retain the ergonomic default.
  • bin/rcf.js: register GROUPS.define.readiness -> readinessMain; src/cli/help.js: import READINESS_HELP and wire into HELP_MAP.define.readiness + DEFINE_HELP + top-level DEFINE listing.
  • src/query/index.js: export computeReadiness (plus its subhelpers where useful for tests) so downstream consumers (slice 3 freeze, slice 5 viewer) import through the same seam every other query verb does.
  • ADR-4126 (0.29.0): fold `levels` and `personas` from `stages[].checks[]` after the eight stage functions run. `levels.intentComplete.ok` is "every productOwner check ok" across every stage (stage state ignored); `levels.intentComplete.blockedBy` lists every failing PO check with ids capped at 20. `levels.readyToBuild.ok` equals freezeable; `levels.readyToBuild.blockedBy` lists every failing check in a stage whose state is `failing` (checks inside an `acknowledged` stage are not blockers). `personas.productOwner.blockers` deep-equals `levels.intentComplete.blockedBy`; `personas.engineer.blockers` is the failing engineer checks in failing stages. `levels.readyToBuild.nextAction` deep-equals the top-level `nextAction`.
  • ADR-4126 (0.29.0): `deriveNextAction(stages, persona?)` gains an optional persona argument. With no persona it behaves exactly as 0.28.4. With a persona it picks the first stage in D1..D8 order holding a failing check of that persona, then the check with the largest failing list; the command carries `--level intent` on the productOwner variant. `formatVerdictLines(result)` builds the two strings (`Intent-complete: yes/no...` and `Ready-to-build: yes/no...`) shared by the CLI (PR B) and the Readiness tab (PR C) so they cannot disagree.
  • ADR-4126 (0.29.0): the levels and personas folds are additive; every 0.28.4 top-level field (tree, delta, stages, nextAction, coverage, decisions, freezeable) is present with its 0.28.4 type. No file under rcf/ is created or modified by any `rcf define readiness` invocation. The CLI flags (`--level`, `--persona`) and the viewer tab are PR B and PR C respectively; the compute lands first (PR A).
  • ADR-4126 PR B (0.29.0): src/cli/readiness.js owns the --level intent|build and --persona productOwner|engineer dispatch. --level drives the exit code against levels.<which>.ok per spec section 3.2 (stricter than --check all on warn-with-ack failures per decision 4); --persona is a display filter that never affects the exit code or JSON content. parseLevelFlag and parsePersonaFlag share the usage-line shape with --check. Unknown values exit 2 with a usage line naming the accepted set. The CLI passes the resolved level into computeReadiness via the readiness context so _meta.level reflects the invocation (null when the flag was absent).
  • ADR-4126 PR B (0.29.0): the text report prints both verdict lines (shared via formatVerdictLines) at the top; regroups blockers into one 'Product owner: N question(s)' and one 'Engineer: N check(s) blocking' section ordered by the profile register (productOwner-first or engineer-first; unstated and absent profile default to PO first); and renders the per-check line in the per-stage detail block with the persona inside the parenthesis after `over`. --persona X collapses the opposite-persona block to one 'hidden; run without --persona' line and restricts the per-stage detail to matching-persona checks.

Internal structure: readiness.js is a linear composer: 1) compute delta and its docHashes; 2) fan-out impacted / impactedFbs; 3) build stage context (freeze, delta, scope, ledgers, profile, validateErrors, probeOpenCount, coverageTree); 4) call the eight check functions; 5) fold freezeable and nextAction. The CLI parses flags, loads the tree once, loads the four ledgers and the freeze record once, computes the readiness, then routes to the text or JSON emitter. --check maps its argument to the STAGE_SHORT_NAMES map (brief -> D1 ... freeze -> D8) or accepts D1..D8 directly. The runWithAdmissibilityGate wrap sits inside main so refusals ride the same exit path as coverage's admissibility refusals.

Interfaces

  • deriveLevels (other) - [draft] Fold the two levels (intentComplete, readyToBuild) from `stages[].checks[]` (ADR-4126, proposal section 2.1).
  • derivePersonas (other) - [draft] Fold the `personas` block; productOwner.blockers deep-equals levels.intentComplete.blockedBy; engineer.blockers is the failing engineer checks in failing stages.
  • deriveNextAction (other) - [draft] Pick the first failing stage (optionally persona-filtered); carries `--level intent` on the productOwner variant.
  • formatVerdictLines (other) - [draft] Build the two verdict strings (Intent-complete and Ready-to-build) shared by the CLI and the Readiness tab so the two surfaces cannot disagree.
  • parseLevelFlag (other) - [draft] Validate --level against the closed value set (intent | build); return 'intent' | 'build' | null (flag absent) or throw a usage error for an unknown value (CLI maps the throw to exit 2 with a stderr usage line).
  • parsePersonaFlag (other) - [draft] Validate --persona against the closed value set (productOwner | engineer); return the value or null (flag absent) or throw a usage error for an unknown value.

Notes: Slice-3 hook (rcf define freeze) reads freezeable and stages[].state; --ack <gate> writes into freeze.gates[<gate>] and re-computes readiness. Slice-5 hook (viewer) fetches the same JSON object over the existing tab wire and renders the pill vocabulary + findings-list + diff components. Performance seam: computeImpact per id on a whole-tree delta (before freeze) may be quadratic on very large trees; the compute stays fast on the dogfood chain (~700 documents, sub-second) but the CLI notes the wall time in text mode so an operator can spot regression.
